Reviewed the queue, configuration and store changes. The targeted issue-queue test could not run because the checkout is missing the @modelcontextprotocol/sdk dependency.

Reviewed the queue, store, configuration, and run creation paths. The targeted queue suite could not start because the checkout lacks @modelcontextprotocol/sdk. A standalone SQLite probe measured the new per-run lookup pattern.

findings.title: Lowercased queue names bypass existing mixed-case repository registrations
findings.detail: The lowercased name is passed to createRun, but resolveRepo and Store.getRepoBySlug look up registered slugs case-sensitively. An existing registration such as Owner/Repo is therefore missed after this change. The factory calls GitHub to create a second owner/repo registration, losing the existing registration's repository settings; if that lookup fails, the queued run cannot start. The config change also lowercases the name before the queue receives it.
findings.suggestion: Deduplicate and key queue state case-insensitively while preserving a usable configured spelling, or make GitHub repository resolution reuse existing registrations case-insensitively.
findings.failure_scenario: A queue configured for Owner/Repo has an existing Owner/Repo registration with a custom merge policy or local repository path. An approved issue is submitted as owner/repo, so the registration is not found and a new repository is resolved instead.

findings.title: Lowercased run requests bypass existing mixed-case repository registrations
findings.detail: The queue now passes the lowercased repository name into every run request. Factory.createRun resolves that name through case-sensitive getRepoBySlug calls. An existing registration such as Owner/Repo is therefore missed, causing an unnecessary gh repo view and creation of a second repository record for the same GitHub repository. If that lookup fails, queue admission fails even though the repository was already registered.
findings.suggestion: Use canonical keys for queue comparisons while resolving run requests to the existing repository registration case-insensitively.
findings.failure_scenario: An installation has Owner/Repo registered and configured for the queue. After upgrade, an approved issue is submitted as owner/repo; resolution misses the existing record and either creates a duplicate or fails on the remote lookup.

findings.title: Every poll synchronously reads and looks up every historical run
findings.detail: Seeding observations loads every run's prompt and source reference, including runs from unrelated repositories, then linkedIssues performs a recursive SQLite ownership query for each row. This work runs synchronously on the daemon thread on every poll and grows with the entire run history, reintroducing the stall pattern the batched lookup was intended to remove. A standalone in-memory SQLite probe of the ownership-query pattern reported `50000 owner lookups: 597.4 ms`; the real path also reads and parses all prompts and builds the observation map.
findings.suggestion: Seed observations with a batched query restricted to relevant linked runs, resolving round ownership in the query instead of issuing one lookup per historical run.
findings.failure_scenario: A daemon accumulates tens of thousands of historical runs, including unrelated runs with large prompts. Each queue poll blocks the event loop while it loads and processes all of them, delaying other daemon activity.

structured.summary: Reviewed the queue, store, configuration, and run creation paths. The targeted queue suite could not start because the checkout lacks @modelcontextprotocol/sdk. A standalone SQLite probe measured the new per-run lookup pattern.

findings.title: Lowercased run requests bypass existing mixed-case repository registrations
findings.detail: The queue now passes the lowercased repository name into every run request. Factory.createRun resolves that name through case-sensitive getRepoBySlug calls. An existing registration such as Owner/Repo is therefore missed, causing an unnecessary gh repo view and creation of a second repository record for the same GitHub repository. If that lookup fails, queue admission fails even though the repository was already registered.
findings.suggestion: Use canonical keys for queue comparisons while resolving run requests to the existing repository registration case-insensitively.
findings.failure_scenario: An installation has Owner/Repo registered and configured for the queue. After upgrade, an approved issue is submitted as owner/repo; resolution misses the existing record and either creates a duplicate or fails on the remote lookup.

findings.title: Every poll synchronously reads and looks up every historical run
findings.detail: Seeding observations loads every run's prompt and source reference, including runs from unrelated repositories, then linkedIssues performs a recursive SQLite ownership query for each row. This work runs synchronously on the daemon thread on every poll and grows with the entire run history, reintroducing the stall pattern the batched lookup was intended to remove. A standalone in-memory SQLite probe of the ownership-query pattern reported `50000 owner lookups: 597.4 ms`; the real path also reads and parses all prompts and builds the observation map.
findings.suggestion: Seed observations with a batched query restricted to relevant linked runs, resolving round ownership in the query instead of issuing one lookup per historical run.
findings.failure_scenario: A daemon accumulates tens of thousands of historical runs, including unrelated runs with large prompts. Each queue poll blocks the event loop while it loads and processes all of them, delaying other daemon activity.

findings.title: Lowercasing the run request can create a duplicate repository
findings.detail: The queue now passes the lowercased repository name into run creation. Repository resolution uses a case-sensitive getRepoBySlug lookup, so a repository already registered under its configured mixed-case name is not found. resolveRepo then calls gh and registers a second repository with the lowercase slug. Queue-created runs consequently use a different repository record from existing runs; if the gh lookup fails, admission fails altogether.
findings.suggestion: Use canonical keys for queue comparisons while preserving or resolving the existing repository identity when creating runs.
findings.failure_scenario: A deployment has an existing repository registered as Owner/Repo and configures that name in github.queue.repos. After this change, an approved issue is submitted as owner/repo, which misses the existing record and triggers remote resolution and duplicate registration.

findings.title: Changes before the issue snapshot unnecessarily invalidate it
findings.detail: The listener records changes from the beginning of the poll, and the new code never clears an issue’s invalidation when its snapshot is taken. A change that completes before `latestIssueRuns` executes is already reflected in that snapshot, yet admission still defers it. If a linked run receives a decision-relevant update during the GitHub lookup on every poll, the approved issue can starve indefinitely—the behavior this request aims to eliminate.
findings.suggestion: Clear an issue’s invalidation when its canonical repository snapshot is captured, while ensuring a duplicate repository read cannot clear an invalidation for an earlier candidate; alternatively track snapshot generations per candidate.
findings.failure_scenario: On every poll, a linked run’s status or finish time changes while the queue awaits the repository’s GitHub response. The subsequent snapshot contains the new state, but the issue is refused with the retry message on every poll.

findings.title: Every poll performs an ownership query for every historical run
findings.detail: Seeding observations loads all runs, including unrelated historical runs, and `decision()` calls `linkedIssues()`, which executes a recursive SQLite ownership query for each one. This work runs synchronously on the daemon thread before any repository lookup and grows with the entire database. A synthetic in-memory check of the same query took 540 ms for 50,000 root runs, excluding the initial load, JSON parsing, and linkage processing; the original poll had no equivalent global scan.
findings.suggestion: Seed observations with a batched ownership lookup, scoped to relevant runs where possible, instead of issuing one query per historical run.
findings.failure_scenario: A long-lived installation accumulates tens of thousands of runs; every issue-queue poll blocks the daemon for hundreds of milliseconds or longer even when only one repository is configured.

Reviewed lease storage and recovery against the requested invariants. The targeted tests could not start because the available Zod dependency lacks prefault; no tests executed.

findings.title: A moved replay clears the intent without classifying the new tip
findings.detail: Every `moved` result marks confirmed ownership lost and clears the release intent. The claim client returns `moved` for any different tip, including a malformed record or a record at the same generation and holder with different fields. Those cases do not establish supersession; the recovery table requires malformed or otherwise unclassifiable tips to remain pending. Clearing the journal also loses the final status and checkpoint that the release was meant to publish.
findings.suggestion: Classify `result.tip` with the same rules used for the initial recovery read. Mark the lease lost only when the returned record establishes supersession; otherwise retain the intent and report pending.
findings.failure_scenario: Recovery reads the confirmed held tip and starts replaying a release. Before its compare-and-swap, the ref moves to a malformed commit. The write returns `moved`, and recovery changes the confirmed state to `lost` and deletes the pending release instead of retaining it for a later readable observation.

findings.title: Classify the tip returned after a failed release replay
findings.detail: Every moved replay is treated as superseded without inspecting the returned tip. ClaimClient.write can return moved when the newly observed record is malformed or when it does not establish a successor. This clears the release intent and marks confirmed ownership lost, even though the recovery table requires malformed content to leave the intent and confirmed history intact for a later retry.
findings.suggestion: Classify result.tip using the same recovery rules as the initial read, and mark the lease lost only when that tip establishes supersession.
findings.failure_scenario: Recovery reads the confirmed tip and starts replaying a release. Before updateRefs, another writer moves the ref to a commit with a malformed claim record. The compare-and-swap fails and write returns moved with that tip; recovery clears the final release intent instead of returning pending.

findings.title: A restart before the slow-regression selector loses the observation
findings.detail: The selector only updates observations whose stage ID equals the current stage ID. Resuming creates a new stage, while reattaching the primary gate preserves the existing observation through the insert's conflict handling. Consequently the existing row retains the old stage ID and is excluded from observedHandles. A subsequent passing slow re-check is recorded as flaky instead of load, and slow_regression remains false.
findings.suggestion: Locate the primary observation by its durable execution identity across stage restarts, and add a restart test that interrupts after observation insertion but before the slow-regression selector.
findings.failure_scenario: A post-merge primary gate fails slowly; the process restarts after inserting its observation but before selecting the re-check; the reattached gate is re-checked successfully. findings.title: Post-merge replay can finalize an interrupted execution with another execution's result
findings.detail: Finalization matches post-merge observations by purpose, round, and SHA, but does not distinguish execution handles. If the process stops after recording a primary result and before saving the post-merge comparison, a local gate can be executed again with a new handle. Both observations are then finalized against the second execution's comparison. This can assign the first failure a retry or confirmation history it never had, and leaves two finalized observations where the requested restart behavior calls for finalization exactly once.
findings.suggestion: Persist and carry the primary execution identity through the post-merge checkpoint, then finalize only the observation belonging to that execution; handle abandoned executions according to the interruption rules.
findings.failure_scenario: A local post-merge gate fails, its observation is inserted, and the daemon stops after the gate-result save but before post-merge-confirmation-pending. On restart the primary gate runs again with a new handle; finalization applies the new comparison to both rows.

output.summary:
Reviewed the lease manager’s ownership, recovery, timing, and renewal paths. The targeted command `bun test test/leases.test.ts` could not initialize: the installed Zod lacks `prefault`, producing `TypeError: floors.prefault is not a function` in `src/evals/settings.ts:14`. The findings below are based on tracing the implementation and its dependencies.

Reviewed the lease manager against the claim client, time predicates, and intent recovery. The targeted command `bun test test/leases.test.ts` could not run any tests because the installed Zod lacks `prefault`; it failed during module loading with `TypeError: floors.prefault is not a function` at `src/evals/settings.ts:14`.

findings.title: Recovery can replay an expired release without a time check
findings.detail: Both startup recovery and ordinary reconciliation call `reconcileLeaseIntent`, whose release replay calls `client.write` without a `beforeSend` predicate or a GitHub-time sample. A release interrupted before its ref update can therefore be sent after the generation has expired. This bypasses the required same-generation send-time check and can publish a stale release.
findings.suggestion: Ensure release replay uses a fresh renewable/window decision and revalidates it immediately before the ref update, including during startup recovery.
findings.failure_scenario: A release intent is journaled, the process stops before updating the ref, and recovery runs more than ten minutes later while the old ref still exists. Recovery writes the expired generation's release without checking its age.

findings.title: A different run cannot reconcile or clear a pending acquisition
findings.detail: The cross-run guard returns before reconciliation whenever the existing row has an intent. It returns `refused` even when the intent is unresolved, and prevents the next run from clearing a dropped, never-confirmed acquisition. Startup recovery also calls `recoverLeases` directly and does not forget rows whose unconfirmed acquisition was dropped.
findings.suggestion: Reconcile pending intents before the cross-run ownership decision and forget dropped rows with no confirmed ownership, including during startup recovery.
findings.failure_scenario: Run A leaves a first-acquisition intent, then ends. After a restart, recovery drops the intent because the ref never moved, leaving an unconfirmed row for A. Run B reaches `forgetLease` only if the row has no intent, but an unresolved intent instead causes an immediate refusal; without a loop tick to settle it, B cannot make progress.

findings.title: Renewal loop omits confirmed leases recovered after restart
findings.detail: The loop iterates only the in-memory `handles` map, which is populated by writes applied through this manager instance. Existing confirmed held rows, including acquisitions confirmed by startup or tick reconciliation, never enter that map. Starting the manager therefore does not renew those active leases.
findings.suggestion: Enumerate confirmed held rows for renewal or populate handles from durable confirmed ownership when recovering and reconciling.
findings.failure_scenario: An acquisition is applied on GitHub but its response is lost. After restart, recovery confirms the pending acquisition, and `start` reports it active; subsequent ticks do not renew it because no handle was added to the map.

findings.title: Supersession check treats released ownership as a lost lease
findings.detail: The supersession predicate accepts any confirmed state rather than only confirmed held ownership. A newer same-run generation following a release is consequently marked lost and returned as superseded, preventing the specified hand-off acquisition.
findings.suggestion: Apply the lost-generation check only to confirmed held ownership, then decide released-tip acquisition from the current tip.
findings.failure_scenario: This store confirms generation 1 as released; another coordinator acquires and later releases generation 2 for the same run. A subsequent acquisition here sees the newer tip, marks generation 1 lost, and returns `superseded` instead of acquiring generation 3.

findings.title: Mutation tests explicitly accept two simultaneous winners
findings.detail: The race helper expects two winners when the unconditional-ref-write mutant is enabled. structured.summary: Reviewed the lease manager against the requested ownership, recovery, timing, and renewal invariants. The targeted command `bun test test/leases.test.ts` could not run: module loading failed with `TypeError: floors.prefault is not a function` in the existing eval settings dependency. The findings below are based on tracing the changed code and its dependencies.

findings.title: Release recovery can write after the lease expires
findings.detail: The manager delegates reconciliation to `reconcileLeaseIntent`, which replays a pending release with `client.write` without a `beforeSend` hook or a GitHub-time decision. This path is also used during manager creation. A release interrupted before its ref update can therefore be sent after its generation's renewable window has closed, bypassing the required same-generation send-time guard.
findings.suggestion: Make release replay use the manager's fresh time decision and send-time revalidation, including during startup recovery.
findings.failure_scenario: A release intent is persisted, the process stops before updating the ref, and recovery runs after the lease has expired while the old tip is still present. Recovery writes the old generation's release without checking whether it is renewable.

findings.title: The renewal loop omits confirmed leases recovered from storage
findings.detail: The loop iterates only the in-memory `handles` map, which is populated after a write returns `applied` in this manager instance. Existing confirmed held rows and acquisitions confirmed by reconciliation never enter that map. Starting a manager after restart, or resolving an unconfirmed first acquisition on a timer tick, therefore leaves the confirmed lease without automatic renewal.
findings.suggestion: Populate or derive loop handles from confirmed held rows, including rows confirmed by reconciliation, while keeping anchors conservative after recovery.
findings.failure_scenario: An acquisition's ref update succeeds but returns `unconfirmed`; a later tick reconciles the intent to applied. No handle is added to `handles`, so subsequent ticks never renew that lease and it expires.

findings.title: A different run bypasses pending-intent reconciliation
findings.detail: The cross-run check returns `refused` before reconciliation whenever the existing row has an intent. The request requires pending intents to be reconciled before every operation and unresolved ones to return `wait`. In particular, a failed first acquisition can leave an intent that is already deterministically droppable, yet the next run cannot clear it through its acquisition.
findings.suggestion: Reconcile the row first, return `wait` if it remains pending, and then apply the cross-run ownership check to the settled row.
findings.failure_scenario: Run A's first acquisition is interrupted before send, leaving an intent with no confirmed ownership. Run B calls `acquire` before the renewal loop runs; it receives `refused: live` rather than reconciling the absent ref, forgetting A's row, and acquiring it.

findings.title: The required unconditional-write mutation does not fail the tests
findings.detail: The concurrency helper explicitly expects two winners when the unconditional-ref-write mutant is enabled, and both mutant cases are included as passing tests. Consequently the suite accepts the exact broken behavior the request says tests 1 and 3 must detect.
findings.suggestion: Assert the one-winner invariant independently of the fake's implementation, and verify separately that substituting the unconditional-write mutant makes those assertions fail.
findings.failure_scenario: The fake's ref update is changed to unconditional writes: both coordinators acquire the same generation, but the mutant test expects two winners and passes.

findings.title: Superseded unpublished question sets can never be published if they become current again
findings.detail: A stale question effect is permanently marked done even when no comment was posted. If the same question set later becomes eligible again, observe() sees the existing effect and never creates another publication. The recovery test explicitly expects this behavior even when the uncertain POST was not accepted, leaving an outstanding question invisible on GitHub.
findings.suggestion: Distinguish a recovered or completed publication from an unpublished superseded effect, and permit a fresh publication when that set becomes current again after recovery establishes that no POST was accepted.
findings.failure_scenario: A run waits on question A, its POST fails before acceptance, and the run temporarily leaves waiting_input. Recovery marks the effect done without a comment. The run returns to waiting_input with A still unanswered; subsequent polls never publish A.

findings.title: Publication failures still log arbitrary exception output
findings.detail: The delivery catch passes the raw exception to logFailure, which only redacts registered credentials. GitHub or an injected runner can return an error containing configured private strings or withheld question text, so diagnostics can disclose content that the publication inspection withheld. This also violates the requirement that diagnostics use fixed codes rather than exception output.
findings.suggestion: Log a fixed diagnostic code for comment delivery and recovery failures without interpolating the exception.
findings.failure_scenario: A question contains a configured private string and is withheld; a failed GitHub call returns an error whose message contains that string. The lifecycle log writes the string because it is not a registered credential.

findings.title: Superseded unsent question sets can never be published if they become current again
findings.detail: A stale checkpoint is permanently marked done even when no POST was issued or recovery confirms that none was accepted. Observation then refuses to create another effect for the same question IDs because it checks only whether the effect exists. An outstanding set can therefore remain unpublished after waiting or linkage resumes. The new supersession test explicitly expects this outcome for a rejected POST.
findings.suggestion: Distinguish a recovered publication from a superseded effect that was never published, and allow a newly eligible occurrence of the latter to be published after recovery is complete.
findings.failure_scenario: A question POST fails before acceptance, the run leaves waiting while recovery is pending, and then returns to waiting with the same unanswered question. Recovery closes the checkpoint without a comment, and later polls never publish that question set.

findings.title: Lifecycle failures log untrusted exception output
findings.detail: The publication catch passes the original exception to logFailure, which only redacts registered credentials. GitHub or identity errors can contain configured private strings or model-written content, and the requirement calls for fixed diagnostic codes without exception output. This also applies to errors during question recovery and posting.
findings.suggestion: Log a fixed failure code for publication and recovery failures instead of the exception text.
findings.failure_scenario: A fake or real GitHub runner rejects a question POST with an error containing a configured private string or the submitted question; that text is written to lifecycle diagnostics.

findings.title: Superseded unsent sets can never be published if they become current again
findings.detail: An ineligible question effect with no uncertain POST is permanently marked done. Observation then refuses to create another effect for the same question IDs, even if the run becomes eligible again. The checkpoint does not distinguish a published set from an unsent superseded set.
findings.suggestion: Represent unsent supersession separately from completed publication and permit a fresh publication when that set becomes current again, while retaining recovery for uncertain POSTs.
findings.failure_scenario: A question publication waits on identity lookup while the repository is temporarily made discreet or its link is removed. The effect is marked done without a POST. If the setting or link is restored while the same question remains open, subsequent polls never publish it.

findings.title: Inspection failure closes an uncertain POST before recovery
findings.detail: The stored body is re-inspected before the pending-page recovery loop. If inspection fails, the code marks the effect done immediately, even when page is nonzero and the previous POST may have been accepted. This loses the posting identity and marker recovery opportunity required for pending effects.
findings.suggestion: Recover an uncertain POST using the independently generated marker and checkpointed identity before closing its checkpoint; suppress any new POST if body inspection fails.
findings.failure_scenario: GitHub accepts a question comment but the response is lost. Before the next poll, private-string inspection becomes unavailable. The next poll records the effect as done without looking for the accepted comment, so the checkpoint never records whether it was delivered.

findings.title: Publication failures log arbitrary command output
findings.detail: The comment delivery and recovery catch passes the exception to logFailure, which logs its string after credential redaction only. A gh command failure includes its arguments and stderr or stdout; configured private strings in GitHub's response are not redacted. This also violates the requirement that publication diagnostics use fixed codes rather than exception output.
findings.suggestion: Log a fixed lifecycle failure code for publication and recovery errors without including the exception or subprocess output.
findings.failure_scenario: A comments recovery request fails and gh returns an error response containing a configured private string from GitHub content. The lifecycle log records that string because it is not a registered credential.

findings.title: A superseded set can never be published if it becomes current again
findings.detail: Superseding an unsent or unaccepted question publication marks its effect done. Observation then refuses to create another effect for the same question IDs, even if that set becomes current again without ever having been published. The new tests explicitly expect this behavior for a run that resumes waiting during recovery.
findings.suggestion: Distinguish a successfully published set from a superseded, unposted attempt, and allow a fresh eligible attempt after recovery confirms that no comment was accepted.
findings.failure_scenario: A run waits on question A, its POST fails before acceptance, and it temporarily leaves waiting_input. Recovery marks the effect done; if the run returns to waiting_input with A still open, subsequent polls never publish A.

findings.title: Publication failures log raw exception content
findings.detail: The new question and reason publication path passes exceptions to logFailure, which emits their text after credential redaction only. GitHub command errors can contain stderr or stdout, and configured private strings are not removed by credential redaction. This also violates the requirement that publication diagnostics use fixed codes rather than exception output.
findings.suggestion: Log a fixed publication failure code for these operations without including exception text or command output.
findings.failure_scenario: A GitHub request fails with a configured private string in its error output. The lifecycle log records that string even though publication inspection would have withheld it from a comment.

This makes `limitless deploy --smoke` fail for an intentional configuration even if other eligible providers work. Backend checks already treat an entirely excluded provider as skipped.
candidates.suggestion: Apply the same excluded-provider skip handling to native checks before selecting a model.
candidates.failure_scenario: Configure an origin exclusion that excludes every Claude model while leaving another provider eligible, then run the deployment smoke check. Every Claude check fails instead of being skipped, so deployment fails.

candidates.title: Log excluded verifier candidates when another verifier remains
candidates.detail: The panel verifier path removes excluded targets before invoking the router. When at least one verifier remains, the collected exclusion reasons are discarded, so the run log does not show the required skip reason for those candidates.
candidates.suggestion: Record the excluded verifier targets and their reasons in the run log before selecting among the remaining targets.
candidates.failure_scenario: A panel verifier list contains one excluded model and one eligible model. Verification uses the eligible model, but the run log never reports `origin excluded (...)` for the excluded candidate.

candidates.title: A declined answer hides the exclusion that exhausted routing
candidates.detail: The last-resort return runs before the new exclusion handling. If an allowed model returns an unsure decline and all remaining candidates are excluded, the invocation succeeds with that declined answer without reporting the exclusion. The request requires the invocation to fail with the exclusion reason when exclusions leave no candidate.
candidates.suggestion: Check and report origin exclusions before accepting the declined-answer fallback when they are what prevents further routing.
candidates.failure_scenario: An allowed review model returns a last-resort decline, and the only remaining model has an excluded origin. Routing returns the declined answer instead of failing with `origin excluded (...)`.

candidates.title: Recheck origin eligibility immediately before dispatch
candidates.detail: The request says excluded models must be ineligible on every route, including models changed at runtime. The routing revision is checked after provider preflight, but the invocation then crosses further awaits before calling the harness. A runtime catalog patch during that interval can change the selected model's origin to an excluded one; unlike the eval and concierge paths, this path never calls assertOriginEligible before dispatch.
candidates.suggestion: Recheck the selected model's origin immediately before each harness dispatch, and handle an exclusion without calling the model.
candidates.failure_scenario: A run selects an allowed runtime model, then waits during invocation setup while an operator patches that model's origin to CN with CN excluded. The existing target is still dispatched to the harness.

candidates.title: Filter excluded verifier alternatives before constructing eval targets
candidates.detail: The request requires the router to treat an excluded model as ineligible for verifier selection. Panel eval preparation eagerly converts every listed verifier through toTarget, which now throws for an excluded model. Consequently, one excluded verifier aborts the trial even when another listed verifier is eligible. Production verifier selection filters the list instead.
candidates.suggestion: Filter excluded verifier alternatives before converting them to targets, and fail with the exclusion reason only when no eligible verifier remains.
candidates.failure_scenario: An eval panel has verifier targets A and B, A has CN origin, B is allowed, and exclude_origins contains CN. Preparing the trial throws for A instead of selecting B.

findings.title: Reviewable text still requires a binary allowance in some mode changes
findings.detail: The new condition applies a stricter definition of text than Git's diff classification. It flags executable text containing non-UTF-8 bytes or control characters, and flags executable text under a media extension regardless of its contents. It also newly blocks a non-UTF-8 text file when an edit removes its executable bit: the old condition did not flag a mode change accompanied by a content change. These paths can be shown as text in the diff but are reported as binary content.

findings.detail: Skipped draft triggers are no longer returned by pendingConflictTriggers, and the only code that reactivates them is in the GitHub poller. The supported github.poll = false configuration does not start that poller, so a land-triggered conflict deferred while a PR is a draft remains skipped permanently, even after the PR becomes ready or the daemon restarts.

findings.failure_scenario: Set github.poll = false, create a land conflict trigger while the PR is a draft, then mark the PR ready on the same head. Subsequent conflict processing never sees the skipped trigger and no round starts.

verification.evidence: src/integrations/index.ts:38-45 starts the poller only when `factory.cfg.githubPoll` is true. The only caller that reactivates draft deferrals is src/integrations/github-poller.ts:374: `store.recheckDraftConflictTriggers(pr.url, snap)`. Meanwhile src/db/store.ts:1114 selects only `WHERE state = 'pending'`, and src/pipeline/conflict-round.ts:14 processes only `store.pendingConflictTriggers()`. Draft observations set the trigger to `skipped` with reason `PR is draft` (src/db/store.ts:1177-1191), so subsequent conflict processing cannot revisit it when polling is disabled.

candidates.title: A head change can be missed while a draft lookup is in flight
candidates.detail: The request says to recheck a draft deferral when the poller observes “a new head.” This guard compares the snapshot only with the poller's previous snapshot. If the poller saves the new head before an in-flight live lookup marks an older-head trigger as draft, subsequent polls see the same head and never call recheckDraftConflictTriggers, even though that method would detect the mismatch against the trigger's observed SHA. The deferred trigger remains stale until another qualifying change occurs.
candidates.suggestion: Check deferred triggers against each observed snapshot, or otherwise make recording the deferral and observing the head change race-safe.
candidates.failure_scenario: A trigger for head A starts a live lookup. While it is awaiting GitHub, the poller observes and saves draft head B. The lookup then returns a draft result and marks the A trigger skipped. Later polls continue to observe draft head B, so the skipped trigger is never rechecked for the A-to-B head change.

verdicts.evidence: src/integrations/github-poller.ts:375–376 immediately processes pending triggers with the new snapshot: `for (const trigger of store.pendingConflictTriggers()) { if (trigger.prUrl === pr.url) store.startConflictTrigger(trigger.id, snap, now()); }`. src/db/store.ts:1143–1144 re-reads eligibility: `const trigger = this.pendingConflictTriggers().find((t) => t.id === id); if (!trigger || trigger.nextAttemptAt > now) return null;`. Thus the poller's B observation already marks the pending trigger skipped; the late lookup cannot overwrite it. src/db/store.ts:1177–1180 explicitly checks draft before head movement: `seen.isDraft ? findings.title: A saved head change can be lost before the draft deferral is rechecked
findings.detail: The poller saves the new snapshot before reactivating draft triggers, and uses the saved snapshot on the next pass to decide whether the head changed. If the process stops between those operations, the next pass sees the same head and an open draft, so it never rechecks the deferred trigger. The same ordering can occur when a live lookup finishes after the poller has saved the newer head and marks the trigger as draft. The trigger remains skipped despite the poller having observed a new head.
findings.suggestion: Make recording the observation and reactivating eligible draft triggers durable together, or compare each deferred trigger's recorded head with the current observation on every poll.

findings.title: A stale poller snapshot can permanently discard a land conflict
findings.detail: A land trigger is immediately evaluated against any saved poller snapshot, even if that snapshot predates the approved head. `startConflictTrigger` marks the trigger skipped when the saved head differs, and a later poll cannot reconsider it. The queue has already blocked the entry, so the requested conflict round never starts.
findings.suggestion: Refresh the PR observation before rejecting a land trigger for a stale head, or retain the trigger pending until a current observation can decide it.
findings.failure_scenario: The poller last observed head A; a review round pushes head B and B is approved before the next poll. Landing B conflicts with the base, but the saved snapshot still says A, so the B trigger is permanently skipped as `PR head moved`.

verification.evidence: src/pipeline/conflict-round.ts:21: `if (snapshot) store.startConflictTrigger(trigger.id, snapshot, now());`. src/db/store.ts:1126: `seen.headRefOid !== trigger.head ? "PR head moved"`; src/db/store.ts:1139: `UPDATE conflict_triggers SET state = 'skipped', reason = ? WHERE id = ?`. src/db/store.ts:1071 selects only `WHERE state = 'pending'`.
verification.trigger: Saved head A plus a land trigger for approved head B permanently skips that land trigger. A later poll can independently create a replacement trigger; permanent loss of all conflict resolution is not established.

findings.title: A conflict observed during another round is lost permanently
findings.detail: An active review or conflict round causes the trigger to be marked skipped. The poller emits `pr.conflicting` only on entry into the conflicting state, so if the active round fails or ends without changing the head, subsequent polls do not create another trigger. The unresolved conflict therefore never gets its own round.
findings.suggestion: Keep the trigger pending while another round is active and reconsider it when that round terminates, subject to a fresh PR observation and the daily cap.
findings.failure_scenario: A review round is in flight when the poller first observes the PR as CONFLICTING. The trigger is skipped; the review round later fails without pushing, and every subsequent poll still sees CONFLICTING, so no conflict round starts.

verification.evidence: src/db/store.ts:1130–1141 checks `rounds.some((r) => !TERMINAL_STATUSES.includes(r.status))`, assigns `"round in flight"`, then executes `UPDATE conflict_triggers SET state = 'skipped', reason = ? WHERE id = ?`. src/db/store.ts:1071 retries only `WHERE state = 'pending'`. src/integrations/github-poller.ts:206 emits another trigger only when `next.mergeable === "CONFLICTING" && prev?.mergeable !== "CONFLICTING"`.
verification.trigger: An eligible factory PR first becomes CONFLICTING while a review round is active. Its conflict trigger is permanently skipped. If that review round fails without pushing and subsequent polls continue reporting CONFLICTING, no new trigger is emitted and no conflict round starts.

findings.title: A stale poller snapshot can permanently discard a land trigger
findings.detail: The land path uses any stored GitHub snapshot without refreshing it. `startConflictTrigger` marks the trigger skipped when that snapshot's head differs from the land entry's approved head, even if the snapshot is simply older than the approval. The trigger is then no longer pending, so this landing-queue trigger cannot recover on restart.
findings.suggestion: Refresh or otherwise establish the snapshot's freshness before permanently skipping a land trigger; retain it pending when the observation cannot establish the current head.
findings.failure_scenario: The poller saved head A, the PR advances to B and B is approved before the next poll, and the land queue detects a conflict at B. Processing compares B with the saved A and skips the trigger instead of starting a round.

verification.evidence: src/pipeline/conflict-round.ts:21 uses the saved snapshot without refreshing it: `if (snapshot) store.startConflictTrigger(trigger.id, snapshot, now());`. src/db/store.ts:1126 rejects a mismatch as `"PR head moved"`; src/db/store.ts:1139 persists `state = 'skipped'`.
verification.trigger: The saved snapshot names A while the land queue records a conflict for approved B. Processing discards the B land trigger instead of starting its round.

findings.title: Retrying comment creation can post duplicate resolution comments
findings.detail: The `gh` wrapper retries transient failures around the entire comment command. If GitHub creates the comment but its response is lost, the retry creates another comment without checking the marker again. The preflight marker lookup only protects a later delivery attempt, not retries within this call.
findings.suggestion: Recheck for the marker after an uncertain comment outcome before issuing another creation request.
findings.failure_scenario: GitHub accepts `pr comment`, but the client receives a timeout or connection reset; the retry posts a second comment with the same conflict-round marker.

verification.evidence: src/pipeline/engine.ts:1894 checks the marker once, then :1899 calls `await gh(["pr", "comment", prUrl, "--body-file", "-"], ctx.signal, text)`. The gh wrapper at :1922 uses `withGitHubRetry`. src/git/repos.ts:55 treats command timeouts as transient; :91-97 retries `call` without repeating the comment lookup.
verification.trigger: GitHub creates the comment but the command reports a transient timeout or connection reset, with retry budget remaining. The retry creates another comment containing the same marker.

findings.title: Auto-merge is disabled before validating the PR delivery grant
findings.detail: The new auto-merge mutation occurs before `stored()` and `assertFactoryBranchPush` verify that the PR is still open, belongs to the expected branch and repository, and matches the round's current grant. A stale or invalid round can therefore modify the PR even though delivery is subsequently refused.
findings.suggestion: Validate the current grant and PR identity before disabling auto-merge, and revalidate after the mutation before pushing.
findings.failure_scenario: The PR head branch changes while a conflict round runs and auto-merge is enabled. Delivery disables auto-merge, then rejects the changed branch.

verification.evidence: src/pipeline/engine.ts:1865-1866 executes `if (review.kind === "conflict" && pr.autoMerge) await gh(["pr", "merge", prUrl, "--disable-auto"], ctx.signal)`. Only afterward, :1869-1870 calls `stored()` and `assertFactoryBranchPush(...)`. src/core/delivery.ts:88 rejects a changed branch: `if (pr.headBranch !== branch) return ...`.
verification.trigger: The PR switches head branches during the conflict round and has auto-merge enabled. Delivery disables auto-merge before rejecting the branch mismatch, leaving an unintended PR mutation.

findings.title: Restart tests do not cover a stale saved observation
findings.detail: The restart tests use either no saved observation or one matching the trigger. They therefore pass while a saved observation for an older head causes a durable land trigger to be skipped permanently, and while an outdated open, non-draft observation can start an ineligible round.
findings.suggestion: Add restart and land-trigger cases with an older saved head and with a PR that became draft or closed after the saved observation. Assert that a current observation governs whether the trigger starts.
findings.failure_scenario: A pending trigger for head B is recovered while the database still contains an open CONFLICTING snapshot for head A; the existing tests never exercise this state.

verification.evidence: test/conflict-rounds.test.ts:331 records the trigger with `await remoteHead()`; the saved-observation restart test likewise uses `headRefOid: await remoteHead()` at line 525, so neither exercises mismatched heads. src/pipeline/conflict-round.ts:21 consumes an existing snapshot directly: `if (snapshot) store.startConflictTrigger(trigger.id, snapshot, now());`. src/db/store.ts:1126–1127 classifies `seen.headRefOid !== trigger.head` as `"PR head moved"`, then line 1139 permanently sets `state = 'skipped'`.
verification.trigger: Recover a pending trigger for current head B with a saved OPEN/CONFLICTING snapshot for older head A: recovery skips the trigger without refreshing the observation. The restart tests do not cover this dropped-trigger state.

findings.title: The non-factory polling case bypasses the poller
findings.detail: The non-factory branch inserts a trigger and calls the store consumer directly, so it does not test whether polling a non-factory PR creates a round. A regression in tracking, event generation, or poller consumption for that case would still pass the test.
findings.suggestion: Exercise a tracked non-factory PR through the same fake GitHub poller path as the other eligibility cases and assert that no conflict round starts.
findings.failure_scenario: The poller erroneously starts a conflict round for a non-factory PR, but the test bypasses the poller and continues to pass.

verification.evidence: test/conflict-rounds.test.ts:365–371 handles `eligibility === "non-factory"` by directly calling `recordConflictTrigger(...)` and `startConflictTrigger(...)`. findings.title: Persisted conflict filenames bypass credential redaction
findings.detail: Conflict paths come from the repository under review and are copied into run state without credential redaction. The state is subsequently persisted by updateRun, so a registered credential embedded in a filename reaches storage even though the later PR comment redacts it.
findings.suggestion: Redact credential-bearing paths before storing them or sending them to any external sink, while retaining whatever representation is needed for local conflict resolution.
findings.failure_scenario: A changed repository contains a conflicting filename that includes a registered token; the token is stored in conflictFiles in the run state.

verification.evidence: src/git/merge.ts:79-83 reads conflicting paths from Git and returns `paths`. src/pipeline/engine.ts:2245 assigns `ctx.state.conflictFiles = conflicts`; :2252 persists that state via `ctx.store.updateRun(..., ctx.state)`. src/db/store.ts:1485-1486 stores `state_json` using `json(state)`, whose implementation at :71-72 is plain `JSON.stringify(v)`.

findings.failure_scenario: The PR head or round grant changes while a conflict round is running and auto-merge is enabled. Delivery disables auto-merge, then rejects the stale round.

verification.evidence: src/pipeline/engine.ts:1865-1866 disables auto-merge before :1869 invokes `stored()` and :1870 invokes `assertFactoryBranchPush(...)`. verification.trigger: The grant or PR head changes while the round runs, with auto-merge enabled. Delivery first disables auto-merge and then refuses the stale round, preserving the unintended mutation.

findings.title: An untrusted PR comment can suppress the resolution comment
findings.detail: The idempotency check accepts the marker in any PR comment without verifying its author. A PR participant can post the predictable marker before delivery, causing the factory to treat the required resolution summary as already published.
findings.suggestion: Tie the checkpoint to a trusted factory-authored comment or another durable publication record rather than trusting arbitrary comment text.
findings.failure_scenario: A PR participant posts `<!-- limitless-conflict-round:<run-id> -->` before the round delivers; the merge is pushed but no factory resolution summary is posted.

verification.evidence: src/pipeline/engine.ts:1891 constructs `<!-- limitless-conflict-round:${ctx.run.id} -->`; :1892-1894 reads comments as `{ body?: string }[]` and skips publication whenever `comments?.some((comment) => comment.body?.includes(marker))`. No author or summary-content check accompanies that condition.
verification.trigger: A PR participant posts a comment containing the round's marker before delivery. After pushing the merge, the factory treats that comment as its own completed publication and omits the resolution summary.

candidates.detail: When a saved poller snapshot exists, trigger processing uses it without refreshing the PR. A PR can become draft or close without changing its head, so the saved observation still passes the start checks. Delivery eventually checks draft status, but the forbidden round and its model work have already started.
candidates.suggestion: Refresh the PR state before starting a pending conflict trigger, and leave the trigger pending if its current state cannot be verified.
candidates.failure_scenario: The poller saves an open non-draft PR, the owner converts it to draft, and a land conflict trigger is processed before the next poll. A conflict round starts from the stale snapshot.

candidates.title: A stale poller snapshot permanently discards a land conflict trigger
candidates.detail: The request says a landing queue conflict must start a conflict round and that the trigger must survive restart. Whenever any saved PR snapshot exists, this path uses it without refreshing it. If its head predates the approved head, startConflictTrigger marks the trigger skipped as "PR head moved". The later poll updates the snapshot, but the skipped trigger is never reconsidered, so the blocked entry has no round.
candidates.suggestion: Refresh the PR observation for a land trigger, or leave a trigger pending when its saved observation is older than the trigger head and retry after a fresh observation.
candidates.failure_scenario: The poller last observed head A, the PR advances to B and B is approved before the next poll, then the land queue detects a conflict at B. The saved A snapshot causes the only land trigger to be skipped permanently.

candidates.title: Auto-merge is disabled before verifying the PR and delivery grant
candidates.detail: The new conflict delivery path changes GitHub state before assertFactoryBranchPush validates that the PR is open, still has the authorized head and branch, and still belongs to the expected repository. A stale or invalid round can therefore disable auto-merge on a PR even though its push is subsequently refused. This is an unrequested side effect of a failed delivery.
candidates.suggestion: Validate the current grant and PR identity before disabling auto-merge, and revalidate after the asynchronous call before pushing.
candidates.failure_scenario: A conflict round finishes after the PR head has moved and auto-merge is enabled. Delivery disables auto-merge, then refuses the push because the head no longer matches the reviewed SHA.

candidates.title: The PR comment does not summarize the resolution
candidates.detail: The request requires "one comment summarizing the resolution." The comment reports the base SHA, conflicting file names and resulting SHA, but does not describe how the conflicting changes were reconciled. A reviewer cannot learn the resolution from the comment.
candidates.suggestion: Include a concise, checked description of the actual resolution in the idempotent comment.
candidates.failure_scenario: A conflict in a shared function is resolved and pushed; the PR comment names that file but gives no account of which behavior was retained or changed.

findings.title: A stale poller snapshot can permanently discard a land conflict
findings.detail: The land-trigger consumer treats any saved GitHub snapshot as current and immediately marks a rejected trigger as skipped. A snapshot can predate the land queue's observation. The poller emits pr.conflicting only on entry into the conflicting state, so a later refresh need not generate another trigger.
findings.suggestion: Verify the land trigger against a fresh PR observation, or retain it pending until a sufficiently recent observation can decide eligibility.
findings.failure_scenario: The saved snapshot says the PR is draft and CONFLICTING. The PR is made ready, then the land queue detects a conflict before the next poll. The trigger is skipped as draft; the next poll still sees CONFLICTING, emits no new conflict event, and no round starts.

findings.suggestion: Keep the trigger pending while the owning run is still delivering, and reconsider it when that run reaches a terminal state.

findings.title: Failed trigger lookups are not retried during normal operation
findings.detail: A lookup error leaves the trigger pending, but this catch only logs the error. The queue processes pending triggers only at startup or after another land entry blocks. If polling is disabled or does not produce another observation for the PR, a transient `gh` failure leaves the conflict unresolved indefinitely until a restart or unrelated block.
findings.suggestion: Arrange a bounded, durable retry for pending lookups during normal operation, without depending on another land failure or daemon restart.
findings.failure_scenario: A land conflict is recorded while `gh pr view` temporarily fails and there is no saved PR snapshot. The command later recovers, but no further land conflict or PR poll occurs, so the pending trigger never starts.

verification.evidence: src/pipeline/conflict-round.ts:23–30 explicitly leaves lookup failures pending: “// Lookup failures leave the durable trigger pending for startup to try again.” and “lookupError ??= error; continue;”. src/land/queue.ts:266–268 catches the error and only logs it. Startup processing is guarded by “if (!this.conflictStartup)” (src/land/queue.ts:128), with no scheduled retry. Poll observations can recover pending triggers (src/integrations/github-poller.ts:373–375), but polling is optional: “factory.cfg.githubPoll ? startGitHubPoller(...)” (src/integrations/index.ts:38–39).
verification.trigger: A land conflict creates a pending trigger without a saved PR snapshot; its gh lookup temporarily fails. With polling disabled and no subsequent land failure or restart, recovery of gh does not initiate another lookup, so the conflict round remains pending indefinitely.

findings.title: A stale saved PR observation can start or discard a land trigger
findings.detail: When any saved GitHub snapshot exists, the trigger consumer uses it without checking the current PR. A snapshot from before the land conflict can say the PR is draft or has a different head, causing the durable trigger to be permanently skipped; it can also say the PR is open and ready after it has become draft or closed, starting a round that should not start. Poller startup likewise consumes pending triggers from the saved snapshot before polling. The restart test supplies a current snapshot and therefore does not cover this case.
findings.suggestion: Verify land and resumed triggers against a current PR observation before consuming them, and test stale snapshots against changed draft, state and head values.
findings.failure_scenario: The last poll recorded head A; the PR advances to head B and the landing queue detects a conflict at B before the next poll. Processing compares B to the saved A and marks the only land trigger skipped, so no conflict round starts from that trigger.

findings.detail: The PR lookup converts a missing or invalid `isDraft` field to false. Conflict delivery therefore proceeds when GitHub's response does not establish that the PR is ready for review. The poller admission path likewise treats an absent `isDraft` as false. This fails open at a condition the request explicitly requires.
findings.suggestion: Require a boolean draft state in both the direct lookup and poller snapshot before starting or delivering a conflict round; refuse or leave the trigger pending when it cannot be confirmed.
findings.failure_scenario: A PR lookup or stored snapshot omits `isDraft` for a draft PR. The conflict round is admitted and the delivery check sees `false`, allowing a push to the draft branch.

candidates.title: Failed trigger lookups are not retried during normal operation
candidates.detail: A lookup error leaves the trigger pending, but this catch only logs the error. The queue processes pending triggers only at startup or after another land entry blocks. If polling is disabled or does not produce another observation for the PR, a transient `gh` failure leaves the conflict unresolved indefinitely until a restart or unrelated block.
candidates.suggestion: Arrange a bounded, durable retry for pending lookups during normal operation, without depending on another land failure or daemon restart.
candidates.failure_scenario: A land conflict is recorded while `gh pr view` temporarily fails and there is no saved PR snapshot. The command later recovers, but no further land conflict or PR poll occurs, so the pending trigger never starts.

candidates.title: A stale saved PR observation can start or discard a land trigger
candidates.detail: When any saved GitHub snapshot exists, the trigger consumer uses it without checking the current PR. A snapshot from before the land conflict can say the PR is draft or has a different head, causing the durable trigger to be permanently skipped; it can also say the PR is open and ready after it has become draft or closed, starting a round that should not start. Poller startup likewise consumes pending triggers from the saved snapshot before polling. The restart test supplies a current snapshot and therefore does not cover this case.
candidates.suggestion: Verify land and resumed triggers against a current PR observation before consuming them, and test stale snapshots against changed draft, state and head values.
candidates.failure_scenario: The last poll recorded head A; the PR advances to head B and the landing queue detects a conflict at B before the next poll. Processing compares B to the saved A and marks the only land trigger skipped, so no conflict round starts from that trigger.

candidates.title: The non-factory poller case bypasses the poller
candidates.detail: The non-factory branch manually inserts and consumes a trigger instead of running the poller. It verifies the store's refusal but cannot catch a regression in how polling handles a conflicting non-factory PR, despite the test name and the requested poller acceptance case.
candidates.suggestion: Drive a non-factory conflicting PR through the fake GitHub poller and assert that it starts no round.
candidates.failure_scenario: A future change makes the poller start rounds for non-factory observations while the direct store-level setup in this test still passes.

candidates.title: Missing draft state is treated as permission to proceed
candidates.detail: The PR lookup converts a missing or invalid `isDraft` field to false. Conflict delivery therefore proceeds when GitHub's response does not establish that the PR is ready for review. The poller admission path likewise treats an absent `isDraft` as false. This fails open at a condition the request explicitly requires.
candidates.suggestion: Require a boolean draft state in both the direct lookup and poller snapshot before starting or delivering a conflict round; refuse or leave the trigger pending when it cannot be confirmed.
candidates.failure_scenario: A PR lookup or stored snapshot omits `isDraft` for a draft PR. The conflict round is admitted and the delivery check sees `false`, allowing a push to the draft branch.

candidates.title: Auto-merge is disabled before validating the current PR head
candidates.detail: The new delivery path changes the PR's auto-merge setting before checking that the PR is still open, belongs to the expected repository and branch, and remains at the reviewed head. A stale round can therefore mutate a PR even though the subsequent delivery guard rejects it.
candidates.suggestion: Validate the stored grant and current PR identity before disabling auto-merge, then revalidate after the awaited mutation and before pushing.
candidates.failure_scenario: The PR head changes while a conflict round runs and a user enables auto-merge for the new head. The stale round disables auto-merge, then fails its head check without pushing.

candidates.title: The PR comment does not summarize the resolution
candidates.detail: The request requires that "The PR gets one comment summarizing the resolution." The comment reports the base SHA and conflicted file names, but contains no account of how the conflicting changes were reconciled. A reader cannot assess the resolution from it.
candidates.suggestion: Include a concise, reviewed summary of the actual resolution in the comment, with the existing publication and redaction checks.
candidates.failure_scenario: A conflict in a file is resolved by combining two behavioral changes; the resulting comment names the file and commit but does not explain the combined behavior.

findings.title: Cached first attempts lose the workspace needed by retries after restart
findings.detail: A completed first attempt is reused from state after restart, but the resumed stage cleans the checkout before reaching this line. A pending or newly started retry therefore runs without the build output or other files produced by that first attempt. Previously, a resumed gate stage reran the first attempt and recreated those files before retrying.
findings.suggestion: Preserve the workspace required by a pending retry, or replay the local first attempt before performing the retry after restart.
findings.failure_scenario: A gate setup creates an ignored build directory, a check fails transiently, and the daemon restarts before or during its retry. On resume, checkoutCommitted removes the directory, the cached initial result is reused, and the retry fails because its build output is missing.

verification.evidence: src/pipeline/engine.ts:1157 calls `await checkoutCommitted(...)` before resuming gates. src/git/repos.ts:476 executes `git clean -ffdxq`. src/pipeline/gate-execution.ts:23 returns `results[purpose]` without rerunning setup. src/gates/run.ts:280 retries with `{ ...cfg, setup: [], checks: selected }`.

findings.title: Executor events are never consumed
findings.detail: The shared execution path awaits only `result` and never reads `execution.events`. Gate reporting and landing logs currently work only because the local executor calls hooks directly; an executor implementing the advertised interface has no way to deliver its streamed check events to those consumers.
findings.suggestion: Consume the event stream in the shared execution path and forward events to the appropriate gate and landing reporting hooks, coordinating stream completion and errors with the result.
findings.failure_scenario: An injected executor yields check events and returns a valid GateRun. The stage verdict is computed, but no per-check pipeline events or landing check output are recorded.

findings.title: Restarting a retry removes the first attempt's build output
findings.detail: A resumed gates stage cleans the checkout before retrieving its saved initial result and attaching to the pending retry. The retry therefore runs without files created by the initial attempt, despite the existing requirement that retries see the same build output. Prepare likewise discards changes before resuming its baseline retry.
findings.suggestion: Preserve or reconstruct the first attempt's required workspace state before resuming a local retry, with restart coverage for checks that depend on generated files.
findings.failure_scenario: A setup or initial check creates an untracked build artifact, a later check fails transiently, and the daemon restarts during its retry. The resumed retry cannot find the artifact and produces a different verdict.

verification.evidence: src/pipeline/engine.ts:1157 unconditionally calls `await checkoutCommitted(cwd, undefined, Boolean(ctx.state.implementerIssue))` on stage resume. src/git/repos.ts:476 executes `["git", "clean", "-ffdxq"]`, deleting untracked and ignored build output. src/pipeline/gate-execution.ts:23 then skips the completed initial attempt: `if (results[purpose]) return results[purpose];`. The pending regression retry therefore runs without rebuilding: src/gates/run.ts:280 passes `await runner({ ...cfg, setup: [], checks: selected })`. Resume deletes the artifact, reuses the persisted initial result, and reattaches the local retry with no setup or earlier checks. findings.title: A checkpoint failure leaves started work uncancelled
findings.detail: The executor starts work before persisting its handle, but if persistence rejects, execution exits without attaching or cancelling. An executor whose start actually launches work can continue indefinitely without a durable handle, and a subsequent attempt can start duplicate work.
findings.suggestion: On persistence failure, attach to the returned handle and cancel the execution before propagating the failure, while preserving the original error.
findings.failure_scenario: A remote executor starts a gate suite and the state save fails because the database write fails; the run fails while the untracked suite continues.

Cancellation is installed only afterward at :140-145. src/pipeline/gate-execution.ts:46 persists using `await ctx.save("gate-started");`, and its catch at :54-56 merely checks cancellation and rethrows.
verification.trigger: An injected remote executor starts work, then saving its handle fails. executeGate exits before attaching or registering cancellation, leaving the already-started suite without cleanup or a durable handle. findings.title: Redacting the local handle changes the request replayed after restart
findings.detail: The local handle contains the gate request, including commands and paths, but the persisted copy is transformed by `redactGateData`. On restart, local attach executes that transformed request rather than the trusted gate configuration. Credential redaction or terminal-control stripping can change a valid command or path, so the resumed run can check different behavior or fail unexpectedly.
findings.suggestion: Keep sensitive request data out of the persisted handle and reconstruct the local request from trusted run state when reattaching, without transforming executable input.
findings.failure_scenario: A configured gate command contains a registered credential or a terminal control character; after a restart, the local executor runs the redacted or stripped command.

verification.trigger: A pending local gate command contains a matching registered credential or a removable terminal escape sequence. After restart, attachment executes the sanitized stored command, changing its behavior.

candidates.title: A checkpoint failure leaves started work uncancelled
candidates.detail: The executor starts work before persisting its handle, but if persistence rejects, execution exits without attaching or cancelling. An executor whose start actually launches work can continue indefinitely without a durable handle, and a subsequent attempt can start duplicate work.
candidates.suggestion: On persistence failure, attach to the returned handle and cancel the execution before propagating the failure, while preserving the original error.
candidates.failure_scenario: A remote executor starts a gate suite and the state save fails because the database write fails; the run fails while the untracked suite continues.

candidates.title: Redacting the local handle changes the request replayed after restart
candidates.detail: The local handle contains the gate request, including commands and paths, but the persisted copy is transformed by `redactGateData`. On restart, local attach executes that transformed request rather than the trusted gate configuration. Credential redaction or terminal-control stripping can change a valid command or path, so the resumed run can check different behavior or fail unexpectedly.
candidates.suggestion: Keep sensitive request data out of the persisted handle and reconstruct the local request from trusted run state when reattaching, without transforming executable input.
candidates.failure_scenario: A configured gate command contains a registered credential or a terminal control character; after a restart, the local executor runs the redacted or stripped command.

candidates.title: Executor event streams are never consumed
candidates.detail: The shared execution path awaits only the result and never reads `execution.events`. The local executor invokes hooks directly, masking the issue, but an injected executor that reports progress and check results through the interface loses those events; landing logs and pipeline gate events are absent.
candidates.suggestion: Consume the event stream while awaiting the result and route events to the appropriate hooks, propagating stream failures according to the executor contract.
candidates.failure_scenario: An executor yields check events and returns a GateRun without invoking local hooks. The gate completes but its check events and landing log output are silently missing.

candidates.title: Persisting a sanitized local request can change the command replayed after restart

A restart attaches using that transformed request, so a gate command or working directory containing a registered credential or terminal control character can differ from the original. The initial attachment uses the unsanitized handle, making behavior depend on whether the daemon restarted.
candidates.suggestion: Persist a replayable request without storing secrets, for example by reconstructing the local request from trusted run state on resume, and keep redaction at the storage boundary.
candidates.failure_scenario: A base gate command contains a string registered for credential redaction. The daemon stops after saving the handle; on resume, local attachment executes the command with that string replaced by the redaction marker.

candidates.title: Restart tests do not exercise replay of a persisted local request
candidates.detail: The restart cases use a fake LAN executor whose handle has no request, while the local replay test serializes a handle directly without passing it through the persistence redaction path. Consequently they cannot catch a local request being changed before restart.

candidates.title: Legacy resume test cannot distinguish local selection from injected selection
candidates.detail: The legacy-state test resumes with no injected executor, so local is the only available choice. It does not test the stated compatibility rule when another executor is selected. The selection code uses the injected executor whenever there is no stored handle.
candidates.suggestion: Resume a pre-change run with a non-local fake executor configured and assert that the legacy gate runs locally without starting the fake.
candidates.failure_scenario: A run created before handles existed resumes with a non-local executor injected and starts that executor instead of local; the current test still passes.

candidates.title: Redacting the local handle changes the command replayed after restart
candidates.detail: The local handle embeds the gate request, including its working directory and base-configured commands. Redacting the entire handle before persistence changes any command or path containing a registered credential and strips terminal control sequences. On restart, `localExecutor.attach` executes that altered request rather than the original trusted gate configuration. A resumed gate can therefore test different conditions and report a pass for a check that would have failed.
candidates.suggestion: Persist only the local execution identity and reconstruct its request from the trusted base configuration and current run context on resume, or otherwise preserve execution semantics without storing secret-bearing values.
candidates.failure_scenario: A base gate command compares a value against a registered credential. The daemon restarts while that gate is pending; the persisted command contains the redaction marker instead of the original value, so the replay evaluates a different condition and can pass incorrectly.

candidates.title: Resumed retries reuse results after their build output has been removed
candidates.detail: The request says regression retries and baseline retries do not change, and the surrounding code requires retries to see the first attempt's build output. After a restart during a retry, this returns the saved initial result without rerunning the initial gate, while prepare has already called discardChanges and the gates stage has called checkoutCommitted. A local retry therefore runs in a cleaned checkout without the files produced by its initial attempt, potentially changing a pass into a failure or vice versa.
candidates.suggestion: Restore the first attempt's required workspace state on local resume, or rerun the initial local execution before retrying while preserving the stored handle semantics for executors that can reattach.
candidates.failure_scenario: A setup command generates an untracked build artifact, an initial check fails transiently, and the daemon restarts during its retry. On resume the artifact is cleaned, the saved initial result is reused, and the retry fails because the artifact is missing.

candidates.title: Landing checks discard the execution handle
candidates.detail: The request requires that the caller persist the handle before awaiting the execution and that landing queue checks use the executor. This call supplies neither a stored handle nor a persistence callback, so executeGate uses its no-op default. A restart during landing checks starts another execution instead of attaching to the existing one, leaving remote work duplicated and its result unobserved.
candidates.suggestion: Persist the landing execution handle in durable queue state before attaching, and restore it when resuming the checks.
candidates.failure_scenario: A landing check is running on an executor whose work survives daemon restart. The daemon restarts before the result arrives; the queue starts a second execution because the first handle was never stored.

candidates.title: Executor events are never consumed
candidates.detail: The requested Execution exposes events and the local executor is to preserve gate events. executeGate awaits only result and never reads execution.events; existing progress and landing logs work only because the local implementation calls injected hooks directly. candidates.suggestion: Consume the execution event stream in the shared path and translate its events into the existing hooks, including setup and status events as needed.
candidates.failure_scenario: An injected executor emits check results through its events iterable while its result is pending. The pipeline displays no check progress, and landing writes only the log header despite the executor providing output.

findings.title: Cargo home allowance exposes registry credentials to gate commands
findings.detail: The gate profile grants file reads throughout Cargo home, but neither the built-in deny list nor the later specific-deny rules exclude Cargo's credentials or credentials.toml files. Changing CARGO_HOME for the gate process does not prevent an untrusted command from reading the original files by absolute path. This leaves registry tokens accessible to candidate code despite the requirement that credential stores fall outside the gate allowlist.
findings.suggestion: Exclude Cargo credential files from the effective gate profile while retaining access to the toolchain files Cargo needs, and add a probe using a temporary Cargo home containing a stand-in credential.
findings.failure_scenario: The owner has a registry token in ~/.cargo/credentials.toml and a malicious test runs a command that reads that absolute path and sends its contents over HTTPS.

findings.detail: The policy derives the home directory from os.homedir(), which uses HOME when set. The request specifically notes that ssh finds keys through the password database rather than HOME. If the daemon starts with HOME pointing elsewhere, the policy denies credential paths under that alternate directory but leaves the account's password-database home and its SSH keys readable to gates and editors.
