findings.title: Resume discards handles for in-flight retries
findings.detail: Stored handles are reused only for baseline, initial, and rebase executions. A pending timeout, baseline retry, or regression retry is discarded when the stage resumes, and the executor starts replacement work instead of attaching to the existing execution. Cancellation cannot recover work owned by a previous daemon process. The new test explicitly expects this behavior, but it contradicts the requested restart contract.
findings.suggestion: Persist enough attempt context to resume each retry and attach to its recorded handle without starting it again.
findings.failure_scenario: The daemon restarts after a remote regression retry starts but before its result is recorded. On resume, the retry handle is discarded and another execution is started while the original may still be running.

verification.evidence: src/pipeline/gate-execution.ts:24-32 requires `pending.purpose === purpose` and `["baseline", "initial", "rebase"].includes(purpose)`; otherwise it executes `ctx.state.gateExecution = undefined; await ctx.save()`. src/pipeline/engine.ts:1156 resumes with purpose `"initial"`, whereas :1195 stores `"regression-retry"`. src/gates/executor.ts:40 only cancels executions found in the process-local `liveExecutions` map.
verification.trigger: Restart with a persisted regression-retry handle. Resume discards it and starts initial gate work again; a remote retry survives because the new process has no live execution to cancel.

findings.title: Handle is cleared before the result has a durable checkpoint
findings.detail: The execution handle is removed and saved as soon as executeGate settles, before the caller records the gate result or the stage completion. A restart in that interval loses both the handle and the result, so the resumed stage starts the execution again. This also affects the initial execution, which otherwise has an attach path.
findings.suggestion: Keep the handle until the corresponding result or completed stage is durably saved, and resume by attaching when that checkpoint is absent.
findings.failure_scenario: A daemon stops immediately after the gate-result save but before the gates stage saves its comparison. Restarting the run starts a new execution instead of attaching to the completed one.

verification.evidence: src/pipeline/gate-execution.ts:63-64 executes `ctx.state.gateExecution = undefined; await ctx.save("gate-result")` before returning the result to its caller. The comparison is assigned later at src/pipeline/engine.ts:1219 (`ctx.state.lastGates = cmp`); the completed-stage checkpoint is saved only after `await fn(stage)` at src/pipeline/context.ts:418-425. Without a stored handle, src/gates/executor.ts:159 calls `executor.start(req, signal)`.
verification.trigger: Stop after the gate-result save but before the comparison and completed-stage checkpoint. Resume has neither a handle nor a completed-stage result, so it starts another execution instead of attaching to the completed one.

findings.title: Landing checks never persist an execution handle
findings.detail: The landing queue calls executeGate without a persistence callback or stored handle, so its default no-op persistence is used. A restart during landing checks cannot reattach to work started by an executor and instead starts another suite. This leaves one of the explicitly required daemon gate paths outside the durability contract.
findings.suggestion: Store the landing execution handle in durable queue state before attaching, and use it when the queue resumes.
findings.failure_scenario: The daemon restarts while a landing suite is running on an executor. The resumed queue starts another suite, leaving the original execution untracked.

verification.evidence: src/land/queue.ts:386-401 calls `executeGate(..., this.deps.gateExecutor)` without a stored handle or persistence callback. src/gates/executor.ts:150-160 defaults to `stored?: ExecutionHandle` and `persist ... = async () => {}`, then uses `stored ?? (await executor.start(req, signal))`. src/land/queue.ts:297 explicitly states: '`checking` re-runs the checks from the start, like a `queued` entry.'
verification.trigger: Restart during landing checks before pushedSha is recorded: recovery starts a new execution because no handle was persisted. Any executor work surviving the daemon becomes untracked. Local rerunning remains intentional, but the required durable executor identity is missing.

findings.title: Pending retry executions are discarded on restart
findings.detail: Only baseline, initial, and rebase handles are eligible for reattachment. On restart during a timeout, baseline retry, or regression retry, the stage starts over and discards the stored handle. After a daemon restart, cancelGateExecution cannot find an execution in its process-local map, so a remote execution can continue while replacement work starts. findings.title: Ancestor exceptions expose files directly under the home directory
findings.detail: The profile grants full file reads for four filenames in every ancestor of every allowed path. Since the checkout and toolchains normally reside under home, this makes `~/package.json`, `~/bunfig.toml`, `~/tsconfig.json`, and `~/jsconfig.json` readable to gate code despite the requested home-wide deny. These files can contain private registry URLs, tokens, or other owner data.
findings.suggestion: Keep files outside the stated allowlist unreadable; arrange tool discovery without granting arbitrary ancestor file contents.
findings.failure_scenario: A gate command reads `~/bunfig.toml` containing a private registry token; the literal allow overrides the home deny.

verification.evidence: src/harness/read-policy.ts:190-191 removes ancestor denies from specificReadDenies: `denied.filter((deny) => !allowed.some((allow) => allow !== deny && within(deny, allow)))`. Lines 204-208 grant ancestor literals including `"bunfig.toml"`. src/harness/sandbox.ts:51 emits `(allow file-read* ${paths(ancestors.literals, "literal")})` after the home deny at line 48.
verification.trigger: With a checkout or toolchain beneath home and a token in ~/bunfig.toml, the generated literal exception permits a gate to read the token by absolute path.

findings.title: Cargo configuration remains readable even when it contains credentials
findings.detail: The gate allowlist explicitly grants reads of Cargo's `config` and `config.toml`, and `runConfined` also copies them into readable scratch. Cargo configuration can contain registry tokens and authenticated proxy URLs, so denying only `credentials` and `credentials.toml` does not keep every credential store outside the allowlist.
findings.suggestion: Avoid exposing credential-bearing Cargo configuration to candidate commands; preserve only the trusted configuration needed for toolchain discovery.
findings.failure_scenario: An owner stores a registry token in `~/.cargo/config.toml`; a malicious gate reads that file or its scratch copy and exfiltrates the token.

verification.evidence: src/harness/read-policy.ts:166 explicitly allows `["bin", "registry", "git", "config", "config.toml"].map((p) => join(cargo, p))`; only Cargo's `credentials` and `credentials.toml` are added to credential denies at lines 148-150. src/harness/sandbox.ts:249-251 also copies both configuration files unchanged: `if (existsSync(source)) copyFileSync(source, join(cargo, name));`. Line 267 exposes that directory as `CARGO_HOME: cargo`.
verification.trigger: If ~/.cargo/config.toml contains a registry token, a gate can read the allowed original or the unchanged copy in its readable scratch directory.

findings.title: Ancestor discovery grants gate reads to files under home
findings.detail: The ancestor exceptions grant full file-read access to package.json, bunfig.toml, tsconfig.json and jsconfig.json at every ancestor of an allowed path. Because the home directory is normally an ancestor of a checkout or toolchain, the resulting Seatbelt profile allows these files directly under home despite the home-wide deny. A report can include both a complete verifier observation and a shorter quotation of it; the complete line is withheld, but the partial quotation can remain visible when it contains no separately catalogued literal. Previously, a match caused the entire report value to be withheld. This exposes holdout-only verifier prose to the reviewer and potentially to the next implementer.
candidates.suggestion: Protect partial quotations of private verifier observations, or withhold the containing report when safe separation cannot be established. Add a regression test with a complete observation and a shorter quotation on separate lines.
candidates.failure_scenario: A private criterion has evidence "Verifier saw the amber lantern glow." A report contains that sentence on one line and "The amber lantern glow was observed" on another. The first line matches the catalogued prose, while the second has no independently harvested syntax-shaped literal and is returned.

candidates.title: Partial quotations of holdout prose can remain visible in reports
candidates.detail: The request says that “any report line that quotes” holdout test text stays withheld. The catalogue generally records complete scenario phrases and syntax-shaped literals, so a report line quoting only an ordinary fragment of a longer scenario can pass every match and be returned. This limitation predates the diff, but remains an unmet privacy requirement of the change.
candidates.suggestion: Protect partial quotations of holdout prose and add a regression test covering a report line that quotes only a fragment of a longer scenario.
candidates.failure_scenario: A holdout description is “The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog.” and a report outside the holdout section says “Observed quick brown fox”. The fragment has no syntax-shaped literal and does not match the complete scenario phrase, so the report exposes it.

verdicts.evidence: src/integrations/mcp-change.ts:460 uses "--diff-filter=D"; lines 471–473 define "prText = (path: string) => !deleted.has(path)" and require it in safePath. Lines 485–499 return the diff for qualifying files. This implements the request's explicit exemption for diffs of files present in the PR tree; the candidate's tracked, partially modified file qualifies.
verdicts.trigger: Removing one line from a tracked file while retaining the file returns the removed line in its diff. That is the requested behavior for files in the PR tree, rather than exposure of holdout-only files outside that tree.

verdicts.evidence: src/integrations/mcp-change.ts:243–244 catalogues the complete private observation with "details.add(prose)". Lines 347–356 then process each line independently and return ": line" when none of the complete patterns matches. src/pipeline/prompts.ts:247 harvests only syntax-shaped literals from observations: "if (observed !== undefined) collectLiterals(observed)".
verdicts.trigger: A private criterion contains "Verifier saw the amber lantern glow." A report outside the holdout section contains that complete sentence and a separate line "The amber lantern glow was observed". The complete quotation is withheld, but the second line exposes the private observation fragment, assuming no other catalogue entry matches it.

verdicts.evidence: src/pipeline/prompts.ts:239–243 collects whole prose phrases, sentences and syntax-shaped literals: "collect(source.trim())", "collect(sentence.trim())", and "collectLiterals(source)". src/integrations/mcp-change.ts:351–356 withholds only matching lines and otherwise returns ": line"; it does not match arbitrary prose fragments.
verdicts.trigger: The holdout description is "The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog." and a report outside the removed holdout section contains "Observed quick brown fox". With no other matching private detail, that partial quotation remains visible.

findings.title: Verifier notes can expose holdout-only prose in reports
findings.detail: Verifier notes are passed to collect without privateProse enabled. That collects only recognizable literals and holdout phrases, so an ordinary sentence unique to the verifier is not added to the redaction catalogue. If a report quotes that sentence outside the holdout section, it is returned unchanged, contrary to the requirement to withhold verifier prose and report lines quoting holdout material.
findings.suggestion: Treat verifier notes as private observations when building the catalogue, and add a test with a plain-prose verifier note quoted in a report.
findings.failure_scenario: A verifier note says "The violet otter failed again." for a holdout check, and the report repeats that sentence outside the holdout section. If those words are absent from the holdout scenarios and public sources, the report exposes the sentence.

verification.evidence: src/integrations/mcp-change.ts:254 calls `collect(verify?.notes)` without enabling `privateProse`. At lines 239–244, observed text contributes literals via `privateHoldoutDetails(...)`, while whole prose is added only if `privateProse` is true. src/pipeline/prompts.ts:247 processes observed text only with `collectLiterals(observed)`, which does not harvest ordinary unquoted sentences. Reports outside the holdout section pass through this catalogue-based redactor at src/integrations/mcp-change.ts:522: `privacy(withoutHoldoutSection(report, holdoutRedact))`.
verification.trigger: Verifier notes contain “The violet otter failed again.” and a persisted report repeats it outside the holdout section. With no matching scenario details, syntax-shaped literals, private strings or credentials, the sentence never enters the redaction catalogue and is returned to the MCP reviewer.

findings.suggestion: Add a report line quoting the hidden test text and assert that the line is withheld while an unrelated report line remains visible.
findings.failure_scenario: A report quotes hidden test code containing details absent from the holdout scenario, and the change view returns that quotation.

verification.evidence: test/mcp-proxy.test.ts:180 writes hidden code `expect(uppercase('${hidden}')).toBe('PRIVATE');`, but :187 puts `${hidden}` in the scenario and :206 quotes only `Quoted hidden test: ${hidden}` in the report. verification.trigger: A report quotes hidden-test-only code outside the holdout section—for example, `toBe('PRIVATE')` from this fixture—whose details occur in neither scenarios nor recorded verifier observations and match no private strings or credentials. The quotation is returned unchanged; the current test never exercises it.

Verifier: 15 candidates, 15 checked, 0 refuted.

findings.title: Cancellation during the new post-merge lookup is overwritten
findings.detail: The new lookup awaits after the merge succeeds. If the land is cancelled while that lookup is in flight, cancellation aborts its signal and records the entry as cancelled, but the catch converts the abort to null and landed() unconditionally writes the entry back to landed. A client that resolves after cancellation has the same effect.
findings.suggestion: After the lookup, re-read the entry and honor the abort or cancelled state before recording the result; make the terminal transition conditional.
findings.failure_scenario: A user cancels an active land while getGitHubPr is waiting after a successful merge; the entry changes from cancelled to landed when the lookup rejects or returns.

verification.evidence: src/land/queue.ts:257–258: `this.inFlight.get(id)?.abort(); this.finish(id, "cancelled", "cancelled");`. At :620–621, the lookup uses `.catch(() => null)` and then unconditionally calls `this.landed(...)`. At :381, landed calls `this.finish(entry.id, "landed", ...)`; src/db/store.ts:2768 updates with only `WHERE id = ?`, without a state guard.
verification.trigger: Cancel an entry while the post-merge metadata lookup is pending. Whether it returns or rejects on abort, landed() overwrites cancelled with landed.

findings.title: Missing merge metadata can remain missing permanently
findings.detail: If the post-merge lookup fails or returns an observation without metadata, landed() records the run as merged with null fields. Reconciliation then only examines an already-saved snapshot and never fetches this PR. With polling disabled, or with the last saved snapshot still OPEN, no later observation will fill the fields, even when GitHub has the merge information.
findings.suggestion: Provide a bounded, retryable way to obtain a confirmed merged observation when the initial metadata lookup fails, including installations without polling.
findings.failure_scenario: The merge succeeds but the following gh pr view times out, and the installation has polling disabled. The parent run retains null mergedBy and mergedAt indefinitely.

verification.evidence: src/land/queue.ts:620-621 catches the post-merge read failure with `.catch(() => null)` and calls `landed` with null; lines 365-379 persist `merged: true` with nullable metadata. src/integrations/github-notifier.ts:159-168 handles already-merged terminal runs using only `savedSnapshot(store.githubPrData(run.prUrl))`, then unconditionally `continue`s. src/integrations/index.ts:50-57 does not start the poller when `githubPoll` is false.
verification.trigger: A queue merge succeeds for a succeeded/resolved parent, the post-merge PR read times out, polling is disabled, and no MERGED snapshot is saved. Subsequent reconciliation skips fetching that PR, leaving mergedBy and mergedAt null indefinitely.

findings.title: Later metadata repair leaves the merge feed item incorrect
findings.detail: Updating only mergedBy and mergedAt does not update the existing run.merged feed item: the feed trigger captures those values when merged changes from false to true. Thus the newly added repair path can make the run record correct while the feed still reports null fields, which is the discrepancy the request identifies.
findings.suggestion: Ensure the feed exposes the confirmed metadata when it arrives, while preserving the intended event ordering and deduplication semantics.
findings.failure_scenario: The initial post-merge observation has null metadata; a later saved MERGED snapshot supplies a login and timestamp. The run is updated, but its existing run.merged feed item's data still contains null for both fields.

verification.evidence: src/db/store.ts:1821–1824 repairs an already merged run using only `this.updateRun(id, { mergedBy, mergedAt });`. src/db/migrations/20261003T2139-run-resolution.sql:7 watches `UPDATE OF status, pr_url, merged`, and lines 11–14 capture merge metadata only `WHERE NEW.merged AND NOT OLD.merged`. src/db/store.ts:91–92 reads persisted feed `data` directly: `SELECT ... summary, data FROM feed`. Thus metadata repair leaves the original feed data unchanged.
verification.trigger: The queue records merged=true with null merger and timestamp, creating a run.merged feed item with null fields. A later saved MERGED snapshot repairs the run row, but the existing feed item retains both nulls.

findings.title: A cancelled land can be overwritten after the metadata lookup
findings.detail: The new awaited lookup creates a cancellation window after the merge succeeds. If cancellation aborts the lookup, its rejection is converted to null and landed() unconditionally changes the cancelled entry to landed. A lookup that ignores the signal has the same result when it eventually returns.
findings.suggestion: After the lookup, re-read the entry and preserve a terminal cancellation before writing the land state; record the confirmed merge separately if needed.
findings.failure_scenario: A user cancels an entry while getGitHubPr is in flight after the merge command succeeds; the entry briefly becomes cancelled and is then overwritten as landed.

verification.evidence: src/land/queue.ts:254–258 permits cancellation of an active entry and records `"cancelled"`. At :620–621, `await ... .catch(() => null)` is followed by unconditional `this.landed(...)`; :381 records `"landed"`. src/db/store.ts:2768 has no conditional state check on the update.
verification.trigger: Cancel during the new metadata await after a successful merge; completion of the lookup changes the cancelled entry to landed.

findings.title: A failed metadata lookup can leave merge fields null permanently
findings.detail: The lookup failure is silently discarded and both runs are marked merged. The poller excludes merged runs from githubTracked, while reconciliation only reads an already-saved snapshot for merged runs. If that snapshot still says OPEN, no later observation fills the fields.
findings.suggestion: Provide a bounded recovery path for missing merge metadata, or persist a suitable confirmed merge observation before excluding the PR from polling.
findings.failure_scenario: GitHub accepts the merge, but the subsequent gh pr view times out or returns an OPEN observation; mergedBy and mergedAt remain null even after GitHub becomes available.

verification.evidence: src/land/queue.ts:620 converts lookup failure to null. At :370–378, a null or OPEN observation supplies null merge metadata while `merged: true` is persisted. src/integrations/github-notifier.ts:159–168 handles already-merged runs only through `savedSnapshot(store.githubPrData(run.prUrl))`, then `continue`s; its comment explicitly says `missing metadata must never trigger another fetch`.
verification.trigger: With polling disabled and no saved MERGED snapshot, the post-merge lookup fails or returns OPEN for a succeeded run. The run becomes merged with null metadata, and later reconciliation never fetches it again even after GitHub recovers.

findings.title: Backfilling run fields leaves the merge feed event inaccurate
findings.detail: resolveMergedRun updates the run's metadata after it was marked merged, but the run.merged feed entry is created only on the merged transition. Consequently its stored JSON retains the original null values even when the run is later repaired.
findings.suggestion: Ensure the feed presents the recovered metadata, including for already-created merge events.
findings.failure_scenario: A queue merge initially records null metadata and a later saved MERGED snapshot supplies the actor and time; the run has the correct fields but its existing run.merged feed item still reports null for both.

verification.evidence: src/integrations/github-notifier.ts:165 backfills through `store.resolveMergedRun(...)`. src/db/store.ts:1821-1824 updates only `{ mergedBy, mergedAt }` for an already-merged terminal run. src/db/migrations/20261003T2139-run-resolution.sql:7 watches only `UPDATE OF status, pr_url, merged`; lines 11-14 capture merge metadata into the feed only `WHERE NEW.merged AND NOT OLD.merged`. src/db/store.ts:716-728 reads the stored feed rows without refreshing their metadata.
verification.trigger: The queue first records merged=true with null metadata, creating a run.merged feed item containing nulls. A later saved MERGED snapshot backfills the run fields, but the existing feed item's mergedBy and mergedAt remain null.

findings.title: An in-progress push can be reported as the current head
findings.detail: reviewableHead returns superseded whenever a push is in progress, even when the recorded SHA is still the old head. The new diagnostic labels that recorded SHA as the current head, although the push has not yet established the new one.
findings.suggestion: Only identify a current head when it is known to be current; otherwise report that the push is in progress.
findings.failure_scenario: A change view is requested while pushingTo is true and the recorded head is the pre-push SHA; the response calls that old SHA the current head.

verification.evidence: src/integrations/mcp-head.ts:14: `if (recorded?.pushing || ...) return { headSha: null, problem: "superseded" }`. src/integrations/mcp-change.ts:416 passes `superseded(recorded?.sha)`, which at line 408 labels it `current head ${sha}`. src/db/store.ts:1546 explicitly says a head recorded when a push began is `only what the push intended`.
verification.trigger: A request arrives during a push, before its remote outcome is known. The response labels the recorded SHA as current despite that uncertainty. Production beginPrPush records the intended destination SHA, so it need not specifically be the pre-push SHA described in the candidate.

findings.title: A cancellation during the new metadata lookup is overwritten
findings.detail: The metadata lookup adds an await after the merge succeeds. If the land entry is cancelled while that lookup is in flight, its rejection is swallowed and landed() unconditionally changes the entry from cancelled to landed.
findings.suggestion: After the lookup, re-read the entry and condition the final state change on it still being active; add a test that holds the lookup open while cancelling.
findings.failure_scenario: GitHub reports a successful merge, the metadata client is still pending, and a caller cancels the land entry. The client rejects on abort, after which the queue records the entry as landed instead of preserving cancelled.

verification.evidence: src/land/queue.ts:257–258 aborts the request and records cancellation. At :620, `.catch(() => null)` swallows the abort rejection; :621 unconditionally invokes landed(), which at :381 finishes the entry as `"landed"`. src/db/store.ts:2768 updates by id without guarding the previous state.
verification.trigger: Cancel while the post-merge metadata client is pending and rejects on abort; the swallowed rejection leads to cancelled being overwritten as landed.

findings.title: Backfilled merge metadata never reaches the existing feed event
findings.detail: When the immediate post-merge lookup lacks metadata, landed() emits run.merged with null fields. A later observation updates only the run row; the feed trigger fires only on the initial merged transition, so the original event permanently retains null mergedBy and mergedAt. This leaves the specific feed inconsistency in the request unresolved for delayed observations.
findings.suggestion: Ensure the feed exposes the subsequently confirmed metadata while preserving the intended event semantics.
findings.failure_scenario: The merge succeeds but its immediate PR lookup returns no metadata; a later poll observes the merger and timestamp. The run row has both values, but its run.merged feed item still has null values.

verification.evidence: src/integrations/github-notifier.ts:159–165 passes a later saved MERGED snapshot to `store.resolveMergedRun(...)`. For an already merged run, src/db/store.ts:1821–1824 only calls `this.updateRun(id, { mergedBy, mergedAt });`. The feed trigger in src/db/migrations/20261003T2139-run-resolution.sql:7,11–14 inserts merge data only on `NEW.merged AND NOT OLD.merged`; it does not repair existing events.
verification.trigger: The immediate post-merge lookup supplies no metadata. Later polling saves the merger and timestamp, updating the run row while its run.merged feed item still reports null values.

findings.title: The delayed-observation test does not check the feed fields
findings.detail: The new test checks that the run row is backfilled and that the number of merge events stays constant, but never checks the existing event's metadata after reconciliation. It therefore passes even though the feed continues to show null fields, the original reported failure.
findings.suggestion: After the later observation, assert the parent run's run.merged feed item contains the observed merger and timestamp.
findings.failure_scenario: A merge is initially recorded without metadata and the poller supplies it later; the test passes while the feed still reports both fields as null.

verification.evidence: test/land-queue.test.ts:411–416 checks metadata with `expect(store.getRun(pr.run.id)).toMatchObject(...)`, but checks the feed only with `expect(feed()).toHaveLength(2)`. src/db/store.ts:1821–1824 backfills an already merged run using `this.updateRun(id, { mergedBy, mergedAt }); return false;`. The feed trigger in src/db/migrations/20261003T2139-run-resolution.sql:7–14 snapshots metadata only `WHERE NEW.merged AND NOT OLD.merged`; src/db/store.ts:91–92 reads stored `data FROM feed`.
verification.trigger: The queue records a merge with null metadata, then later observations supply the actor and timestamp. Run fields are backfilled, but the existing run.merged feed data retains both nulls, and the delayed-observation test passes because it asserts only feed counts.

findings.title: Redact consumer names before recording approvals
findings.detail: The new consumer value is passed directly into recordApproval. The database stores it verbatim, and the review_approvals trigger copies it into the feed summary and data. A registered credential supplied as a consumer name therefore leaves the process and persists without redaction.
findings.suggestion: Apply credential redaction to the normalized reviewer identity before passing it to recordApproval, and cover the database and feed outputs with a test.
findings.failure_scenario: An MCP client submits an approval with consumer set to a registered API token; the token appears in review_approvals and the review.approved feed item.

verification.evidence: src/pipeline/review-round.ts:196-201 sets reviewer to `mcpRequestedBy(parsed.data.consumer)` and passes it to `store.recordApproval(...)`. src/feed.ts:36 only prefixes it: `` `mcp:${consumer}` ``. src/db/store.ts:1518-1522 inserts `reviewer` directly into `review_approvals` without redaction. src/db/migrations/20261004T1757-review-rounds.sql:54-59 copies `NEW.reviewer` into the review.approved feed summary and data.
verification.trigger: Submit a valid approval for the current PR head with consumer equal to a registered API token (the daemon token is 64 characters, within the 200-character consumer limit). The unredacted token is persisted in review_approvals and the review.approved feed record.

findings.title: Do not overwrite a cancellation while fetching merge metadata
findings.detail: The new metadata lookup adds an await after the merge succeeds. If the land is cancelled while that lookup is pending, cancel() records cancelled and aborts the signal, but the caught lookup failure then calls landed(), which unconditionally changes the entry back to landed and emits another feed event.
findings.suggestion: Re-read the entry after the lookup and condition the terminal update on its still being in the expected merging state.
findings.failure_scenario: A merge succeeds, the PR metadata request is still pending, and a user cancels the land entry. The request aborts, but the entry changes from cancelled to landed afterward.

verification.evidence: src/land/queue.ts:620–621: `const observed = await ... .catch(() => null); this.landed(...)`. There is no abort or current-state check between those statements. Cancellation records `"cancelled"` at :258, but landed() records `"landed"` at :381 through the unconditional update in src/db/store.ts:2768.
verification.trigger: A user cancels after the merge succeeds but before metadata lookup completion. The lookup abort is swallowed and the subsequent finish overwrites cancellation.

findings.title: Later merge metadata does not correct the feed event
findings.detail: The request says to fill the parent run's `run.merged` fields from the recorded merge. If the queue's immediate GitHub lookup fails or returns no metadata, it emits a `run.merged` event with null fields. This later update fills the run row but does not update that event or emit a correction, so the feed retains the original disagreement permanently. The new test explicitly verifies that no further event is produced but does not check the original event's data after reconciliation.
findings.suggestion: Make the feed expose the subsequently confirmed metadata, either by correcting the existing event or by a suitable correction mechanism that preserves feed semantics.
findings.failure_scenario: The post-merge lookup returns null, then a later saved PR snapshot contains the merger and timestamp; the run row is corrected but its `run.merged` feed item still reports both as null.

verification.evidence: src/db/store.ts:1821–1824 handles metadata backfill with `this.updateRun(id, { mergedBy, mergedAt });` and returns. src/db/migrations/20261003T2139-run-resolution.sql:11–14 stores `json_object(... 'mergedBy', NEW.merged_by, 'mergedAt', NEW.merged_at ...)` only `WHERE NEW.merged AND NOT OLD.merged`. Feed reads use stored `data` directly (src/db/store.ts:91–92), so the earlier event remains unchanged.
verification.trigger: A merge is recorded with null metadata after the post-merge lookup returns null. A later saved PR snapshot corrects the run's merger and timestamp, but its existing run.merged feed item continues to show both as null.

findings.title: MCP approvals still default to human
findings.detail: The request says to record the MCP consumer instead of `reviewer: "human"`. The new consumer argument is optional, and an existing MCP approval call without it still reaches `submitReview` with neither consumer nor reviewer and records `human`. The added test explicitly expects that old behavior, so it does not establish the requested behavior for all MCP approvals.
findings.suggestion: Ensure MCP approval calls provide a consumer identity, or require one for MCP approvals and make the tool instructions explain that requirement.
findings.failure_scenario: An MCP client calls `limitless_review` with the previously documented run, verdict and reviewedSha arguments but no consumer; the resulting `review.approved` feed item still names `human`.

verification.evidence: src/feed.ts:14 defines `consumer: consumer.optional()`. src/integrations/mcp.ts:343 forwards `backend.review(run, ReviewVerdictSchema.parse(input))` without adding provenance. src/pipeline/review-round.ts:196–201 selects `parsed.data.consumer === undefined ? (parsed.data.reviewer ?? "human") : mcpRequestedBy(parsed.data.consumer)` and passes it to `store.recordApproval`. test/mcp-proxy.test.ts:93 explicitly expects `"human"` when consumer is omitted.
verification.trigger: An MCP client submits a valid approval with run, verdict and reviewedSha but omits consumer. The approval and review.approved feed item identify the reviewer as human.

findings.title: A concurrent snapshot change can report the old head as current
findings.detail: The final consistency check reports `now.sha` whenever the snapshot and recorded head disagree. If the saved snapshot advances during the awaited Git reads while the recorded head still contains the old SHA, the response calls that old SHA the current head. The request asks a changed-head error to give the new head.
findings.suggestion: Only name a head when the current observations agree on it; otherwise report the mismatch without presenting the old recorded SHA as current.
findings.failure_scenario: A read starts at head A, the saved PR snapshot advances to B during Git reads, and the recorded head remains A. The response says `current head A`.

verification.evidence: src/integrations/mcp-change.ts:575 checks `reviewableHead(JSON.parse(current).headRefOid, ...).headSha !== headSha`, but line 578 returns `superseded(now?.sha)`. Thus snapshot B versus recorded A produces `current head A`. Normal polling first calls `observePrHead` (src/integrations/github-poller.ts:341), but its post-await nudge path saves the captured snapshot without another current-head guard: lines 400–401, `const res = await call(...); if (res) save(head, []);`.

candidates.title: A failed post-merge lookup permanently records incomplete merge events

candidates.title: Post-merge lookup can overwrite a concurrent cancellation

candidates.title: A cancelled land entry can be overwritten after the metadata lookup

candidates.suggestion: Recheck the abort signal and current entry state after the lookup, and make the terminal transition conditional on the entry still being owned and in the expected state.
candidates.failure_scenario: A user cancels while the post-merge PR lookup is in flight; the lookup aborts, its error is caught, and the cancelled entry becomes landed.

candidates.title: A push in progress can be reported as the current head
candidates.detail: reviewableHead classifies an in-progress push as superseded even when the recorded SHA is still the old head. The new error labels that recorded SHA as the current head, although the push has not yet recorded its new SHA.
candidates.suggestion: Only label a SHA as the current head when it is known to be the newer observed head; otherwise report that the push is in progress and the new head is unavailable.
candidates.failure_scenario: A change-view request arrives while a conflict round is pushing a new commit, before the recorded head has advanced. The response identifies the old commit as the current head.

candidates.title: Backfilled merge metadata never reaches the merge feed event

findings.title: Missing merge metadata is never retried when polling is off
findings.detail: Once the queue marks a run merged, reconciliation only reads a saved poller snapshot and skips the GitHub client. If the queue's one metadata request fails, times out, or is interrupted by a restart, an installation with polling disabled has no later observation to fill the fields. The parent feed can therefore retain the null values this change is meant to fix.
findings.suggestion: Keep incomplete merge metadata eligible for a bounded, retryable GitHub observation, including after restart and when polling is disabled.
findings.failure_scenario: The merge succeeds, the metadata lookup times out, and the daemon restarts with GitHub polling disabled. Subsequent reconciliation passes leave mergedBy and mergedAt null indefinitely.

verification.evidence: src/land/queue.ts:624–626 records `this.landed(entry, run, sha, null)` before the metadata lookup and returns if no MERGED observation arrives. src/integrations/github-notifier.ts:159–168 handles already-merged runs using only `savedSnapshot(store.githubPrData(run.prUrl))`, then unconditionally `continue`s before the client fetch. src/integrations/index.ts:50–57 disables the poller when `githubPoll` is false, leaving no poller to refresh that saved observation.
verification.trigger: With polling disabled and no saved MERGED observation, a successful queue merge marks the runs merged with null metadata. The metadata lookup times out, then the daemon restarts. Subsequent reconciliation skips fetching these already-merged runs, leaving mergedBy and mergedAt null indefinitely.

findings.title: Successful lands no longer mark failed or cancelled runs as merged
findings.detail: The previous land path set merged on the run regardless of its status. The replacement calls resolveMergedRun, which only transitions succeeded, resolved, or needs_human runs. Land requests do not restrict the target run to those statuses, so a PR from a failed or cancelled run can land while its run remains unmerged and has no run.merged event.
findings.suggestion: Preserve the previous merged transition for other eligible run statuses while retaining their existing terminal state.
findings.failure_scenario: A failed run has a delivered PR and an approval; a land request succeeds, but resolveMergedRun returns false because the run status is failed.

verification.evidence: src/land/queue.ts:379-381 finishes the entry as "landed" and calls `this.store.resolveMergedRun(...)`. src/db/store.ts:1843 handles only `"resolved"` or `"succeeded"` directly; line 1851 passes `from: ["needs_human"]`. Line 1808 rejects other statuses: `if (!from || !(opts.from ?? ["needs_human", "failed"]).includes(from)) return null;`. Previously, landed unconditionally set `{ merged: true }`.
verification.trigger: An approved delivered PR belongs to an unmerged failed or cancelled run. Landing succeeds, but resolveMergedRun rejects its status, leaving merged=false despite the landed queue entry.

findings.title: Consumer-bearing reviews fail against an older daemon
findings.detail: The HTTP-backed MCP server forwards the new consumer property to the daemon. The previous daemon's strict ReviewVerdictSchema rejects that unknown property, so a newer CLI cannot submit an approval with consumer provenance to an older running daemon.
findings.suggestion: Encode the MCP identity in the existing reviewer field before forwarding, while respecting its validation limits, or otherwise provide a compatible payload for older daemons.
findings.failure_scenario: A newer MCP proxy calls limitless_review with consumer set while connected to a daemon from the base release; the daemon rejects the request as an unrecognized key.

verification.evidence: src/integrations/mcp.ts:343–346 forwards `...ReviewVerdictSchema.parse(input)` with `reviewer: "mcp"`; the current schema includes `consumer` (src/pipeline/review-round.ts:31). The HTTP backend forwards this unchanged: `review: (id, input) => api(`${path(id)}/review`, input)` (src/integrations/mcp.ts:279). At base 21f8de5, src/pipeline/review-round.ts:25–31 permits only `verdict`, `reviewedSha`, `findings`, and `reviewer`, followed by `.strict()`. Lines 154–156 reject failed parsing with `ReviewRefused(..., 400)`, returned as HTTP 400 by src/server/http.ts:535.
verification.trigger: A new MCP proxy submits limitless_review with consumer set to a daemon running the base release. The proxy includes consumer in the HTTP body; the older daemon rejects the unknown key with HTTP 400 instead of recording the review.

findings.title: A failed metadata lookup can permanently leave merge fields empty
findings.detail: The queue records the land before a single best-effort metadata lookup, then silently discards lookup errors, timeouts, and incomplete observations. Reconciliation skips already-merged runs unless a saved merged snapshot happens to exist, so installations without polling, or without a later usable snapshot, never recover the merger and timestamp.
findings.suggestion: Keep missing merge metadata eligible for bounded later reconciliation, while preserving the completed merge and avoiding another merge operation.
findings.failure_scenario: The PR merge succeeds, but the subsequent GitHub metadata request times out while polling is disabled. The queue reports the entry as landed, and both the parent and round run retain null mergedBy and mergedAt indefinitely.

verification.evidence: src/land/queue.ts:624-626 calls `this.landed(entry, run, sha, null)` before fetching metadata and returns when the observation is absent. Lines 644-646 convert lookup rejection or abort into null. src/integrations/github-notifier.ts:159-168 enriches already merged runs only from `savedSnapshot(store.githubPrData(run.prUrl))`, then continues without fetching.
verification.trigger: The merge succeeds, the metadata lookup times out, polling is disabled, and no saved MERGED snapshot exists. The entry remains landed while both runs retain null merge metadata indefinitely.

findings.title: The reported unpinned request cannot identify a changed head
findings.detail: A request with a nonzero file index and no SHA pins fails schema validation before the saved and recorded PR heads are compared. The resulting message asks for pagination pins even when the head has moved, so it does not give the requested new head for the original failure scenario. The MCP tool's schema validation can reject the request before getChange is called as well.
findings.suggestion: Allow the head state to be diagnosed before returning the missing-pins error, while retaining the pin requirement for actual further reads.
findings.failure_scenario: After a conflict round advances the recorded PR head, limitless_get_change called with {"run":"…","file":1} reports that pins are required instead of reporting the new head.

verification.evidence: src/integrations/mcp-change.ts:29 requires pins when file is nonzero: `((!q.filesOffset && !q.file && !q.diffOffset && !q.reportOffset) || (q.headSha && q.baseSha))`. Lines 383–390 return on validation failure before inspecting the recorded head. src/integrations/mcp.ts:529 reports `Further reads require headSha and baseSha from the first page.`
verification.trigger: After a conflict round advances the recorded head, request {run: "…", file: 1} without pins. Validation rejects it before head inspection, so the response omits the changed head and its SHA.

findings.title: The original change-view failure is asserted as a pagination error
findings.detail: The new test sends the same unpinned file request described in the issue but expects the missing-pins response. Its superseded-head cases supply SHA pins, so neither backend test checks that the original request after a conflict head move identifies the changed head and names its replacement. candidates.title: Merge feed items are published before their metadata is available
candidates.detail: A successful queue merge records and publishes `run.merged` with null metadata before fetching the merger and timestamp. The later database update changes the existing feed row without publishing a new feed item. A consumer that reads and acknowledges the original item during the metadata lookup will never receive the corrected fields.
candidates.suggestion: Make the authoritative merge metadata available before publishing the merge item, or publish a distinct correction that cursor-based consumers can observe.
candidates.failure_scenario: A feed consumer long-polls while a queue merge completes, receives and acknowledges the parent run's `run.merged` with null fields, and the subsequent metadata lookup succeeds.

candidates.title: A failed metadata lookup can leave merge fields null permanently
candidates.detail: After the queue records a merge, reconciliation only fills missing fields from an already saved merged snapshot and never asks its client for one. If the queue's one metadata request fails or is interrupted and polling is disabled, no later observation need be saved, so both the run and its merge feed item retain null fields indefinitely.
candidates.suggestion: Keep incomplete merge metadata eligible for a bounded reconciliation lookup, including when polling is disabled.
candidates.failure_scenario: The merge succeeds, the immediate GitHub metadata request times out or the daemon restarts, and the installation has polling disabled.

candidates.title: A failed metadata lookup can permanently leave merge fields empty
candidates.detail: The queue marks both runs merged before its single metadata lookup. If that lookup fails, times out, or returns an observation that has not yet changed to MERGED, it silently returns. Reconciliation skips further fetches for merged runs and only uses an already-saved merged snapshot, so installations without a subsequent poller observation can retain null merge fields indefinitely.
candidates.suggestion: Keep missing merge metadata eligible for bounded reconciliation after a failed or premature observation, including when polling is disabled.
candidates.failure_scenario: A successful queue merge is followed by a transient GitHub lookup failure while polling is disabled; both the parent and round run remain merged with null mergedBy and mergedAt.

candidates.title: Superseded response can label an unconfirmed SHA as the current head
candidates.detail: The superseded condition includes an in-progress push and disagreement between the saved observation and recorded head. In either case, recorded.sha has not been established as the current PR head, yet the new error labels it as such. The same issue exists in the final recheck when the observation and recorded head disagree.
candidates.suggestion: Only report a current head when it has been confirmed by a consistent observation; otherwise report that the head is changing or unavailable.
candidates.failure_scenario: A push is in progress while the recorded SHA is still the previous head. A change-view request reports that previous SHA as the current head.

candidates.title: Supersession can identify the old SHA as the current head
candidates.detail: When a push is in progress, reviewableHead reports superseded even if the recorded SHA is still the old head. The tests cover a recorded head that has already advanced but do not cover a push in progress before the new SHA is recorded.
candidates.suggestion: Only label a SHA as current when the observation establishes it; otherwise report that the head is changing. Add a test with pushing set and the recorded SHA still at the previous head.
candidates.failure_scenario: A change-view request arrives while a push is in progress, before the new head has been recorded. The refusal says the old SHA is the current head.

candidates.title: Redact consumer names before storing approval provenance

candidates.suggestion: Apply credential redaction to the consumer-derived reviewer before it reaches persistent storage and the feed.
candidates.failure_scenario: An MCP caller supplies a registered API token as its consumer name while approving a PR; the token is stored verbatim in review_approvals and the feed.

candidates.title: The reported unpinned change-view request still does not identify the failing part
candidates.detail: The request explicitly asks the change-view error to name “an unknown file index, a head that changed (give the new head), or a commit not available locally.” The exact reported call, with a run and file 1 but no SHA pins, is rejected by schema validation and returns only “Further reads require headSha and baseSha from the first page.” It never checks the current head or file index, so the requested diagnostic remains unavailable for that call.

candidates.failure_scenario: An agent calls limitless_get_change with {"run":"…","file":1} after a conflict round changes the PR head; it receives the pinning instruction without the new head or an unknown-index diagnosis.

candidates.title: Merge metadata can remain missing permanently after a failed post-merge read
candidates.detail: The request says to “fill them from the merge the queue recorded.” The queue marks both runs merged before its optional metadata lookup. findings.title: Repeated credential matches make patch filtering quadratic
findings.detail: Every occurrence scans every line range synchronously before paging. An untrusted large patch with many occurrences of a registered multiline value can therefore block the daemon's event loop for a prolonged period, and each page request repeats the work. A targeted invocation of the extracted function took 893 ms for 50,000 lines and 3,514 ms for 100,000 lines, consistent with quadratic growth.
findings.suggestion: Map match offsets to affected ranges using an ordered cursor or binary search, so work grows with the patch size and number of matching lines.
findings.failure_scenario: A changed file contains hundreds of thousands of repetitions of a two-line registered credential; requesting its change view monopolizes the daemon event loop for minutes.

verification.evidence: src/integrations/mcp-change.ts:74 iterates `for (const range of ranges)` for every occurrence found by the loop at lines 80–84. Filtering runs before paging (lines 617–629, 693). The Git output limit is 50,000,000 characters (src/util/proc.ts:603). In-memory measurements for 16k/32k/64k repetitions were 376/1505/6089 ms, demonstrating quadratic scaling.
verification.trigger: A file containing hundreds of thousands of repeated two-line credentials remains below the Git output limit. Each match scans every line synchronously, blocking the daemon event loop for potentially minutes.

findings.suggestion: Map clipped matches to every affected patch line, including additions and deletions, and cover credentials embedded within surrounding line text.

findings.title: A passing retry clears a security check failure
findings.detail: The retry classification treats every check alike: a successful full retry becomes non-blocking flaky, with no way to preserve a security check's failure. The request explicitly requires security failures never to become passes. A direct call to retryRegressions with a failing security-scan followed by a passing retry returned verdict "flaky" and blocking false.
findings.suggestion: Represent which checks are security checks and keep their initial failures blocking regardless of retry outcome.
findings.failure_scenario: A security scan reports a vulnerability on the first post-change run but exits successfully on its retry; the gate becomes non-blocking and the change can proceed.

verification.evidence: src/gates/run.ts:374-383 selects regressed checks without distinguishing security scans. At src/gates/run.ts:393-394: `verdict: confinementError ? "confinement_error" : retry.ok ? "flaky" : "regressed", blocking: confinementError || !retry.ok`. Only confinement failures are preserved, not vulnerability findings.
verification.trigger: A configured security scan passes on baseline, fails after the change without naming a changed-file location, then passes its full retry. It becomes flaky and nonblocking despite the original security failure.

findings.title: Bun's report can omit failed files entirely
findings.detail: Bun's JUnit reporter omits files that fail during module loading when another file has a normal test failure. The parser accepts the remaining report as a complete failure list, so the targeted retry runs even though not all failing files are known. A local Bun reproduction with one failed assertion and a second file throwing at module load produced a report containing only the assertion failure, and parseJUnit returned only that file.
findings.suggestion: Detect incomplete Bun reports, including runner-level or module-load errors, and fall back to the full retry when the complete failure list cannot be established.
findings.failure_scenario: A suite has a failing test in a.test.ts and an import-time exception in b.test.ts. Only a.test.ts is retried; if it fails, the full check is skipped despite b.test.ts being an unknown failing file.

verification.evidence: src/gates/junit.ts:85-88 visits only reported suites and accepts any valid nonempty file list: `else for (const suite of elements(root).filter((child) => child.name === "testsuite")) visit(suite);`. A Bun 1.4.3 reproduction with an assertion failure in a.test.ts and an import-time exception in b.test.ts produced a report containing only a.test.ts; parseJUnit returned that file. src/gates/run.ts:259-261 records a failing targeted attempt and executes `continue`, skipping the full retry.
verification.trigger: An assertion failure and an import-time exception occur in separate files. Bun omits the import-error file from JUnit; the parser accepts the remaining file. If its targeted retry fails, no full retry covers the omitted failure.

findings.title: An incomplete failure list is accepted as complete
findings.detail: A suite reporting multiple failures is accepted when only one failure has a file-bearing testcase. The parser does not reconcile the suite's failure and error counts with the represented failures, so it can choose a targeted retry when the remaining failing files are unknown. The command `bun -e 'import {parseJUnit} from "./src/gates/junit.ts"; console.log(JSON.stringify(parseJUnit(`<testsuite failures="2"><testcase file="test/gate-retry-files.test.ts"><failure/></testcase></testsuite>`, process.cwd())))'` returned `{"failedFiles":["test/gate-retry-files.test.ts"],"failedFileTimes":{}}`.
findings.suggestion: Reject reports whose declared failures cannot all be attributed to files, and fall back to the full retry.
findings.failure_scenario: A report declares two failures but identifies only one failing testcase; the known file is retried alone instead of falling back to the full check.

verification.evidence: src/gates/junit.ts:79-81 checks only whether declared failures/errors exceed zero: `else if (!caseFailed && !nested.length) throw new Error("Failing suite without files");`. It never compares declared counts with identified failures. A focused reproduction of `<testsuite failures="2"><testcase file="a.test.ts"><failure/></testcase></testsuite>` returned `failedFiles: ["a.test.ts"]`. src/gates/run.ts:241 uses that list for targeted retry.
verification.trigger: A suite without a file declares two failures but contains only one file-attributed failing testcase. caseFailed becomes true, so the incomplete list is accepted and only that file is retried.

findings.title: No test covers a partially reported failure list
findings.detail: The unknown-file cases cover an explicitly fileless failure, but not a suite whose failure count exceeds the represented file-bearing failures. Consequently the parser accepts an incomplete list without a test failing.
findings.suggestion: Add a report with two declared failures and only one identifiable failing testcase, and assert that it triggers exactly one full retry.
findings.failure_scenario: A structured report contains one known failure and another failure represented only by the suite count.

verification.evidence: test/gate-retry-files.test.ts:79 covers an explicit unknown testcase: `'<testsuite>${suite()}<testcase><error/></testcase></testsuite>'`, but no fixture covers a suite count exceeding its reported failures. src/gates/junit.ts:75 sets `caseFailed = true`; line 81 rejects only `!caseFailed && !nested.length`, so one known failure permits an incomplete list.
verification.trigger: A fileless suite declares failures="2" but contains only one failing testcase with a known file. The parser returns that file instead of treating the list as unknown; existing tests do not catch this missing full-retry fallback.

findings.title: Untrusted report timings can bypass the gate slot for a long retry
findings.detail: The decision to bypass the gate slot relies entirely on durations from the JUnit report, which the test process and code under review can write. A test can report a duration below 60 seconds while the selected file actually consumes substantial time or CPU. The targeted command retains the original check timeout, so it can run outside the gate slot for up to 1,800 seconds in this repository. This lets change-controlled data steer the shared-machine scheduling boundary.
findings.suggestion: Base the bypass decision on a trusted measurement that bounds the selected work, and enforce a corresponding runtime limit for an unslotted attempt; otherwise acquire a gate slot.
findings.failure_scenario: A failing test writes a JUnit report naming one existing file with time="1", then that file runs CPU-heavy work for many minutes on retry. The retry acquires agentTestSlots instead of the configured gate slot.

verification.evidence: src/gates/junit.ts:78 accepts report timing via `addTime(suiteFile, seconds(suite.attributes.time))`. src/gates/run.ts:242-246 derives `skipGateSlot` solely from file count and reported times totaling at most 60 seconds. src/gates/run.ts:200 uses `(options.skipGateSlot ? agentTestSlots : gateSlots).acquire(...)`; src/gates/run.ts:108 retains `(cmd.timeoutSec ?? 900) * 1000` as the execution timeout.
verification.trigger: An eligible failure supplies a valid report naming one existing file with time="1". That file performs many minutes of work on retry. The reported timing enables bypassing gateSlots, without checking measured earlier duration or bounding retry execution to 60 seconds.

findings.title: A failing suite with an unaccounted failure can be treated as complete

candidates.suggestion: Add a report with two declared failures and only one identifiable failing testcase, and assert that it triggers exactly one full retry.
candidates.failure_scenario: A structured report contains one known failure and another failure represented only by the suite count.

candidates.title: No retry test covers a failing security check
candidates.detail: The new retry matrix exercises ordinary gate failures and confinement errors, but does not verify the requested case where a security check fails and a subsequent attempt passes. The tests therefore would not catch a retry path that incorrectly clears a security failure.
candidates.suggestion: Add a focused test through the relevant security-check path asserting that the original failure remains blocking after a successful retry.
candidates.failure_scenario: A security check fails initially and a retry succeeds; an incorrect implementation turns that failure into a pass.

candidates.title: Untrusted report timings can bypass the gate slot for a long retry
candidates.detail: The decision to bypass the gate slot relies entirely on durations from the JUnit report, which the test process and code under review can write. A test can report a duration below 60 seconds while the selected file actually consumes substantial time or CPU. The targeted command retains the original check timeout, so it can run outside the gate slot for up to 1,800 seconds in this repository. This lets change-controlled data steer the shared-machine scheduling boundary.
candidates.suggestion: Base the bypass decision on a trusted measurement that bounds the selected work, and enforce a corresponding runtime limit for an unslotted attempt; otherwise acquire a gate slot.
candidates.failure_scenario: A failing test writes a JUnit report naming one existing file with time="1", then that file runs CPU-heavy work for many minutes on retry. The retry acquires agentTestSlots instead of the configured gate slot.

candidates.title: A failing suite with an unaccounted failure can be treated as complete
candidates.detail: A suite with a positive failure count, no file, and any nested suite is accepted even when its nested suite accounts for none of its failures. If another suite names a valid failing file, parsing returns that partial list instead of falling back to the full retry. I reproduced this with `bun -e 'import {parseJUnit} from "./src/gates/junit.ts"; console.log(JSON.stringify(parseJUnit(`<testsuites><testsuite file="test/gate-retry-files.test.ts" failures="1" time="1"/><testsuite failures="1"><testsuite tests="0"/></testsuite></testsuites>`, process.cwd())))'`, which returned `{"failedFiles":["test/gate-retry-files.test.ts"],"failedFileTimes":{"test/gate-retry-files.test.ts":1}}`.
candidates.suggestion: Verify that failing suite counts are accounted for by identifiable failing descendants, and return unknown when they are not.
candidates.failure_scenario: A report contains one identifiable failed file and a separate failing suite whose failure has no file and is not represented in its nested suite. Only the identifiable file is retried, despite the incomplete failure list.

candidates.title: A security check can become nonblocking after a retry passes
candidates.detail: The request says, "A security check's failure never becomes a pass." This path treats every successful full retry as flaky and nonblocking, with no distinction for security checks. A direct fake-runner check of a regressed check named security returned verdict "flaky" and blocking false after its retry passed.
candidates.suggestion: Represent security checks explicitly in trusted configuration and keep their original failure blocking when a retry passes.
candidates.failure_scenario: A security scan detects a vulnerability on its first post-change run but passes on retry; the gate becomes nonblocking.

candidates.title: Known failing files are not retried when output names a changed file
candidates.detail: The request says that a failure whose files are known gets a targeted retry. The existing pointsAt exclusion still skips retry selection when output contains a changed filename and line number, even when the structured report identified its failing files. This is a common form of test failure output.
candidates.suggestion: Apply the targeted retry rule to known failing files before applying the existing output-based exclusion.
candidates.failure_scenario: A test report identifies test/example.test.ts as failing and the output includes example.test.ts:12 for a changed file; no targeted retry runs.

candidates.title: Incomplete JUnit failure lists are accepted as complete
candidates.detail: The parser does not reconcile suite failure counts with the failures for which it found files. For example, parsing a suite with failures="2" and one failing testcase with a valid file returns that one file instead of falling back. A failing targeted retry then confirms the baseline or regression without checking the omitted failure.
candidates.suggestion: Reject reports whose declared failures or errors cannot be accounted for by file-attributed failures, and use the full retry.
candidates.failure_scenario: A report declares two failures but contains only one file-attributed failing testcase; the targeted retry runs only that file despite the failure list being incomplete.

findings.title: Pairing code does not authenticate the initial TLS connection
findings.detail: The initial connection accepts any certificate, and the displayed code is supplied by that connection. A man-in-the-middle can relay the pairing request to the real coordinator, return its code and secret to the worker, and present its own certificate. The owner sees the same code on both sides and approves it; the attacker then observes the claim and issued token. Pinning the attacker's certificate on subsequent requests does not prevent this. The submitted worker certificate fingerprint is never authenticated or used to bind the exchange.
findings.suggestion: Bind the owner-verified pairing code to both endpoints' certificate fingerprints and the pairing exchange, so relaying through a different TLS certificate changes the code or causes verification to fail.
findings.failure_scenario: An attacker intercepts the worker's first connection, proxies the real coordinator's pairing response, and forwards the approved claim while terminating both TLS connections.

verification.evidence: src/workers/client.ts:23-28 calls the initial workerRequest with only `{ signal }`; src/workers/tls.ts:103 sets `rejectUnauthorized: false`. src/workers/client.ts:39 then pins `first.fingerprint`. src/db/workers.ts:55 generates a random code, while :83-89 issues the token using only the pairing secret.
verification.trigger: An active interceptor terminates TLS and relays the real pairing code and secret. Owner approval authorizes the relayed request; the interceptor obtains the token and the worker pins the interceptor's certificate.

findings.title: Worker credentials are not denied to sandboxes in other processes
findings.detail: Private read protection is an in-memory registry. Pairing releases the token and fingerprint registrations on return, and `runWorker` registers them only in the worker CLI process. The coordinator TLS key has the same lifetime problem when its listener is disabled after the key has been created. Mode 0600 does not protect files from another process running as the same user.

findings.failure_scenario: Pair a worker, then run a factory daemon and a gate on the same machine; the daemon's sandbox is built without the worker token path registered, allowing a gate with access to that path to read the token.

verification.evidence: src/util/private-reads.ts:4 stores protection in `const privatePaths = new Map<string, number>()`; :30 returns only that process's keys. src/workers/client.ts:55-57 releases pairing protections. src/harness/read-policy.ts:190 builds denies from `credentials` and `privateReadPaths()`; :217 adds the home-wide deny only for gates.

A gate whose readable roots include the credential location, such as a configured toolchain directory, can read the token. findings.title: Interrupted certificate creation permanently blocks restart
findings.detail: Certificate generation creates the final key path before invoking OpenSSL. If generation fails, times out, or the process stops before both files are complete, the next start either rejects the incomplete pair or tries to parse invalid material. No cleanup or recovery occurs, so the worker listener or pairing command continues to fail on every subsequent start.
findings.suggestion: Generate both files under temporary names, validate them, and publish them only after successful generation; clean up incomplete temporary material on failure.
findings.failure_scenario: The daemon is stopped after creating the empty key file but before OpenSSL creates the certificate; every later listener start throws `Incomplete worker TLS material`.

verification.evidence: src/workers/tls.ts:18 creates the key before certificate generation: `writeFileSync(keyPath, "", { flag: "wx", mode: 0o600 });`. On restart, line 17 throws when only one file exists: `if (existsSync(keyPath) || existsSync(certPath)) throw new Error("Incomplete worker TLS material");`. Lines 45–47 only call `release()` and rethrow; they do not remove incomplete files.
verification.trigger: Interrupt initial TLS creation after key.pem is created but before cert.pem exists. Every subsequent listener start throws until the files are manually repaired; with workers enabled, this also aborts daemon startup (src/cli/daemon.ts:30,44–46).

findings.title: Pairing code does not authenticate the coordinator connection
findings.detail: The initial pairing request accepts any TLS certificate, and the worker pins the certificate observed on that connection. The displayed code comes from the coordinator but is not bound to that certificate or to an authenticated exchange. An intermediary can relay the pairing request and code unchanged, obtain the pairing secret and issued token, and leave the worker pinned to the intermediary's certificate even though the owner compared matching codes.
findings.suggestion: Bind the owner-verified pairing code to the coordinator certificate and pairing exchange so a relaying intermediary cannot obtain a usable token or substitute its certificate.
findings.failure_scenario: An attacker intercepts the worker's first connection, forwards the request to the real coordinator, and relays its code. The owner approves the matching code; the attacker claims the token and the worker pins the attacker's certificate.

verification.evidence: src/workers/client.ts:23-28 makes the initial request without a pin; :33 prints the returned code; :39 trusts `first.fingerprint`; :47 persists it. src/workers/tls.ts:103 uses `rejectUnauthorized: false`. src/db/workers.ts:83-89 returns the approved token based solely on the secret hash.
verification.trigger: An interceptor forwards pairing to the coordinator and relays its code. After the owner approves, the interceptor claims the token and relays it to the worker, which stores the interceptor's certificate fingerprint.

findings.title: Permanent TLS and configuration errors are retried silently forever
findings.detail: The heartbeat loop catches every request exception and retries without a deadline or diagnostic. This includes a changed coordinator fingerprint and malformed coordinator URL, neither of which can be repaired by retrying. The worker remains running but never sends another heartbeat, and the owner receives no explanation.
findings.suggestion: Retry only transient transport failures with a bounded policy; propagate permanent validation and certificate-pin failures with their original reason.
findings.failure_scenario: The coordinator certificate changes after pairing. Every heartbeat fails fingerprint validation, but the worker silently retries indefinitely instead of reporting that it must be paired again.

verification.evidence: src/workers/tls.ts:114-115 rejects with `"Coordinator certificate fingerprint changed"`. src/workers/client.ts:93 loops `for (;;)`, and :99-102 catches request errors and returns `undefined`; :106-107 sleeps and caps only the retry delay at 10 seconds.
verification.trigger: The coordinator certificate changes, or the coordinator URL is invalid. Each heartbeat throws a permanent error that is discarded, leaving the worker retrying indefinitely without reporting the required corrective action.

findings.title: Existing TLS key loses sandbox protection when the listener is disabled
findings.detail: The TLS key is registered with the sandbox deny list only when the listener starts. After a listener has created the key, restarting the daemon with workers.listen unset skips registration even though the key remains on disk. Agent sandboxes that can read that data directory can then read the coordinator's private key, contrary to the requirement that it be denied in every agent sandbox.
findings.suggestion: Register protection for existing worker TLS material independently of whether the listener is enabled, and retain it for the daemon lifetime.
findings.failure_scenario: Enable the listener once, then disable it and restart the daemon with the data directory outside the default home deny paths. A subsequent agent can read worker-tls/key.pem.

verification.evidence: src/server/workers.ts:15–16: `if (!listen) return undefined;` precedes `const tls = await certificate(join(paths.home, "worker-tls"));`. The key's protection is registered only inside that call: src/workers/tls.ts:12–14: `const keyPath = join(home, "key.pem")` and `const release = protectPrivateFile(keyPath);`. src/util/private-reads.ts:4 initializes a process-local `new Map<string, number>()`; src/harness/read-policy.ts:190 builds denials from `...credentials, ...privateReadPaths()`. No independent worker-key denial exists.

findings.title: Interrupted certificate generation prevents future startup
findings.detail: Certificate generation creates the final key path before running openssl, but its error path leaves partial files behind. A timeout, failed openssl invocation, or interruption can therefore leave only the empty key or other incomplete material. Every later start rejects the incomplete material, requiring manual cleanup.
findings.suggestion: Generate both files in temporary paths and publish them only after successful generation, cleaning up partial temporary files on failure.
findings.failure_scenario: The daemon is interrupted after creating key.pem but before openssl writes cert.pem. Subsequent starts fail with `Incomplete worker TLS material`.

verification.evidence: src/workers/tls.ts:18 writes an empty key.pem before awaiting OpenSSL at line 19. Line 17 rejects the resulting key-only state with `throw new Error("Incomplete worker TLS material")`; the catch at lines 45–47 performs no filesystem cleanup.
verification.trigger: Stop certificate generation between creation of key.pem and cert.pem. Subsequent starts repeatedly reject the persisted incomplete state, preventing listener and configured daemon startup.

findings.title: Credential read protection ends with the pairing process
findings.detail: The worker token and coordinator fingerprint are registered in an in-memory deny list only while `pairWorker` or `runWorker` holds them. findings.failure_scenario: Pair a worker, exit the pairing command, and run an agent through a separate daemon using the same data directory: that daemon's private-file deny list does not contain the stored worker token or coordinator fingerprint.

verification.evidence: src/workers/client.ts:47-48 registers the credential files, then :55-57 invokes all release callbacks. src/util/private-reads.ts:4 uses a process-local Map and :21 deletes released entries. src/harness/read-policy.ts:150-161 lists built-in credential directories without the worker data directory; :190 adds only currently registered private paths.

findings.failure_scenario: A paired worker sends a coordinator credential or private string in `osVersion`; the value is written verbatim to the workers table.
