A separately running daemon on the same machine does not receive those registrations when it constructs Claude or Codex sandbox policies, so its agents can read the persistent worker token and coordinator fingerprint. Mode 0600 does not protect them from agents running as the same user.
candidates.suggestion: Register the persistent worker credential paths in every daemon process that launches agents, including when the worker is stopped, and cover separate-process sandbox behavior.
candidates.failure_scenario: A machine runs both a worker and a factory daemon under the same user. An agent launched by the daemon reads `<data>/worker/token` and impersonates that worker.

candidates.title: Disabling the listener leaves its existing TLS key unprotected from agents
candidates.detail: The TLS key is added to the process-local private-read registry only when the listener is enabled. After an owner removes `workers.listen` and restarts the daemon, the existing key remains on disk but is no longer included in agent sandbox deny paths. An agent running as the same user can read it, compromising the certificate trusted by already paired workers if the listener is later re-enabled.
candidates.suggestion: Register the persistent TLS key path independently of whether the listener is currently enabled, or securely remove and rotate the material when disabling it.
candidates.failure_scenario: A coordinator previously enabled workers, then starts with the listener disabled. A tool-enabled agent reads `<data>/worker-tls/key.pem` before the listener is enabled again.

candidates.title: Store untrusted heartbeat fields only after redaction
candidates.detail: Heartbeat capabilities are serialized directly into SQLite. Several worker-controlled strings can contain coordinator credentials or private strings, but sanitization occurs only when listing workers. This leaves the unredacted values in persistent storage even though the trust-boundary rules require redaction before storage.
candidates.suggestion: Redact and apply private-string policy to worker-supplied capability fields before persisting them, while preserving the fields needed for version matching.
candidates.failure_scenario: A paired worker sends a coordinator credential or private string in `osVersion`; the value is written verbatim to the workers table.

candidates.title: Worker credentials are not denied in the daemon's agent sandboxes
candidates.detail: The request requires the worker token and coordinator fingerprint to be read-denied to gates. The deny registry is process-local, but pairing and the worker loop run as separate CLI processes from the daemon. Their registrations are also released when those commands exit. A daemon on the same machine therefore does not add these files to its agent sandbox deny lists; mode 0600 does not protect them from agents running as the same user.
candidates.suggestion: Register the persistent worker credential paths in every daemon process that can launch agents and gates, including when the worker command is not running.
candidates.failure_scenario: A machine is both a paired worker and a coordinator. An agent launched by its daemon reads the token under the worker data directory and uses it to impersonate the worker.

candidates.title: Disabling the listener removes protection for an existing TLS key
candidates.detail: The request says the TLS key is read-denied in every agent sandbox. When the listener is disabled, startup returns before registering the previously generated key with the process-local deny registry. The key remains on disk, and editor sandboxes do not otherwise deny the worker TLS directory.
candidates.suggestion: Register the existing key path for the daemon lifetime independently of whether the listener is enabled.
candidates.failure_scenario: An owner disables workers after having enabled them, then starts a run. An editor agent can read the retained coordinator TLS private key.

candidates.title: Interrupted certificate generation permanently blocks listener startup
candidates.detail: The key file is created before openssl runs, but a failed or interrupted generation leaves it behind. The next start sees incomplete TLS material and throws instead of generating a certificate, so a transient failure prevents the daemon from starting whenever the worker listener is configured.
candidates.suggestion: Generate the certificate and key in temporary files and publish them together, cleaning up incomplete generation safely.
candidates.failure_scenario: The daemon is stopped or openssl fails after the empty key file is created but before the certificate is written; every subsequent daemon start fails with "Incomplete worker TLS material".

candidates.title: A changed pinned certificate is retried indefinitely without an explanation
candidates.detail: The request requires the coordinator fingerprint to be pinned. Although the transport detects a mismatch, the heartbeat loop catches that error along with transient connection failures and retries forever. The operator receives no indication that the certificate changed and that intervention is required.
candidates.suggestion: Surface fingerprint mismatch as a terminal error while retaining retries for transient transport failures.
candidates.failure_scenario: The coordinator certificate changes after pairing. The worker remains running but never sends another heartbeat and never reports the pin mismatch.

findings.title: Initial pairing permits a relay to steal the worker token
findings.detail: The first connection accepts any TLS certificate and receives both the comparison code and the claim secret. An attacker between the worker and coordinator can relay the initial request and response, so the owner and worker see matching codes, while the attacker learns the secret and can claim the approved token. Pinning the attacker's certificate for subsequent requests does not prevent this.
findings.suggestion: Bind the owner-verified pairing code to the coordinator certificate and the claim secret, or use an authenticated pairing exchange that does not expose the claim credential to an unverified intermediary.
findings.failure_scenario: A network attacker proxies the initial pairing exchange, forwards the genuine code to the worker, and claims the token after the owner approves that code.

verification.evidence: src/workers/client.ts:23-28 sends the initial pairing request with only `{ signal }`, without a pin. src/workers/tls.ts:103 sets `rejectUnauthorized: false`; lines 114-115 compare fingerprints only when `options.pin !== undefined`. src/db/workers.ts:83-89 returns the approved token based solely on the pairing secret: `return w.state === "approved" ? { token: this.issued(w) } : { pending: true };`.
verification.trigger: An attacker terminates the initial TLS connection, relays pairing to the genuine coordinator, and forwards its code. The attacker learns the returned secret and can claim the worker token after owner approval; the worker instead pins the attacker's certificate.

findings.title: Worker credentials are not denied to sandboxes in other processes
findings.detail: The token and fingerprint are registered in an in-memory private-path map only in the pairing or worker CLI process, and pairing releases those registrations before exiting. A daemon running on the same machine has a separate map and does not register these persisted files when constructing its agent sandboxes. Thus an agent reader in that daemon can read the worker token and fingerprint; file mode 0600 does not protect against another process running as the same user.
findings.suggestion: Register the persisted worker credential paths in every process that creates agent sandboxes, including when the worker command is not running.
findings.failure_scenario: A machine runs both a paired worker and a Limitless daemon; an agent launched by the daemon reads the worker token from the data directory and impersonates the worker.

verification.evidence: src/util/private-reads.ts:4 stores protection in a process-local `const privatePaths = new Map<string, number>()`. src/workers/tls.ts:52 registers files using `protectPrivateFile(path)`. src/harness/read-policy.ts:190 builds sandbox denials from `[...credentials, ...privateReadPaths()]`; the built-in credential list at lines 150-161 omits `.limitless/worker`. src/cli/daemon.ts:15-32 registers the API credential and coordinator listener, but no worker credentials.
verification.trigger: A paired worker and a separate daemon run as the same user with default sandbox settings. The daemon's process has no worker-file registrations, so an editor agent can read the mode-0600 worker token and impersonate that worker.

findings.title: Interrupted certificate generation permanently blocks listener startup
findings.detail: The key file is created before the asynchronous OpenSSL command completes. If generation fails or the process stops before the certificate is written, the next startup encounters the incomplete pair and always throws. Normal restarts cannot recover without manually deleting the leftover material.
findings.suggestion: Generate both files under temporary names and publish them only after successful generation, or safely clean up an incomplete first-generation attempt.
findings.failure_scenario: The daemon is interrupted after creating key.pem but before OpenSSL writes cert.pem; every subsequent worker-listener startup fails with `Incomplete worker TLS material`.

verification.evidence: src/workers/tls.ts:18 creates key.pem before awaiting OpenSSL: `writeFileSync(keyPath, "", { flag: "wx", mode: 0o600 });`. On restart, src/workers/tls.ts:17 throws when only one file exists: `if (existsSync(keyPath) || existsSync(certPath)) throw new Error("Incomplete worker TLS material");`. The catch at lines 45–47 only calls `release()` and rethrows; it removes no files. src/server/workers.ts:16 awaits certificate generation, and src/cli/daemon.ts:30 awaits the listener before starting the owner API.
verification.trigger: With the worker listener enabled, interrupt initial generation after key.pem is created but before cert.pem exists. Every subsequent daemon startup fails with `Incomplete worker TLS material` until the files are manually repaired or removed.

findings.title: Certificate replacement prevents the documented re-pairing flow
findings.detail: The guide says a worker must pair again after the coordinator certificate changes, but an approved worker's existing name is always rejected by the pairing route. Re-running the documented pairing command with the default name therefore cannot recover unless the owner first revokes the existing record or chooses another name.
findings.suggestion: Support an explicit secure re-pairing flow for an existing worker, or document the required revocation before re-pairing.
findings.failure_scenario: The coordinator certificate changes and an existing worker runs `limitless worker pair` with its original name; the coordinator rejects the request as already paired.

verification.evidence: docs/GUIDE.md:236 says "Changing the coordinator's certificate requires pairing again." However, src/db/workers.ts:44–46 rejects an existing worker when `existing.state === "approved"`, throwing "Worker name already paired or pending". src/workers/client.ts:23–29 starts re-pairing with `/worker/pair` and throws `Pairing refused (${first.status})` on rejection.
verification.trigger: Replace the coordinator certificate while retaining its workers database, then pair an approved worker using its original name. Pairing is refused; the owner must first revoke the worker or choose another name.

findings.title: Pairing code does not authenticate the coordinator connection
findings.detail: The first request accepts any TLS certificate, and the worker pins the certificate observed on that connection. An active intermediary can forward the pairing request to the real coordinator, relay the same code to the worker, and use the observed pairing secret to claim the approved token. Comparing the displayed codes does not detect the intermediary because the code is not bound to the TLS connection.
findings.suggestion: Bind the owner-verified pairing code to the coordinator certificate or otherwise authenticate the coordinator before sending the pairing secret.
findings.failure_scenario: An attacker intercepts the initial pairing connection, relays the request and code to the real coordinator, and claims the worker token after the owner approves the matching code.

verification.evidence: src/workers/client.ts:23-33 requests pairing without a pin and prints the returned code; line 39 subsequently uses `{ pin: first.fingerprint, signal }`. src/workers/tls.ts:103 uses `rejectUnauthorized: false`. src/db/workers.ts:85-89 looks up `pairing_secret_hash` and returns the approved token without verifying possession of the worker certificate.
verification.trigger: An interceptor relays the genuine pairing request and code while presenting its own TLS certificate to the worker. Matching codes do not authenticate that connection; the interceptor knows the pairing secret and can retrieve the approved token.

findings.title: Credential read protection ends when pairing exits
findings.detail: The private-file deny registry is process-local, and pairing releases both credential paths before exiting. A separate daemon on the worker machine therefore does not register those files in its agent sandbox deny rules; running the worker in another process does not share its registrations either. The same lifecycle problem affects an existing coordinator TLS key when its listener is disabled.
findings.suggestion: Register the persistent worker credential and TLS key paths in every process that launches agent sandboxes, independently of whether the worker listener or client is running.
findings.failure_scenario: A machine is paired, the pairing command exits, and an agent launched by a separate local daemon reads the worker token from the data directory.

verification.evidence: src/workers/client.ts:47-48 saves the fingerprint and token with private-file registrations, then lines 55-57 execute `cert.release(); for (const release of held) release();`. src/util/private-reads.ts:19-21 removes released paths with `else privatePaths.delete(p)`. The registry itself is process-local (line 4), and src/harness/read-policy.ts:150-190 contains no built-in worker credential paths.
verification.trigger: Pairing succeeds and exits, leaving the credential files on disk without persistent sandbox protection. A separate daemon's editor agent can read the token under the default policy.

findings.title: Permanent TLS and configuration failures retry forever
findings.detail: The catch treats every request error as transient and retries indefinitely without logging the original error. A changed certificate fingerprint, malformed coordinator URL, or invalid stored pin therefore leaves the worker silently looping instead of reporting the failure and requiring corrective action.
findings.suggestion: Retry only transient transport errors with an appropriate bound, and propagate certificate, pin and configuration errors with their original cause.
findings.failure_scenario: The coordinator certificate changes after pairing; every heartbeat fails fingerprint verification, but the worker remains running indefinitely with no diagnostic.

verification.evidence: src/workers/tls.ts:114-115 rejects a changed certificate with `new Error("Coordinator certificate fingerprint changed")`. src/workers/client.ts:93-107 runs `for (;;)`, catches request errors with `.catch(() => { signal.throwIfAborted(); return undefined; })`, then sleeps and retries with delay capped at 10 seconds. Only returned HTTP statuses below 500 terminate the retry.
verification.trigger: The coordinator certificate changes, or the configured origin is permanently invalid. Every heartbeat request throws, but the worker discards the error and retries indefinitely without a diagnostic until externally aborted.

findings.title: Interrupted certificate generation prevents future startup
findings.detail: Certificate generation creates the key path before invoking OpenSSL, but failures leave generated or partial files in place. The next start either rejects the incomplete pair or reads invalid material, so a transient interruption permanently blocks the worker listener until the files are manually removed.
findings.suggestion: Generate both files in temporary paths, clean them up on failure, and publish the completed pair only after validation.
findings.failure_scenario: OpenSSL times out or the process stops after creating key.pem but before writing cert.pem; subsequent daemon starts fail with `Incomplete worker TLS material`.

verification.evidence: src/workers/tls.ts:18 creates key.pem before invoking OpenSSL, whose timeout is configured at line 38: `{ cwd: home, env: agentEnv(), timeoutMs: 30_000 }`. Lines 45–47 only release protection and rethrow on failure. A later invocation encounters the explicit rejection at line 17: `if (existsSync(keyPath) || existsSync(certPath)) throw new Error("Incomplete worker TLS material");`. src/server/workers.ts:16 and src/cli/daemon.ts:30 propagate this failure through daemon startup.
verification.trigger: OpenSSL fails or times out, or generation is interrupted, leaving key.pem present and cert.pem absent. Subsequent starts with the worker listener enabled consistently fail instead of recovering. This is the same defect as C3.

findings.title: Worker credentials lose sandbox protection when pairing exits
findings.detail: Protection is held in a process-local registry and released when pairing finishes. A separate daemon or agent process does not inherit that registration, even though the token and coordinator fingerprint remain on disk. The real-Seatbelt test explicitly registers synthetic files in the same process that launches the gates, so it does not exercise this lifecycle or cross-process case.
findings.suggestion: Register the persistent worker credential paths in every process that constructs an agent sandbox, and test access from a separately started process after pairing has finished.
findings.failure_scenario: A machine pairs a worker, the pairing command exits, and a separate local factory process launches an agent sandbox that can otherwise reach the worker data directory; the persisted token and fingerprint are absent from that process's private-read registry.

verification.evidence: src/workers/client.ts:47-48 saves credentials through `privateFile(...)`; src/workers/client.ts:55-57 then executes `for (const release of held) release()`. src/util/private-reads.ts:4 defines the process-local `const privatePaths = new Map<string, number>()`; line 21 removes released entries with `privatePaths.delete(p)`.
verification.trigger: Pairing completes and exits; a separate factory process launches a sandbox that otherwise permits reading the worker directory. The persisted token and fingerprint have no deny registrations in that process and can be read.

findings.title: No test covers claiming an approved pairing after coordinator restart
findings.detail: The implementation reconstructs an issued token from the persistent TLS key so that a worker can claim it after a restart, but the pairing tests approve and claim within one listener lifetime. A regression in key reuse or token reconstruction would leave an approved worker unable to pair without being caught.
findings.suggestion: Approve a pending request, restart the listener and store, then claim with the original secret and verify that the returned token authenticates a heartbeat.
findings.failure_scenario: The coordinator restarts after the owner approves a pending request but before the worker claims its token.

verification.evidence: test/workers.test.ts:67–68 calls `workers.approve(pending.code)` immediately followed by `/worker/pair/claim`, without restarting. The explicit pairing test does the same at lines 84–85. The listener restart at test/workers.test.ts:123–126 only asserts `expect((await listen()).tls.fingerprint).toBe(fingerprint)`. Thus no test exercises the restart reconstruction in src/db/workers.ts:66: `createHmac("sha256", this.pairingKey).update(w.pairing_secret_hash).digest("hex")`.
verification.trigger: Coordinator restarts after approval and before token claim: token reconstruction and subsequent authentication are untested. This confirms a coverage gap, not a demonstrated runtime failure.

findings.title: Pairing code does not authenticate the coordinator certificate
findings.detail: The initial pairing request accepts any TLS certificate, and the coordinator generates a random code that is unrelated to either endpoint's certificate. A man-in-the-middle can relay the pairing request and response unchanged, present its own certificate to the worker, and relay the subsequent claim. findings.title: Pairing expiration depends on synchronized worker and coordinator clocks

Reviewed the lease, validation, restart, and worker execution paths. Targeted tests could not start: test/workers.test.ts lacked @simplewebauthn/server, and test/gate-executor.test.ts loaded an incompatible Zod version without number().overwrite.

Reviewed the worker protocol and its tests. Targeted tests could not run: the environment lacks @simplewebauthn/server and resolves an incompatible Zod version. Found two coverage gaps in privacy and bundle handling.

The targeted command `bun test test/gate-executor.test.ts test/workers.test.ts` could not run: this checkout lacks `@simplewebauthn/server` and has an incompatible Zod installation (`z.number().overwrite is not a function`).

Verifier: 10 candidates, 10 checked, 1 refuted.

findings.title: Treat a worker confinement failure as a terminal failure
findings.detail: A check reporting a confinement failure is rejected as an invalid result, which calls workers.fail. After the retry is exhausted, the LAN executor runs the gates locally and can return a pass. This converts a failed security check into a successful gate result.
findings.suggestion: Preserve confinement failures as a distinct terminal failure and propagate them through the gate result without retrying them into a pass.
findings.failure_scenario: Both worker attempts report a Seatbelt launch failure, but the local fallback executes successfully; the overall gate is reported as passing.

verification.evidence: src/workers/protocol.ts:65 rejects confinement failures: `.refine((r) => !r.confinementError && !launchFailure(r.output), "Worker confinement failed")`. src/server/workers.ts:131 handles that rejection with `workers.fail(id, ...)`. src/db/workers.ts:260 transitions using `j.attempt < 2 ? "queued" : "failed"`. src/gates/lan.ts:72 handles `job.state === "failed"` by running locally, then at lines 88–89 calls `workers.complete(handle.id, run, true); return workers.sanitize(run);`, preserving no terminal confinement failure.
verification.trigger: Two worker attempts report confinement launch failures; both become retryable infrastructure failures. A successful local fallback supplies the final passing GateRun, erasing the confinement failure from the verdict.

findings.title: Do not discard failed checks received before an infrastructure failure
findings.detail: Check events from a worker are persisted and forwarded, but the final result is replaced by the next attempt or local fallback if that worker disconnects before posting its GateRun. A later pass therefore erases an already observed failing check, contrary to the requirement that infrastructure retries never turn a failing check into a pass.
findings.suggestion: Preserve and account for validated failing check results across attempts when producing the final gate outcome.
findings.failure_scenario: A worker posts a failing test check and loses its connection before posting the final result; the retry or local fallback passes, so the run receives a passing GateRun.

verification.evidence: src/gates/lan.ts:68–72 copies stored events into the event stream, then returns the final result directly: `if (job.state === "done" && job.result) return JSON.parse(job.result) as GateRun;`. The local fallback likewise returns only its new result at src/gates/lan.ts:86–89: `workers.complete(handle.id, run, true); return workers.sanitize(run);`. Neither path incorporates previously failed checks. src/gates/executor.ts:210–215 forwards check events to hooks but returns `execution.result` unchanged.
verification.trigger: A worker posts a valid failing check event, then disconnects before completing its GateRun. A replacement worker or local fallback passes the check. The returned GateRun reports passing despite the recorded failure, violating the requirement that infrastructure retries never turn a failing check into a pass.

findings.title: Do not retry certificate pin failures indefinitely
findings.detail: The catch treats every workerRequest exception as a transient connection error. That includes an invalid coordinator URL or a changed pinned TLS fingerprint, so the worker silently retries forever instead of surfacing the security or configuration failure. The retry has no deadline.
findings.suggestion: Classify request errors and propagate certificate validation and configuration failures; bound retries for transient transport errors.
findings.failure_scenario: The coordinator presents a certificate whose fingerprint differs from the stored pin. The worker stays running and retries indefinitely without reporting the fingerprint mismatch.

verification.evidence: src/workers/tls.ts:114-115 rejects a mismatched pin with `reject(new Error("Coordinator certificate fingerprint changed"))`. src/workers/client.ts:146-148 discards that exception with `.catch(() => { requestSignal.throwIfAborted(); return undefined; })`. The enclosing `for (;;)` at :139 then sleeps and retries at :157-158, capping only the delay.
verification.trigger: The coordinator consistently presents a different certificate while the worker's abort signal remains active → the worker silently retries indefinitely without reporting the fingerprint mismatch.

findings.title: The credential test does not establish worker-side redaction
findings.detail: The worker and coordinator run in the same process and share the credential registry. The test registers the secret globally and checks only the stored coordinator result and events, so coordinator-side sanitization can make it pass even if the worker sends the credential in plaintext.
findings.suggestion: Inspect the outgoing worker event and result bodies before coordinator processing, or run the worker in a separate process with a credential unknown to the coordinator.
findings.failure_scenario: Worker-side redaction is removed and a gate prints a worker-only credential; the shared coordinator registry still redacts the stored output, so this test passes while the credential crosses the connection.

verification.evidence: test/workers.test.ts:659 registers the secret with `registerCredential("WORKER_OUTPUT_TEST", secret)`, while assertions at :681–683 inspect only stored `result` and `events`. Coordinator storage independently sanitizes both: src/db/workers.ts:238 uses `events.push(this.sanitize(event))`, :291 stores `JSON.stringify(this.sanitize(run))`, and :59 calls `redactGateData(data)`. No assertion inspects the outbound worker payload.
verification.trigger: Worker-side redaction regresses and sends a plaintext credential. Because this in-process test registers the credential in the coordinator's shared registry and checks only sanitized storage, it can still pass despite disclosure over the connection.

findings.title: The bundle test never exercises distinct head and base commits
findings.detail: The shared request fixture assigns the same commit to headSha and baseSha. Consequently, the end-to-end bundle test cannot detect an implementation that bundles only the head, even though the request requires both commits to be available on the worker.
findings.suggestion: Create distinct base and head commits and have a worker gate verify that both requested commits are present.
findings.failure_scenario: Bundle creation omits baseSha when it differs from headSha; the existing end-to-end test still passes because its two SHAs are identical.

verification.evidence: test/workers.test.ts:123–124 sets `baseSha: sha, headSha: sha`; the bundle end-to-end test at :657 uses `request(true)`. Production bundle creation at src/server/workers.ts:88 uses `[...new Set([request.headSha, request.baseSha].filter(Boolean))]`, so this fixture exercises only one distinct commit.
verification.trigger: Bundle creation regresses to omit a distinct base commit. The existing end-to-end fixture still passes because its base and head are identical, leaving the distinct-base requirement untested.

findings.title: Reconcile streamed check failures with the final result
findings.detail: The coordinator validates each check event and the final GateRun independently. It accepts a passing final result even if the same lease previously reported that check as failed. The failed event is stored, but it does not influence the returned GateRun, so an inconsistent worker response can turn an observed failure into a pass.
findings.suggestion: Validate the final run against the check events recorded for the current lease and treat inconsistent results as an infrastructure failure.
findings.failure_scenario: A worker posts a valid failed event for a requested check, then posts a valid GateRun reporting that same check as passed; the coordinator completes the job with the passing result.

verification.evidence: src/server/workers.ts:123–130 validates events and final runs independently through `validCheck(...)` and `validRun(...)`. At lines 136–137 it executes `workers.event(id, event.data)` or `workers.complete(id, result.data.run)`. src/db/workers.ts:237–239 only appends events; lines 288–291 store the final result without consulting them. src/gates/executor.ts:214–215 returns the final result: `const [result] = await Promise.all([execution.result, events]); return result;`.
verification.trigger: A leased worker submits a schema-valid failed check event, then a schema-valid passing final result for the same requested check and SHA. The coordinator accepts the final result and completes the job as passing despite its recorded failure.

findings.title: Coordinator-only credentials can be truncated before redaction
findings.detail: runLocalGates truncates output on the worker after redacting only credentials registered on that worker. The coordinator subsequently redacts the already-truncated value using its own credentials. If the tail boundary cuts through a coordinator credential that the worker does not know, the coordinator sees only a fragment and literal credential redaction cannot remove it before the event or result is stored.
findings.suggestion: Ensure coordinator-only credentials cannot be cut before coordinator-side redaction, such as by sending bounded raw output with enough overlap for coordinator redaction before applying the final output limit.
findings.failure_scenario: A gate prints a coordinator credential unknown to the worker, followed by enough output that the 6,000-character tail starts in the middle of that credential. The credential suffix is sent to and stored by the coordinator.

verification.evidence: src/gates/run.ts:74 sets `OUTPUT_TAIL = 6_000`; :114 redacts using worker credentials, then :126 stores `combined.slice(-OUTPUT_TAIL)`. src/workers/client.ts:233 sends that already-truncated run. Coordinator sanitization at src/db/workers.ts:58-60 applies `redactGateData(data)` and `privateOutputData(...)`; src/util/proc.ts:684 replaces complete secret literals using `text.split(secret).join("[redacted]")`. src/util/private-output.ts:23 calls `privacy(field)` without enabling truncated matching.
verification.trigger: A gate prints a credential registered only on the coordinator, followed by output positioning the tail boundary inside that credential → the worker sends a credential suffix, and coordinator sanitization cannot match the complete secret, so the suffix is stored.

findings.title: A failed check from a lost lease can become a pass
findings.detail: The request says infrastructure retries must “never turn a failing check into a pass.” Check events from an attempt are streamed to hooks, but after that attempt loses its lease the final verdict uses only the later worker's GateRun. A failed check already reported by the first worker is therefore discarded for verdict purposes.
findings.suggestion: Retain completed check failures across infrastructure attempts and ensure a later passing result cannot erase them.
findings.failure_scenario: A worker posts a failing check event, disconnects before posting its GateRun, and the replacement worker reports that check as passing. The returned GateRun marks it as passing.

verification.evidence: src/db/workers.ts:275–277 calls `this.fail(j.id, "Worker disconnected")` or fails an expired lease. src/db/workers.ts:257–260 requeues the first failed attempt with `j.attempt < 2 ? "queued" : "failed"`. The replacement result is stored directly by src/server/workers.ts:136: `workers.complete(id, result.data.run)`, and returned directly by src/gates/lan.ts:72: `return JSON.parse(job.result) as GateRun;`. Earlier check events are streamed at lines 68–70 but never merged into that result.
verification.trigger: The first worker posts a failing check and loses its lease before submitting its GateRun. A second worker leases the requeued job and submits a passing result. The executor returns the second worker’s passing check without preserving the first failure.

findings.title: Restart discards leased retry and timeout jobs
findings.detail: The request says `attach` waits for the stored result so “a coordinator restart re-attaches without enqueueing again.” Resume is restricted to baseline, initial and rebase purposes. A persisted timeout or retry job is cancelled and replaced when its stage resumes, even if the worker is still running or has completed it.
findings.suggestion: Provide durable resume handling for every LAN gate execution purpose, preserving the original job identity and any state needed to consume its result.
findings.failure_scenario: The daemon restarts while a LAN timeout rerun or regression retry is leased. On resume the pending handle fails the purpose whitelist, is cancelled, and a new job is enqueued.

verification.evidence: src/pipeline/gate-execution.ts:29–37 requires matching purpose and `["baseline", "initial", "rebase"].includes(purpose)` to reuse a handle; otherwise it calls `await cancelGateExecution(pending.handle, ctx.deps.gateExecutor)`. src/pipeline/engine.ts:1215 restarts the gates stage with purpose `"initial"`, while :1237 and :1265 create `"timeout"` and `"regression-retry"` jobs. src/gates/executor.ts:60 calls `executor.discard?.(handle)` for a detached handle; src/gates/lan.ts:23–24 implements discard with `workers.cancel(handle.id)`. src/gates/executor.ts:188 starts a new execution when no stored handle survives.
verification.trigger: Restart the daemon while a LAN timeout rerun or regression retry is leased. Its durable handle survives shutdown, but the resumed stage starts with purpose "initial", rejects and cancels the pending retry handle, then enqueues a new job instead of reattaching.

candidates.title: Verify the worker checkout SHA after gates run
candidates.detail: The worker records HEAD before running gate commands and posts that saved SHA with the result. Gate commands can change the worker checkout's HEAD. The coordinator checks its own untouched checkout after the remote execution, so it cannot detect this change and can record passing gate evidence for the requested commit even though a gate ran against another commit.
candidates.suggestion: Re-read HEAD after all gates complete and reject the job as an infrastructure failure if it differs from the requested head; add a test in which a gate changes HEAD.
candidates.failure_scenario: A requested gate checks out an earlier commit containing passing tests and then runs those tests. The worker posts the original pre-gate SHA, and the coordinator accepts the passing result for the requested head.

candidates.title: Treat a worker confinement failure as a terminal failure
candidates.detail: A check reporting a confinement failure is rejected as an invalid result, which calls workers.fail. After the retry is exhausted, the LAN executor runs the gates locally and can return a pass. This converts a failed security check into a successful gate result.
candidates.suggestion: Preserve confinement failures as a distinct terminal failure and propagate them through the gate result without retrying them into a pass.
candidates.failure_scenario: Both worker attempts report a Seatbelt launch failure, but the local fallback executes successfully; the overall gate is reported as passing.

candidates.title: Do not discard failed checks received before an infrastructure failure
candidates.detail: Check events from a worker are persisted and forwarded, but the final result is replaced by the next attempt or local fallback if that worker disconnects before posting its GateRun. A later pass therefore erases an already observed failing check, contrary to the requirement that infrastructure retries never turn a failing check into a pass.
candidates.suggestion: Preserve and account for validated failing check results across attempts when producing the final gate outcome.
candidates.failure_scenario: A worker posts a failing test check and loses its connection before posting the final result; the retry or local fallback passes, so the run receives a passing GateRun.

candidates.title: Do not retry certificate pin failures indefinitely
candidates.detail: The catch treats every workerRequest exception as a transient connection error. That includes an invalid coordinator URL or a changed pinned TLS fingerprint, so the worker silently retries forever instead of surfacing the security or configuration failure. The retry has no deadline.
candidates.suggestion: Classify request errors and propagate certificate validation and configuration failures; bound retries for transient transport errors.
candidates.failure_scenario: The coordinator presents a certificate whose fingerprint differs from the stored pin. The worker stays running and retries indefinitely without reporting the fingerprint mismatch.

candidates.title: The credential test does not establish worker-side redaction
candidates.detail: The worker and coordinator run in the same process and share the credential registry. The test registers the secret globally and checks only the stored coordinator result and events, so coordinator-side sanitization can make it pass even if the worker sends the credential in plaintext.
candidates.suggestion: Inspect the outgoing worker event and result bodies before coordinator processing, or run the worker in a separate process with a credential unknown to the coordinator.
candidates.failure_scenario: Worker-side redaction is removed and a gate prints a worker-only credential; the shared coordinator registry still redacts the stored output, so this test passes while the credential crosses the connection.

candidates.title: The bundle test never exercises distinct head and base commits
candidates.detail: The shared request fixture assigns the same commit to headSha and baseSha. Consequently, the end-to-end bundle test cannot detect an implementation that bundles only the head, even though the request requires both commits to be available on the worker.
candidates.suggestion: Create distinct base and head commits and have a worker gate verify that both requested commits are present.
candidates.failure_scenario: Bundle creation omits baseSha when it differs from headSha; the existing end-to-end test still passes because its two SHAs are identical.

The focused command `bun test test/workers.test.ts test/gate-executor.test.ts` could not run: one test file could not resolve `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/server/index.js`, and the other resolved a Zod version without `z.number().overwrite`.

Verifier: 8 candidates, 8 checked, 0 refuted.

findings.title: Accepting a passing final result can erase an already reported failure
findings.detail: Check events and the final GateRun are validated independently. The coordinator never compares an event with the corresponding final result, so a worker can report a failed check and then submit the same check as passing. The final passing result is returned to the pipeline even though the coordinator has already received evidence of failure.
findings.suggestion: Track check results by lease attempt and reject a final result that contradicts the events for that attempt, preserving failures as infrastructure failures or explicitly represented retries.
findings.failure_scenario: A worker posts a valid event for the requested test with ok=false, then posts a valid GateRun for the same SHA and command with ok=true and exitCode=0. The job completes successfully.

verification.evidence: src/server/workers.ts:130 validates the final result using only `!validRun(request, result.data.run)`; lines 135–136 independently call `workers.event(id, event.data)` or `workers.complete(id, result.data.run)`. src/db/workers.ts:290–291 sets `state='done',result=?` without consulting stored events. src/gates/lan.ts:72 returns that stored final result.
verification.trigger: A leased worker submits a requested check with ok=false, then submits an otherwise valid passing GateRun for the requested SHA. No comparison with the failed event occurs, and the job returns a passing result.

findings.title: Restart discards in-flight LAN retry jobs
findings.detail: Only baseline, initial, and rebase handles are eligible for reattachment. A shutdown during a timeout rerun or a baseline or regression retry leaves its durable LAN job running, but resume treats its handle as stale, cancels it, and enqueues another execution. This repeats work that had already been leased or completed and defeats durable reattachment for these gate executions.
findings.suggestion: Persist enough retry context to reattach the matching durable handle on resume, including timeout and targeted retry purposes.
findings.failure_scenario: The coordinator shuts down after a worker completes a regression-retry job but before the pipeline checkpoints its result. On restart, the completed handle is discarded and the retry is run again.

verification.evidence: src/pipeline/gate-execution.ts:29–37 only restores handles when stage/round/purpose match and '["baseline", "initial", "rebase"].includes(purpose)'; otherwise it calls 'await cancelGateExecution(pending.handle, ctx.deps.gateExecutor)'. Regression retries use purpose 'regression-retry' (src/pipeline/engine.ts:1265). On restart the gates stage first calls 'runGateExecution(ctx, "gates", "initial", cwd, gates, events)' (src/pipeline/engine.ts:1215), discarding the pending retry handle. A fresh LAN start calls 'workers.enqueue(req)' (src/gates/lan.ts:30), although attachment could recover a completed result through 'if (job.state === "done" && job.result) return JSON.parse(job.result) as GateRun' (src/gates/lan.ts:74).
verification.trigger: Coordinator restarts with a persisted regression-retry LAN handle after the worker completed the job but before its result was checkpointed. Resume discards that handle, reruns initial gates, and can enqueue the regression retry again instead of consuming its stored result.

findings.title: Local fallback can populate a LAN baseline cache entry
findings.detail: After infrastructure failures, the LAN executor returns a locally executed GateRun as an ordinary LAN result. The baseline cache key was selected as LAN before execution, so a passing fallback baseline is cached under that key. A later run can reuse it while its actual gates execute on a worker with a different environment, even though the cache distinguishes executors to avoid comparing results from different environments.
findings.suggestion: Do not cache a baseline produced by local fallback under the LAN executor key; propagate the actual execution environment or mark fallback results non-cacheable.
findings.failure_scenario: No worker is available for a baseline, so local fallback passes and is cached as LAN. A worker later becomes available and runs the change, while the pipeline reuses the local baseline as its worker baseline.

verification.evidence: src/pipeline/engine.ts:551 keys the baseline using configured selection: `executor: cfg.gateExecutor === "lan" && cfg.workers.repos.includes(ctx.repo.slug) ? "lan" : "local"`. src/gates/lan.ts:77-89 executes fallback via `local.start(request, controller.signal)` and returns `workers.sanitize(run)` without execution provenance. src/pipeline/engine.ts:574-577 then caches that result: `const fresh = await runBaseline(); ... if (cacheableBaseline(fresh, gates)) store.putBaselineCache(key, fresh, ctx.run.id);`. Lines 568-572 reuse a passing entry under the same key.
verification.trigger: Configure LAN execution for an opted-in repository with baseline caching enabled. With no workers available, the baseline falls back locally and passes, populating the LAN cache key. A later run on the same base reuses that local baseline while an available worker executes the change, comparing results from different execution environments.

findings.title: Bound retries for job requests and propagate permanent failures
findings.detail: The shared request loop discards every transport error and retries indefinitely, including certificate fingerprint mismatches and other permanent errors. It also retries every server error without a deadline. Heartbeats can continue renewing a job while a bundle, event, result, or failure request is stuck in this loop, so the coordinator never expires the lease or falls back locally. Permanent connection errors also leave the worker silently retrying instead of reporting the cause.
findings.suggestion: Classify retryable transport and server errors, propagate permanent errors, and bound job-request retries so a failed job stops renewing its lease or reports its infrastructure failure.
findings.failure_scenario: The coordinator accepts heartbeats but repeatedly returns HTTP 500 for a job's result endpoint. The worker retries that result forever while heartbeats renew the lease, leaving the gate run pending indefinitely.

verification.evidence: src/workers/client.ts:139–158 uses `for (;;)`, throws only for `reply.status < 500`, and caps only the delay: `delay = Math.min(delay * 2, 10_000)`. The result submission awaits this loop at line 233. Meanwhile, lines 250–254 run heartbeats independently, reporting `jobs: heldJobs()` (line 173); the job remains reported until the submission finishes (lines 237–239). src/db/workers.ts:187–189 renews each reported lease with `this.now() + this.times.lease`.
verification.trigger: Result submissions continually return HTTP 500 while heartbeats succeed and no cancellation occurs → the worker retries indefinitely, continuously renews the lease, and leaves the gate run pending without retrying another worker or falling back locally.

findings.title: Reject a final result that contradicts streamed check failures
findings.detail: Check events are validated and stored independently of the final GateRun. The final result is checked only against the requested names and commands, so a worker can first report a failing check and then submit a passing result for the same check. The coordinator accepts the pass even though it has already recorded evidence of a failure.
findings.suggestion: Reconcile the final result with the events from the current lease and reject contradictory outcomes as an infrastructure failure.
findings.failure_scenario: A worker posts a valid check event with `ok: false`, then posts a GateRun containing the same check with `ok: true` and exit code 0. Both requests are accepted and the gate completes as passing.

verification.evidence: src/server/workers.ts:125 validates streamed events with `validCheck(request, event.data.result, event.data.phase)`, while line 130 validates final results with `validRun(request, result.data.run)`. Neither receives prior events. Lines 135–136 store the event and complete the job independently; src/gates/lan.ts:72 returns `JSON.parse(job.result) as GateRun`.
verification.trigger: A valid failed check event followed by a valid passing final result for the same check and SHA is accepted. The final passing result determines the gate outcome.

findings.title: Worker-side credential redaction is not independently tested
findings.detail: The end-to-end test registers the credential in the same process that runs both the worker and coordinator, then checks only the stored coordinator result and events. Coordinator-side redaction can therefore make the test pass even if the worker sends the credential unredacted. That leaves the requested boundary check untested.
findings.suggestion: Capture the worker's outgoing event and result payloads before they reach the coordinator, or run the worker in a separate process with a credential unknown to the coordinator, and assert that the credential is absent.
findings.failure_scenario: Worker-side redaction regresses and a gate prints a worker-only credential. The credential crosses the network, but the current test still passes because the coordinator shares the credential registry and redacts it before storage.

verification.evidence: test/workers.test.ts:659 registers the secret with `registerCredential("WORKER_OUTPUT_TEST", secret)`, and test/workers.test.ts:459 invokes `runWorker(...)` in the same process. Assertions at test/workers.test.ts:681–683 inspect only stored data: `expect(jobs[0]?.result).not.toContain(secret)` and `expect(jobs[0]?.events).not.toContain(secret)`. Coordinator storage independently sanitizes events via `events.push(this.sanitize(event))` (src/db/workers.ts:238), with `sanitize` calling `redactGateData(data)` (src/db/workers.ts:57–60).
verification.trigger: Worker-side redaction regresses and sends a registered credential in gate output. Because this test shares the credential registry with the coordinator and checks only sanitized stored results/events, coordinator redaction masks the network disclosure and the privacy assertions still pass.

findings.title: Publish worker check events before validating the final result
findings.detail: Individual check events are stored and forwarded to the run as gate results after only their name, command, and shape are checked. The worker has not yet supplied a checked SHA or a complete GateRun. If its eventual result has the wrong SHA, omits a check, or never arrives, those earlier events remain visible as pass or fail evidence even though the attempt is classified as an infrastructure failure.
findings.suggestion: Keep worker check events provisional until the final SHA and GateRun have been validated, or clearly mark and exclude them from authoritative gate evidence until validation succeeds.
findings.failure_scenario: A leased worker posts a passing event for a requested check, then posts a result with a different SHA. The result is rejected and retried, but the earlier passing event has already been persisted in the run's gate events.

verification.evidence: src/db/workers.ts:238–239 immediately appends and persists events: `events.push(this.sanitize(event))`. src/gates/lan.ts:68–69 streams those stored events without waiting for final validation. src/gates/executor.ts:211–212 forwards checks to `hooks.onResult`; src/pipeline/engine.ts:400–406 persists them as gate events with a pass/FAIL message. src/server/workers.ts:128–133 subsequently rejects a mismatched final SHA through `workers.fail(...)`.
verification.trigger: A worker posts a passing check event, which is streamed into the run's persisted gate events, then submits a final result for a different SHA. The result is rejected and retried, but the earlier passing event remains visible.

findings.title: A failed streamed check can be replaced by a passing final result
findings.detail: The request says infrastructure failures must “never turn a failing check into a pass” and that the result is untrusted. Streamed check events are stored independently, but the final GateRun is validated only against the requested names and commands; it is never compared with the events already accepted for that lease. A worker can therefore report a failed check and then submit the same check as passing, and the coordinator accepts the passing GateRun as the authoritative outcome.
findings.suggestion: Track the accepted check events for each lease attempt and reject a final result that disagrees with them, treating the mismatch as an infrastructure failure.
findings.failure_scenario: A worker posts a valid event for the requested `test` check with `ok: false`, then posts a valid final GateRun for `test` with `ok: true` and exit code 0. The job completes as passing despite the recorded failed check.

verification.evidence: src/server/workers.ts:135–136 uses `workers.event(id, event.data)` for streamed checks and `workers.complete(id, result.data.run)` for final results. Final validation at line 130 calls `validRun(request, result.data.run)` without stored events. src/db/workers.ts:290–291 stores the final result as done; src/gates/lan.ts:72 returns it directly.
verification.trigger: A leased worker reports test as failed, then supplies a schema-valid passing final GateRun for the same requested command and SHA. The recorded failure does not prevent the job from completing as passing.

candidates.title: Accepting a passing final result can erase an already reported failure
candidates.detail: Check events and the final GateRun are validated independently. The coordinator never compares an event with the corresponding final result, so a worker can report a failed check and then submit the same check as passing. The final passing result is returned to the pipeline even though the coordinator has already received evidence of failure.
candidates.suggestion: Track check results by lease attempt and reject a final result that contradicts the events for that attempt, preserving failures as infrastructure failures or explicitly represented retries.
candidates.failure_scenario: A worker posts a valid event for the requested test with ok=false, then posts a valid GateRun for the same SHA and command with ok=true and exitCode=0. The job completes successfully.

candidates.title: Restart discards in-flight LAN retry jobs
candidates.detail: Only baseline, initial, and rebase handles are eligible for reattachment. A shutdown during a timeout rerun or a baseline or regression retry leaves its durable LAN job running, but resume treats its handle as stale, cancels it, and enqueues another execution. This repeats work that had already been leased or completed and defeats durable reattachment for these gate executions.
candidates.suggestion: Persist enough retry context to reattach the matching durable handle on resume, including timeout and targeted retry purposes.
candidates.failure_scenario: The coordinator shuts down after a worker completes a regression-retry job but before the pipeline checkpoints its result. On restart, the completed handle is discarded and the retry is run again.

candidates.title: Local fallback can populate a LAN baseline cache entry
candidates.detail: After infrastructure failures, the LAN executor returns a locally executed GateRun as an ordinary LAN result. The baseline cache key was selected as LAN before execution, so a passing fallback baseline is cached under that key. A later run can reuse it while its actual gates execute on a worker with a different environment, even though the cache distinguishes executors to avoid comparing results from different environments.
candidates.suggestion: Do not cache a baseline produced by local fallback under the LAN executor key; propagate the actual execution environment or mark fallback results non-cacheable.
candidates.failure_scenario: No worker is available for a baseline, so local fallback passes and is cached as LAN. A worker later becomes available and runs the change, while the pipeline reuses the local baseline as its worker baseline.

candidates.title: Bound retries for job requests and propagate permanent failures
candidates.detail: The shared request loop discards every transport error and retries indefinitely, including certificate fingerprint mismatches and other permanent errors. It also retries every server error without a deadline. Heartbeats can continue renewing a job while a bundle, event, result, or failure request is stuck in this loop, so the coordinator never expires the lease or falls back locally. Permanent connection errors also leave the worker silently retrying instead of reporting the cause.
candidates.suggestion: Classify retryable transport and server errors, propagate permanent errors, and bound job-request retries so a failed job stops renewing its lease or reports its infrastructure failure.
candidates.failure_scenario: The coordinator accepts heartbeats but repeatedly returns HTTP 500 for a job's result endpoint. The worker retries that result forever while heartbeats renew the lease, leaving the gate run pending indefinitely.

candidates.title: Reject a final result that contradicts streamed check failures
candidates.detail: Check events are validated and stored independently of the final GateRun. The final result is checked only against the requested names and commands, so a worker can first report a failing check and then submit a passing result for the same check. The coordinator accepts the pass even though it has already recorded evidence of a failure.
candidates.suggestion: Reconcile the final result with the events from the current lease and reject contradictory outcomes as an infrastructure failure.
candidates.failure_scenario: A worker posts a valid check event with `ok: false`, then posts a GateRun containing the same check with `ok: true` and exit code 0. Both requests are accepted and the gate completes as passing.

candidates.title: Worker-side credential redaction is not independently tested
candidates.detail: The end-to-end test registers the credential in the same process that runs both the worker and coordinator, then checks only the stored coordinator result and events. Coordinator-side redaction can therefore make the test pass even if the worker sends the credential unredacted. That leaves the requested boundary check untested.
candidates.suggestion: Capture the worker's outgoing event and result payloads before they reach the coordinator, or run the worker in a separate process with a credential unknown to the coordinator, and assert that the credential is absent.
candidates.failure_scenario: Worker-side redaction regresses and a gate prints a worker-only credential. The credential crosses the network, but the current test still passes because the coordinator shares the credential registry and redacts it before storage.

findings.title: A restart can retain a flake whose evidence was overwritten
findings.detail: The flake reason is persisted before the checked head is checkpointed as pushedSha. If the process stops in that interval, the resumed entry reruns checks and truncates the land log. A clean rerun does not clear the old reason, so the eventual landed entry still reports the earlier flake while its log no longer contains that failure or retry.
findings.suggestion: Associate the flake outcome with the completed checks checkpoint, or clear and recompute the reason when restarting checks while preserving the corresponding log evidence.
findings.failure_scenario: A targeted retry passes, the flake reason is stored, and the daemon stops before pushedSha is recorded. On restart, all checks pass cleanly; the entry lands with the old flaky reason and a replacement log containing only the clean run.

verification.evidence: src/land/queue.ts:463 persists `this.store.updateLandEntry(entry.id, { reason });` before checks return and `pushedSha` is recorded (lines 352–359). On resume with no pushed SHA, lines 350–352 run checks again; line 408 uses `writeFileSync(log, ...)`, replacing the previous log. Lines 459–463 update the reason only `if (retries.size)`, so a clean rerun retains it. Line 385 preserves that reason in the landed entry: `${current.reason?.startsWith("flaky:") ? `${current.reason}; ` : ""}merged ...`. src/db/store.ts:2787–2788 reclaims the entry without clearing its reason.
verification.trigger: A retry passes and stores the flaky reason; the daemon stops before pushedSha is persisted. Resumed checks pass cleanly and overwrite the log. The entry subsequently lands with the previous flaky reason but without the original failure and retry evidence in its log.

findings.title: A restart can erase the evidence for a recorded flaky landing
findings.detail: The flaky reason and warning are persisted before the land reaches its durable pushed-SHA checkpoint. If the daemon stops in that interval, the entry resumes from checking and checks() truncates the same land log before rerunning the gates. A subsequent clean run leaves the old flaky reason in place, so the landed entry claims a flake whose first failure and retry have disappeared from its log. This violates the requirement to “Write the first failure and the retry to the land log” and keep the outcome on the entry.
findings.suggestion: Make the retry evidence and recorded outcome consistent across a checking restart, for example by preserving prior attempts in the log and associating the reason with the checks that authorize the eventual landing.
findings.failure_scenario: A targeted retry passes, the flaky reason is stored, and the daemon restarts before pushedSha is recorded. On resume, the full checks pass cleanly; the log is overwritten, but the eventual landed reason still says flaky.

verification.evidence: src/land/queue.ts:408 overwrites the per-entry log with `writeFileSync(log, ...)` whenever checks restart. Lines 350–352 rerun checks when `entry.pushedSha` is absent. Lines 459–463 persist a reason only `if (retries.size)` and do not clear a previous reason on a clean run. Line 385 explicitly retains `current.reason` when it starts with `"flaky:"`. The original flaky reason is persisted at line 463 before the pushedSha checkpoint at lines 354–359.
verification.trigger: After a successful targeted retry records its flaky reason, a restart occurs before the pushedSha checkpoint. A clean resumed run replaces the log while retaining the flaky reason, leaving the eventual landed entry without the corresponding log evidence. This is the same defect as C1.

findings.title: Stop before retrying when another check reports a confinement failure
findings.detail: The queue selects retryable checks before considering confinement failures elsewhere in the gate run. A failed test with reported files is therefore retried even when another check has already reported a confinement failure. The land eventually blocks, but only after running and waiting for a retry that cannot make it eligible to land.
findings.suggestion: Inspect the complete initial gate run for confinement failures before starting targeted retries, and block immediately if one is present.

findings.title: Allow the Bun executable resolved by the verifier’s PATH
findings.detail: The read exception grants only process.execPath, which is the Bun running the daemon. A verifier normally invokes `bun test` through its inherited PATH, which can resolve to a different installation under a private read root. That executable remains denied, so the reported verifier failure can persist. The new smoke check also invokes process.execPath explicitly, so it can pass in this configuration without exercising the verifier’s actual command.
findings.suggestion: Resolve the Bun executable using the same PATH supplied to the verifier, validate its canonical path against the denied paths, and have the smoke check exercise `bun test` through that PATH.
findings.failure_scenario: The daemon starts with `/opt/homebrew/bin/bun`, while the verifier’s PATH resolves `bun` to `~/.bun/bin/bun`; the sandbox allows the former and denies the latter, but the smoke probe passes using the former.

verification.evidence: src/harness/claude.ts:174 defaults to `bunExecutable = process.execPath`; :225 grants only `spellings([bunExecutable])`; :246 sets `allowRead: [...readable, ...bun]`. src/harness/scratch.ts:279 includes `homedir()` in denied roots. src/util/proc.ts:782 describes agent environments as inheriting `PATH`. scripts/smoke.ts:755 uses `${quote(process.execPath)} ${quote(probe)}`, bypassing PATH resolution.
verification.trigger: Daemon uses /opt/homebrew/bin/bun while verifier PATH selects a distinct ~/.bun/bin/bun outside cwd and scratch. The selected Bun remains read-denied; the smoke probe can pass using the daemon binary.

findings.title: Smoke probe bypasses the verifier's test-command wrapper
findings.detail: The probe invokes Bun by absolute path and sets confineReads to true. The production verification stage does not set confineReads, so it receives the configured slotted-command wrappers and normally runs `bun test` through them. Consequently, the smoke check can pass while the wrapper hangs or otherwise prevents a verifier from running tests—the failure this change also attempts to address through EPERM handling.
findings.suggestion: Run the live probe through the same verification invocation setup and command wrapper used by the pipeline, including invoking `bun test` as a verifier would.
findings.failure_scenario: A regression makes the slotted `bun test` wrapper wait indefinitely when the sandbox denies its socket connections, while direct execution of the Bun binary still succeeds. The smoke check reports a pass, but production verifiers remain unable to run tests.

verification.evidence: scripts/smoke.ts:744 executes `cmd: [${JSON.stringify(process.execPath)}, "test", ...]` directly; scripts/smoke.ts:761 sets `confineReads: true`. Production verification invokes `role: "verify"`, `mode: "readonly"` without confineReads (src/pipeline/engine.ts:1721–1740). src/pipeline/context.ts:846 selects `opts.confineReads ? [] : (this.state.slottedCommands ?? [])`, so production verifiers can receive wrappers that this probe excludes.
verification.trigger: With slotted commands configured, a wrapper regression can block production verifier tests while the smoke probe passes by executing Bun directly.

findings.title: Home-relative paths and file URLs bypass sanitization
findings.detail:
The sanitizer compares link destinations only against literal filesystem roots. A home-relative link such as the one in the request is left broken, and a file URL containing the absolute worktree path is published unchanged, including the owner's username. The direct check below returned both inputs unchanged.

Command: bun -e 'let s=await Bun.file("src/gates/publication.ts").text(); let f=new Function(s.slice(s.indexOf("export function sanitizePublication"),s.indexOf("/** Check both")).replace("export function","function").replace(/: string( \| undefined)?/g,"")+";return sanitizePublication")(); for(let x of ["[file](~/.limitless/work/run/a.ts)","[file](file:///Users/alice/.limitless/work/run/a.ts)","[/Users/alice/.limitless/work/run/a.ts](a.ts)"]) console.log(f(x,"/Users/alice/.limitless/work/run","/Users/alice/.limitless"))'
Output:
[file](~/.limitless/work/run/a.ts)
[file](file:///Users/alice/.limitless/work/run/a.ts)
[/Users/alice/.limitless/work/run/a.ts](a.ts)
findings.suggestion: Recognize home-relative paths and local file URLs before comparing them with the configured roots, and add cases for both forms.
findings.failure_scenario: A report contains [file](file:///Users/alice/.limitless/work/run/a.ts) or [file](~/.limitless/work/run/a.ts).

verification.evidence: src/gates/publication.ts:8-9 matches only `path === root || path.startsWith(`${root}/`)` and otherwise returns the path. Neither `file:///...` nor `~/...` matches an absolute configured root.
verification.trigger: A report links to the worktree through a file URL or home-relative path; the link remains unchanged, retaining private directory information and a broken GitHub target.

findings.title: Absolute paths in link labels are published unchanged
findings.detail: The link regex consumes the entire Markdown link, but the replacement examines only its destination. If the destination is already relative, an absolute worktree path in the visible label is never visited by the bare-path matcher and is published with the owner's username. The direct check reported in the preceding finding returned [/Users/alice/.limitless/work/run/a.ts](a.ts) unchanged.
findings.suggestion: Sanitize local paths in link labels as well as destinations while preserving ordinary relative links.
findings.failure_scenario: An implementer reports [/Users/alice/.limitless/work/run/a.ts](a.ts), a relative link whose visible label contains the absolute worktree path.

verification.evidence: src/gates/publication.ts:21-24 examines only the destination (`const path = angle ?? bare`) and returns the entire original link when `result === path`.
verification.trigger: `[/factory/data/work/run/a.ts](a.ts)` has a relative destination, so its absolute visible label is published unchanged. Reproduced with the sanitizer.

findings.title: File URI links retain the absolute local path
findings.detail: The link matcher captures the whole file URI, but rewrite only recognizes destinations beginning directly with a configured filesystem root. A file URI therefore passes through unchanged and can publish the owner's username and data layout. An isolated probe of the sanitizer returned `[file](file:///factory/data/work/run/a.ts)` unchanged.
findings.suggestion: Recognize local file URI destinations and rewrite their decoded filesystem paths, while preserving ordinary remote URLs.
findings.failure_scenario: A report contains `[file](file:///factory/data/work/run/a.ts)` and the configured worktree is `/factory/data/work/run`.

verification.evidence: src/gates/publication.ts:8-9 requires the destination to begin with the configured root; src/gates/publication.ts:24 preserves the original link when rewriting makes no change.
verification.trigger: With worktree `/factory/data/work/run`, `[file](file:///factory/data/work/run/a.ts)` remains unchanged. Reproduced with the sanitizer; this overlaps C1.

findings.title: Bare paths immediately after a colon are skipped
findings.detail: The negative lookbehind excludes a colon, so a common `path:/absolute/path` form is left untouched. An isolated probe returned `path:/factory/data/work/run/a.ts` unchanged, allowing the local path to reach publication when the private-string list does not already block it.
findings.suggestion: Recognize bare local paths following punctuation such as a colon without rewriting paths embedded in remote URLs.
findings.failure_scenario: An implementer report contains `path:/factory/data/work/run/a.ts` with that directory configured as the worktree.

verification.evidence: src/gates/publication.ts:17 uses the negative lookbehind `(?<![\\w/.:~%-])`, explicitly excluding a root immediately preceded by a colon.
verification.trigger: `path:/factory/data/work/run/a.ts` remains unchanged instead of becoming `path:a.ts`. Reproduced with the sanitizer.

findings.title: Dot segments classify paths outside the worktree as inside it
findings.detail: Classification uses a string prefix without resolving dot segments. The sanitizer turns `[file](/factory/data/work/run/../other/log)` into `[../other/log](../other/log)`, although the destination is outside the worktree and should be rendered as a data-directory placeholder.
findings.suggestion: Normalize path segments before deciding which root contains a local destination.
findings.failure_scenario: A report links to a data-directory file using an absolute path containing `work/run/../other/log`.

verification.evidence: src/gates/publication.ts:8 classifies paths using a lexical prefix; lines 10-11 slice that prefix without resolving dot segments: `return index === 0 ? suffix.slice(1) || "." : `<data>${suffix}`;`.
verification.trigger: `[log](/factory/data/work/run/../other/log)` becomes `[../other/log](../other/log)` instead of plain `<data>/work/other/log`, misclassifying an outside-worktree file. Reproduced with the sanitizer.

findings.title: File-URL links retain the absolute local path
findings.detail: The link destination is compared directly with the filesystem roots, so a file:// URL never matches. The fallback bare-path matcher also excludes a path preceded by a slash. The publication therefore retains the username and factory layout, or is blocked when those strings are configured as private.
