An isolated sanitizer probe returned `[file](file:///factory/data/work/run/src/a.ts)` and `[log](file:///factory/data/runs/log)` unchanged. These links expose local paths and remain broken for GitHub readers.
findings.suggestion: Recognize local file URI destinations, convert worktree targets to repository-relative links, and render data-directory targets as plain placeholder text.
findings.failure_scenario: An implementer report links a local source file as `[file](file:///factory/data/work/run/src/a.ts)` or a log as `[log](file:///factory/data/runs/log)`.

verification.evidence: src/gates/publication.ts:8–9: `path === root || path.startsWith(`${root}/`)` followed by `if (index < 0) return path;`. A `file:///...` destination matches neither root. Direct execution preserved both candidate links.
verification.trigger: `[file](file:///factory/data/work/run/src/a.ts)` or `[log](file:///factory/data/runs/log)` passes through sanitization unchanged, retaining the absolute local path.

findings.title: Paths in Markdown link labels bypass sanitization
findings.detail: The link pattern consumes an entire Markdown link, but the replacement examines only its destination. If the destination is relative, it returns the original link unchanged, including an absolute worktree path in its visible label. A direct sanitizer check returned `[/factory/data/work/run/a.ts](docs/a.ts)` unchanged. This can publish the owner's local path or cause delivery to be blocked once the username is added to private strings.
findings.suggestion: Sanitize path occurrences in the link label as well as the destination while preserving ordinary links.
findings.failure_scenario: A report contains `[/factory/data/work/run/a.ts](docs/a.ts)` and is published before the username is present in private-strings.txt.

verification.evidence: src/gates/publication.ts:13 matches the entire Markdown link; lines 21–24 rewrite only its destination and return the entire original match when that destination is unchanged: `if (result === path) return match;`. Direct execution reproduced the candidate.
verification.trigger: `[/factory/data/work/run/a.ts](docs/a.ts)` retains its absolute label and is publishable before the username is listed in private-strings.txt.

findings.title: File URLs containing worktree paths are left unchanged
findings.detail: The bare-path pattern excludes a path preceded by `/` or `:`, so a `file://` URL is not rewritten. The link handler also treats a `file://` destination as outside both roots. A direct sanitizer check returned `file:///factory/data/work/run/a.ts` unchanged, allowing the absolute local path to reach publication.
findings.suggestion: Recognize local file URLs and sanitize their decoded local paths before publication.
findings.failure_scenario: An implementer report contains `file:///factory/data/work/run/a.ts` or a Markdown link to that URL.

verification.evidence: src/gates/publication.ts:17 uses `(?<![\\w/.:~%-])` before bare roots, preventing a root preceded by the slash in `file:///` from matching. Lines 8–9 also leave URI destinations unchanged. Direct execution preserved the bare URI and Markdown URI link.
verification.trigger: A bare `file:///factory/data/work/run/a.ts` or Markdown link to it retains the absolute worktree path in publication text.

findings.title: Paths in Markdown link labels bypass sanitization
findings.detail: The link expression consumes the entire link, but when its destination is not a local path the callback returns the entire match unchanged. A local path in the visible label therefore reaches publication intact. The tests cover local paths in destinations and bare text, but not in labels.
findings.suggestion: Sanitize local paths in link labels as well as destinations, and add a publication test for a local label with a relative destination.
findings.failure_scenario: `[/factory/data/work/run/src/a.ts](docs/a.md)` remains unchanged, exposing the factory data path in the PR body or comment.

verification.evidence: src/gates/publication.ts:21–24: `const path = angle ?? bare; ... if (result === path) return match;`. The relative destination is unchanged, so the original link, including its absolute label, is returned. Direct execution confirmed this exact input.
verification.trigger: `[/factory/data/work/run/src/a.ts](docs/a.md)` remains unchanged and exposes the local data path in a published body or comment unless private-string checks block publication.

findings.title: Line-number links remain broken on GitHub
findings.detail: The sanitizer preserves a `:12` line suffix as part of the relative link destination. GitHub treats that as a filename rather than a line anchor. The test exercises a line suffix only on a bare path, so it does not catch this common report-link form.
findings.suggestion: Convert supported line-number suffixes to GitHub line anchors and test a worktree link with a line number.
findings.failure_scenario: `[file](/factory/data/work/run/src/a.ts:12)` becomes `[src/a.ts:12](src/a.ts:12)`, which does not link to line 12 of `src/a.ts`.

verification.evidence: src/gates/publication.ts:10–11 slices the prefix without converting line suffixes: `const suffix = path.slice(roots[index]?.length); return index === 0 ? suffix.slice(1) || "." : `<data>${suffix}`;`. Line 25 uses that result as the link destination.
verification.trigger: `[file](/factory/data/work/run/src/a.ts:12)` becomes `[src/a.ts:12](src/a.ts:12)`, pointing to a filename containing `:12` rather than GitHub's `src/a.ts#L12`. Reproduced with the extracted function.

findings.title: Sanitizing an image link removes its image syntax
findings.detail: The link matcher accepts the leading `!` of Markdown images, but reconstruction always emits an ordinary link. No test covers an image destination under the worktree.
findings.suggestion: Preserve the image marker when rewriting a worktree image destination and add a corresponding test.
findings.failure_scenario: `![diagram](/factory/data/work/run/diagram.png)` becomes `[diagram.png](diagram.png)`, so the published report no longer displays the diagram.

verification.evidence: src/gates/publication.ts:13 matches optional image syntax with `/!?\[/`; line 25 reconstructs it as `[${result}](${angle ? `<${result}>` : result})`, omitting `!`.
verification.trigger: `![diagram](/factory/data/work/run/diagram.png)` becomes `[diagram.png](diagram.png)`, replacing the displayed image with a link. Reproduced with the extracted function.

findings.title: Round delivery rewrites the existing published PR body
findings.detail: Sanitizing the concatenation of `pr.body` and the new round section rewrites existing published content, although rewriting already published PR bodies is explicitly out of scope. The new round test uses a comment route and does not exercise this PR-body edit route with existing local paths.
findings.suggestion: Sanitize the new section before appending it without transforming the existing body, and cover that route with a pre-existing body containing a local path.
findings.failure_scenario: When a review round appends a section to an existing PR body containing an old worktree link, the edit also changes that old link.

verification.evidence: src/pipeline/engine.ts:2148 constructs `const body = publicationText(ctx, pr.body + text);`, sanitizing the existing body along with the new section. Line 2151 publishes it with `gh(["pr", "edit", prUrl, "--body-file", "-"], ctx.signal, body)`. src/gates/publication.ts:11 rewrites matching paths to repo-relative paths or `<data>` placeholders.
verification.trigger: A normal review round appends a section whose marker is absent from an existing PR body containing an old absolute worktree link under the factory data directory. Sanitizing the concatenated body changes that previously published link, violating the explicit exclusion of rewriting already-published PR bodies.

findings.title: Absolute paths in link labels bypass sanitization
findings.detail: The link expression consumes the entire Markdown link, but only its destination is inspected. If the destination is already relative, the original link is returned unchanged, including any absolute worktree or data-directory path in its visible label.
findings.suggestion: Sanitize path text in link labels as well as destinations, while preserving unrelated links.
findings.failure_scenario: A report containing `[/factory/data/work/run/test/a.ts](test/a.ts)` publishes the absolute path and its owner-specific prefix unchanged.

verification.evidence: src/gates/publication.ts:21 extracts only the destination: `const path = angle ?? bare;`; line 24 returns the entire original link when that destination is unchanged: `if (result === path) return match;`.
verification.trigger: `[/factory/data/work/run/test/a.ts](test/a.ts)` remains unchanged because its destination is relative. The absolute local path in its label survives sanitization and can be published or cause the subsequent privacy check to block delivery.

findings.title: Encoded link destinations evade path matching
findings.detail: The sanitizer compares the raw Markdown destination with literal filesystem roots. HTML character references and URL escapes can represent the same local path without matching those roots, leaving the path in the published text. The later private-text check decodes HTML entities, but it only blocks values present in the private strings list and does not perform the requested rewrite.
findings.suggestion: Decode Markdown link destinations for classification before checking their path boundaries, then emit a sanitized destination.
findings.failure_scenario: With worktree `/factory/data/work/run`, `[x](/factory/data/work/run/file)` remains unchanged and exposes the decoded absolute path.

verification.evidence: src/gates/publication.ts:8 compares the raw destination using `path === root || path.startsWith(`${root}/`)`; lines 23–24 call `rewrite(path)` and return the original match when unchanged. HTML decoding occurs only in the separate checker at line 32: `checkPrivateText(decodeHTML(text).replace(/\s+/g, " "), location, entries);`.
verification.trigger: `[x](/factory/data/work/run/file)` remains unchanged during sanitization. Its Markdown destination decodes to an absolute local path; publication can expose it when no private-string entry blocks it, or delivery is blocked when one does.

findings.title: Traversal paths outside the worktree are classified as inside it
findings.detail: The prefix comparison does not normalize `..` components before deciding which root contains a path. A path that starts with the worktree prefix but resolves elsewhere in the data directory is turned into a repository-relative link rather than plain `<data>` text.
findings.suggestion: Normalize path components before selecting the containing root, and classify the normalized path against directory boundaries.
findings.failure_scenario: `[x](/factory/data/work/run/../other/log)` becomes `[../other/log](../other/log)` instead of a `<data>` placeholder, producing a broken link to a path outside the repository.

verification.evidence: src/gates/publication.ts:8 classifies paths by textual prefix: `path.startsWith(`${root}/`)`; lines 10–11 remove that prefix without resolving traversal: `const suffix = path.slice(roots[index]?.length); return index === 0 ? suffix.slice(1) || "." : `<data>${suffix}`;`.
verification.trigger: `[x](/factory/data/work/run/../other/log)` becomes `[../other/log](../other/log)`. The path resolves outside the worktree but receives a relative repository link instead of the required `<data>` placeholder. Reproduced with the extracted function.

Reviewed claim ownership across land queue operations and their Git helpers. The targeted command `bun test test/land-queue.test.ts` could not run because the checkout is missing `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/client/index.js`. The review found gaps where a reclaimed worker can still issue commands or remove the new worker’s checkout.

The requested deferred merge-result and CI-response guards are present, but ownership can still be lost inside nested helpers before they issue a merge or push, and stale workers can still make CI and worktree changes. The targeted command `bun test test/land-queue.test.ts` could not start because the checkout is missing `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/client/index.js`.

Verifier: 14 candidates, 14 checked, 0 refuted.

findings.title: Recheck ownership inside the merge helper before each merge command
findings.detail: The ownership check precedes mergePullRequest, but that helper awaits a GitHub PR lookup before issuing gh pr merge and can repeat that sequence on retry. A reclaim during the lookup is invisible until the heartbeat, so the old worker can still issue a merge after losing its claim.
findings.suggestion: Pass an ownership guard into the helper and check it immediately before each merge command, including retries.
findings.failure_scenario: The old worker enters mergePullRequest, its PR view request is deferred, another owner reclaims the entry, and the view returns before the old heartbeat fires. The old worker then runs gh pr merge.

verification.evidence: src/land/queue.ts:701 awaits `mergePullRequest(...)`; the next ownership check is at :715, `this.assertClaim(entry.id)`. Inside the helper, src/git/repos.ts:1447 awaits `sh(view, { cwd, signal })`, then :1462 runs `sh(cmd, { cwd, signal, stdin: body })` without checking claim ownership.
verification.trigger: Reclaim the entry while the helper's PR view is pending, then return an OPEN PR with the expected head before the heartbeat aborts. The displaced worker issues gh pr merge.

findings.title: Guard the actual push after its preparation awaits
findings.detail: The transaction verifies the claim before calling pushExistingBranch, but that helper awaits commit resolution, transport setup, a remote lookup, and an ancestry check before issuing git push. A reclaim during any of those awaits leaves the old worker able to push before its heartbeat notices.
findings.suggestion: Check ownership inside the push helper immediately before issuing the push, using a guard supplied by the land worker.
findings.failure_scenario: The worker passes the ownership transaction, pauses in the helper's ls-remote call, and another owner reclaims the entry. When ls-remote returns, the stale worker pushes its merge commit.

verification.evidence: src/land/queue.ts:517 checks ownership through `this.owned(...)`, then :522 calls `pushExistingBranch(...)`. That helper awaits `ls-remote` at src/git/repos.ts:1313 and an ancestor check at :1315, then executes `remoteSh([...BRANCH_PUSH, ...])` at :1321 without rechecking ownership.
verification.trigger: Reclaim during the helper's ls-remote call; return the approved remote SHA and a successful ancestor check before the heartbeat fires. The displaced worker pushes its merge commit.

findings.title: Do not discard a checkout reused by the new claimant
findings.detail: All attempts for an entry use the same land-<id> worktree path. After a reclaim, the old worker reaches this unconditional cleanup even when a new worker has already recreated and started using that path. It can remove the new worker's worktree and cause its checks or merge to fail.
findings.suggestion: Isolate checkout paths by claim or otherwise ensure cleanup cannot remove a newer claimant's checkout.
findings.failure_scenario: A CI response is deferred, the entry is reclaimed and the new worker creates its checkout, then the old response returns. The old worker detects the lost claim but its finally block removes the new worker's checkout.

verification.evidence: src/land/queue.ts:549 calls `this.assertClaim(entry.id)` after the CI observation, but :396–397 unconditionally executes `finally { await this.discard(repo, cwd); }`. The checkout path is shared: :812 returns `join(this.deps.paths.work, `land-${entry.id}`)`. At :842, discard executes `rmSync(cwd, { recursive: true, force: true })`.
verification.trigger: A new claimant creates the same entry's checkout while the old worker awaits CI. The old response returns, ownership validation throws, and unconditional cleanup deletes the new claimant's checkout.

findings.title: CI inspection can still write after the claim is reclaimed
findings.detail: Passing the ownership check as `current` does not guard every write inside `ciDecision`. Its inspection awaits the default branch and check-run responses, then emits feed events and updates the `ci.main` setting before checking `current()`. A claim reclaimed during either read can therefore leave the old worker writing outcomes after ownership was lost.
findings.suggestion: Check ownership after the awaited reads and in the same transaction as each resulting durable write, including CI inspection writes.
findings.failure_scenario: A worker starts CI inspection, another owner reclaims the entry while the default-branch check response is pending, and the old response contains a failing check. The old worker emits a `ci.main_red` event and updates the CI setting after reclaim.

verification.evidence: src/land/queue.ts:625–634 passes the ownership-aware `current` callback into `ciDecision`. However, src/integrations/ci-classifier.ts:239 awaits `checks(mainSha)`, :258–264 emits `ci.main_red`, and :267 calls `store.setSetting(...)`; only afterward does :268 execute `if (!current()) return true`. The read wrapper at :97–103 checks HTTP status but not ownership.
verification.trigger: Reclaim while default-branch checks are pending, then return a failing check matching the PR's failing check name before heartbeat abort. The displaced worker writes a ci.main_red event and updates the CI setting.

findings.title: A displaced worker can delete the new owner's worktree
findings.detail: The unconditional cleanup runs after `LandClaimLost` as well as normal completion. Both attempts use the same `land-<entry id>` worktree path, so once a new owner has checked it out, the old worker's `discard` removes that checkout and its Git worktree registration. The new owner can then fail or operate on a deleted checkout.
findings.suggestion: Give each attempt an isolated worktree path or otherwise ensure cleanup cannot remove a successor's checkout.
findings.failure_scenario: A worker is waiting for CI, its claim is reclaimed, and the new worker creates the same checkout. When the old CI response arrives, its ownership check throws and its `finally` deletes the new worker's checkout.

verification.evidence: src/land/queue.ts:396–397 unconditionally runs `finally { await this.discard(repo, cwd); }`, including when :549 detects lost ownership. Both claimants use :812, `join(this.deps.paths.work, `land-${entry.id}`)`, and discard at :842 runs `rmSync(cwd, { recursive: true, force: true })` without an ownership guard.
verification.trigger: The entry is reclaimed and its replacement checkout is created while the old worker waits for CI. Releasing the old response triggers lost-claim cleanup, deleting the replacement checkout. This duplicates C3.

findings.title: A worker that lost its claim can remove the new worker's checkout
findings.detail: The unconditional cleanup runs when an ownership check throws after a reclaim. Both attempts use the same `land-<entry id>` worktree path, so the old worker can remove the checkout after the new owner has created it. This violates the requirement that a worker that lost its claim write nothing and can cause the new attempt's Git commands or gates to fail.
findings.suggestion: Make checkout ownership and cleanup safe across overlapping attempts, and prevent an old attempt from removing a newer attempt's worktree.
findings.failure_scenario: The old worker waits for CI, another queue reclaims the entry and creates its checkout, then the CI response returns. The old worker detects the lost claim but its finally block removes the shared checkout.

verification.evidence: src/land/queue.ts:547 checks `this.assertClaim(entry.id)` after CI observation, but unwinding still executes src/land/queue.ts:396–397: `finally { await this.discard(repo, cwd); }`. The path is shared: src/land/queue.ts:812 returns `join(this.deps.paths.work, `land-${entry.id}`)`. src/land/queue.ts:842 unconditionally executes `rmSync(cwd, { recursive: true, force: true })`.
verification.trigger: A new owner reclaims the entry and recreates its checkout while the old worker awaits CI. The old response returns, ownership validation throws, and unconditional cleanup deletes the new owner's checkout.

findings.title: Reclaim tests do not exercise a running replacement worker
findings.detail: The new tests replace the claim owner in the store but never start a replacement worker or inspect its checkout. Their snapshots therefore pass even though the old worker's unconditional cleanup can delete a replacement worker's files.
findings.suggestion: Add a test that pauses the old worker, reclaims the entry with a second queue, waits until the second attempt has created its checkout, then releases the old worker and verifies that the checkout and second attempt remain intact.
findings.failure_scenario: A reclaim occurs while the old worker awaits CI or a merge result, and the new worker begins using the same worktree before the old worker exits.

verification.evidence: test/land-queue.test.ts:1642 only calls `store.claimLandEntry(..., "new-owner", ...)`; lines 1650–1654 snapshot state, release the old worker and stop its queue without starting a replacement worker. The snapshot omits worktree contents. src/land/queue.ts:396–397 unconditionally executes `finally { await this.discard(repo, cwd); }`; lines 811–812 derive the shared path as `land-${entry.id}`, and lines 838–842 remove it, including `rmSync(cwd, { recursive: true, force: true })`.
verification.trigger: A replacement worker reclaims the entry and starts using its worktree while the old worker awaits CI or merge. Releasing the old response runs unconditional cleanup, deleting the replacement's worktree. The tests exercise only the ownership-row change and therefore miss this overlap.

findings.title: Merge helper can issue a merge after the claim is reclaimed
findings.detail: The ownership check happens before calling mergePullRequest, but that helper awaits a GitHub PR lookup before issuing `gh pr merge`, and can await further reconciliation and retry operations. A reclaim during one of those awaits leaves the old signal active until its next heartbeat, so the old worker can still issue the merge. The check after the helper returns is too late.
findings.suggestion: Pass an ownership guard into the merge helper and check it immediately before every merge command, including retries.
findings.failure_scenario: The old worker enters mergePullRequest, its `gh pr view` response is deferred, another owner reclaims the entry, and the response is released before the old heartbeat. The old worker then runs `gh pr merge`.

verification.evidence: src/land/queue.ts:701 invokes `await mergePullRequest(...)`; ownership is checked only after it returns at line 715: `this.assertClaim(entry.id)`. Inside the helper, src/git/repos.ts:1447 awaits `sh(view, { cwd, signal })`, then lines 1461–1462 construct `gh pr merge` and execute `sh(cmd, { cwd, signal, stdin: body })` without checking claim ownership.
verification.trigger: Reclaim the entry while the helper's PR view is pending, then return a valid OPEN response before the old heartbeat. Its signal remains active, so the old worker issues the merge command.

findings.title: Push helper can push after the claim is reclaimed
findings.detail: The transactional ownership check precedes pushExistingBranch, but that helper awaits commit resolution, a remote lookup, and an ancestry check before starting the push. A reclaim during any of those operations is not detected before the push is issued.
findings.suggestion: Check ownership immediately before the actual push inside the helper, including after its asynchronous preparation.
findings.failure_scenario: The old worker passes the ownership check and blocks in pushExistingBranch's remote lookup. Another owner reclaims the entry and the lookup returns before the next heartbeat; the old worker pushes its merge commit.

verification.evidence: src/land/queue.ts:517–522 validates ownership in `this.owned(...)` before calling `await pushExistingBranch(...)`. Inside that helper, src/git/repos.ts:1313 awaits `remoteSh(["git", "ls-remote", url, ref], ...)`, line 1315 awaits the ancestry check, and line 1321 executes `remoteSh([...BRANCH_PUSH, ...])` without another claim check.
verification.trigger: Reclaim after the initial ownership check while the helper's remote lookup is pending. If the remote still matches the approved SHA and ancestry passes before the heartbeat aborts, the old worker pushes despite losing ownership.

findings.title: A worker that loses its claim still removes the shared checkout
findings.detail: The `finally` block always discards the worktree, including when an ownership check throws LandClaimLost. Both attempts use the same `land-<entry id>` path, so the old worker can remove the checkout a new owner has already created, disrupting its checks or merge.
findings.suggestion: Give attempts distinct worktree paths or otherwise ensure cleanup cannot remove a checkout owned by a newer claim.
findings.failure_scenario: A new owner reclaims an entry and recreates its worktree while the old worker awaits CI. The CI response returns, the old worker detects the lost claim, and its finally block removes the new owner's worktree.

verification.evidence: src/land/queue.ts:396–397 unconditionally runs `finally { await this.discard(repo, cwd); }`, including when claim validation throws. src/land/queue.ts:812 uses the owner-independent path `join(this.deps.paths.work, `land-${entry.id}`)`, and line 842 removes it with `rmSync(cwd, { recursive: true, force: true })`.
verification.trigger: The replacement owner recreates the same entry's checkout during the old worker's CI wait. When the old worker detects the reclaim, its finally block deletes the replacement checkout.

findings.title: Recheck ownership inside the merge helper before issuing the command
findings.detail: The request says a worker that lost its claim “issues no merge or push.” The ownership check before calling `mergePullRequest` does not cover its internal awaits: the helper awaits a fresh `gh pr view` and can also await reconciliation and retry operations before issuing `gh pr merge`. A reclaim during one of those awaits leaves the signal live until the next heartbeat, so the stale worker can still merge.
findings.suggestion: Pass an ownership guard into the helper and check it immediately before each merge attempt, including retries.
findings.failure_scenario: Pause the helper's PR view response, reclaim the entry with a new owner, then release the response before the old heartbeat fires; the old worker issues `gh pr merge`.

verification.evidence: src/git/repos.ts:1447 awaits the PR view response: `JSON.parse((await sh(view, { cwd, signal })).stdout)`. After validating its contents, lines 1461–1462 execute `gh pr merge` through `sh(cmd, ...)` without ownership validation. The caller's `this.assertClaim(entry.id)` at src/land/queue.ts:715 runs only after the helper completes.
verification.trigger: Pause the helper's view response, reclaim with another owner, and release a valid OPEN response before the next heartbeat. The old worker issues `gh pr merge` with its still-active signal.

findings.title: Recheck ownership immediately before the actual push
findings.detail: The request says a worker that lost its claim “issues no merge or push.” `pushExistingBranch` performs several asynchronous operations after the guarded checkpoint, including resolving the commit, reading the remote and checking ancestry, before starting the push. A reclaim during those operations is not detected until the heartbeat.
findings.suggestion: Provide an ownership guard to the push helper and invoke it immediately before starting the push.
findings.failure_scenario: Pause the helper's remote lookup after `pushedSha` is recorded, reclaim the entry, and release the lookup before the next heartbeat; the old worker pushes the merge commit.

verification.evidence: src/land/queue.ts:517-522 validates ownership while recording `pushedSha`, then calls `await pushExistingBranch(...)`. Inside that helper, src/git/repos.ts:1313 awaits `remoteSh(["git", "ls-remote", url, ref], ...)`, then at :1321 executes `await remoteSh([...BRANCH_PUSH, ...])` without rechecking claim ownership. Claim loss aborts the signal only on the heartbeat (src/land/queue.ts:306).
verification.trigger: Defer the helper's remote lookup after pushedSha is recorded, reclaim the entry, then release the lookup before the heartbeat. If the remote head still matches approvedSha, the former owner pushes the merge commit.

findings.title: Guard CI inspection writes after its internal awaits
findings.detail: The request says “a worker that lost the claim writes nothing.” Although `current` now checks ownership, `ciDecision` delegates to `inspectCi`, which writes default-branch CI feed and settings after awaited reads and only checks `current()` afterward. Its rerun response handler also writes the failure outcome after an awaited request without rechecking ownership.
findings.suggestion: Recheck ownership at each CI inspection write boundary, in the same transaction as the write.
findings.failure_scenario: Reclaim the entry while default-branch check data or a rerun response is deferred; releasing the response lets the old worker update CI settings, feed, or failure records.

verification.evidence: src/land/queue.ts:584-587 includes `this.store.ownsLandClaim(entry.id, this.owner)` in `current`, passed to ciDecision at :631-632. However, src/integrations/ci-classifier.ts:239 awaits `checks(mainSha)`, emits feed records at :258-264 and calls `store.setSetting(...)` at :267 before checking `current()` at :268. Likewise, :223 awaits the rerun response and :233 calls `store.finishCiFailure(f, "rerunning")` without checking current ownership.
verification.trigger: Reclaim while default-branch checks or a rerun response is deferred, then release the response before the heartbeat. The former owner updates CI settings/feed or failure records despite losing its claim.

findings.title: Do not discard a reclaimed worker's shared worktree
findings.detail: Every attempt for an entry uses the same `land-<id>` path. This also conflicts with the request's requirement that a worker that lost its claim writes nothing.
findings.suggestion: Give attempts separate worktree paths or otherwise ensure stale cleanup cannot remove a newer attempt's checkout.
findings.failure_scenario: The old worker is awaiting CI, another process reclaims the entry and creates its checkout, and the old CI response arrives; its `finally` removes the new worker's worktree.

verification.evidence: src/land/queue.ts:393 awaits CI, but :396-397 unconditionally runs `finally { await this.discard(repo, cwd); }`. verification.trigger: While the former owner awaits CI, another process reclaims the entry and recreates its checkout at the same path. Releasing the old CI response causes the ownership check to fail, but its finally block still deletes the new owner's checkout.

findings.title: PR numbers cannot target unowned pull requests
findings.detail: The existing CLI accepts a PR number or URL, but the unowned path accepts only a full GitHub URL. A valid number that has no matching factory run is rejected as "run not found", even when its repository is configured.
findings.suggestion: Resolve PR-number targets in the configured repository context, and report ambiguity when the repository cannot be determined.
findings.failure_scenario: Running `limitless land 7 --sha <full-head-sha>` for a hand-opened PR returns "run not found" instead of queuing it.

verification.evidence: src/cli/main.ts:573 forwards `target: sub` unchanged. src/land/queue.ts:184: `if (!run) return this.requestUnowned(input);`. Lines 226–227 require `/^https:\/\/github\.com\/([^/]+\/[^/]+)\/pull\/[1-9]\d*$/` and otherwise `throw new Error("run not found")`.
verification.trigger: `limitless land 7 --sha <full-head-sha>` with no owning factory run passes target `7`, fails the URL-only matcher, and returns `run not found`.

findings.title: Fork pull requests are categorically refused
findings.detail: The request covers open PRs on configured GitHub repositories without excluding PRs from forks. This check rejects every cross-repository PR before it can enter the queue, leaving that common class of hand-opened PR without the requested confined land path.
findings.suggestion: Support the head repository when fetching and updating the approved branch, while retaining the pinned-head and publication checks.
findings.failure_scenario: An open PR from a contributor's fork targets a configured repository and has the supplied current head SHA; the request fails with "cross-repository pull requests cannot be landed".

verification.evidence: src/land/queue.ts:251–252: `if (pr.state !== "OPEN") throw new Error(...)`; `if (pr.isCrossRepository) throw new Error("cross-repository pull requests cannot be landed");`. This precedes SHA approval at line 258.
verification.trigger: An unowned, open fork PR targeting a configured repository is rejected even when the supplied SHA matches its current head.

findings.title: Rollback blocks active unowned land entries
findings.detail: Unowned entries are stored with an empty run ID in the existing queue table. After a rollback, the previous release claims these entries and requires that ID to resolve to a run; it instead marks them blocked as "run  is gone". This loses the active land's progress, including a possible already-pushed base merge, rather than preserving it for the newer release.
findings.suggestion: Keep entries that the previous release cannot process out of its claimable queue, with a migration and resume strategy that preserves active work across rollback.
findings.failure_scenario: An unowned land is queued or waiting for CI when the daemon rolls back to the base release. The older queue claims the entry and permanently marks it blocked because no run has ID "".

verification.evidence: HEAD src/db/store.ts:2721 stores an unowned entry as `entry.runId ?? ""`. At base 381e4384, src/db/store.ts:100 reads `run_id AS runId`; src/land/queue.ts:153 resumes active entries, and src/db/store.ts:2784-2785 permits claiming queued or expired waiting_ci entries. Base src/land/queue.ts:819-821 executes `this.store.getRun(entry.runId)` and throws `run ${entry.runId} is gone` when absent. Its catch at :327 calls `this.block(...)`, which at :912 persists `this.finish(id, "blocked", reason)`.
verification.trigger: Queue an unowned land, then roll back to the base release while it is queued or waiting for CI. Once claimable, the old queue reads runId "", fails its run lookup, and persistently blocks the entry with "run  is gone"; upgrading again does not automatically resume it.

findings.title: Bare PR numbers cannot request an unowned land
findings.detail: The existing CLI accepts a PR number, and the request asks for `limitless land <pr> --sha <full sha>`, but the new path accepts only a complete GitHub URL. An unowned PR has no run through which the preceding lookup can resolve its number.
findings.suggestion: Resolve a PR number to a configured repository and canonical PR URL, refusing clearly if the repository is ambiguous.
findings.failure_scenario: `limitless land 77 --sha <current-full-sha>` returns `run not found` even when PR 77 is open on the configured repository.

verification.evidence: src/land/queue.ts:183–184 resolves an owning run, then calls `this.requestUnowned(input)` when absent. Lines 226–227 match only a full GitHub PR URL and otherwise `throw new Error("run not found")`.
verification.trigger: `limitless land 77 --sha <current-full-sha>` for an unowned PR fails before GitHub lookup because `77` is not a full URL.

findings.title: Open fork PRs are categorically refused
findings.detail: The request covers open PRs on configured GitHub repositories and does not exclude PRs whose head is in a fork. This check rejects every such PR before attempting the land, leaving a common class of hand-opened PRs outside the feature.
findings.suggestion: Support the fork head repository throughout checkout and any required base-merge push, or explicitly resolve this restriction against the requested scope.
findings.failure_scenario: An open PR targeting a configured repository from a contributor's fork is rejected with `cross-repository pull requests cannot be landed`, even with its exact current SHA.

verification.evidence: src/land/queue.ts:252: `if (pr.isCrossRepository) throw new Error("cross-repository pull requests cannot be landed");`. test/land-queue.test.ts:3282 explicitly expects rejection for `{ isCrossRepository: true }`.

findings.title: Rollback blocks active unowned lands
findings.detail: The empty-string sentinel keeps the old schema writable, but the previous release reads it as a run ID and requires that run to exist. After a rollback, its queue claims an unowned entry and blocks it as a missing run instead of resuming it. This violates the requirement that the previous release remain working across deploy rollback.
findings.suggestion: Provide a rollback-compatible representation and processing strategy for active unowned entries, or prevent the previous release from claiming entries it cannot process.
findings.failure_scenario: An unowned land is waiting for CI when deployment rolls back; the previous daemon claims it, looks up run `""`, and marks the entry blocked because the run is gone.

verification.evidence: HEAD src/db/store.ts:2721 writes `entry.runId ?? ""`. Base 381e4384 src/db/store.ts:100 exposes that value through `run_id AS runId`, and :2784-2785 claims waiting_ci entries with released or expired claims. Base src/land/queue.ts:819-821 requires an existing run and throws `run ${entry.runId} is gone`; :327 invokes `this.block(...)`, and :912 saves `this.finish(id, "blocked", reason)`.
verification.trigger: Roll back while an unowned land is waiting for CI. When the previous daemon claims the entry, its lookup for run "" fails and it saves a terminal blocked state instead of preserving the land for resumption.

findings.title: Blocked unowned lands disappear from the CLI digest
findings.detail: The new feed entries have a null run ID, but the digest removes every feed item without a run ID before checking whether a blocked land is actionable. Operators relying on the digest therefore do not see these failures, despite the land feed containing them.
findings.suggestion: Teach the digest to resolve unowned land entries by PR URL or land ID and display their current blocked state.
findings.failure_scenario: A confined check fails for an unowned PR; its `land.blocked` feed item exists, but `limitless digest` omits it from blocked lands.

verification.evidence: src/land/queue.ts:260 creates unowned entries with `runId: null`. src/db/store.ts:2853–2854 emits feed items with `kind` and `runId: entry.runId`. src/cli/digest.ts:89–91: `if (!item.runId) { group.items.delete(key); continue; }`.

findings.title: Revalidate the PR base before landing

The queue can run checks from one base and then squash-merge into another, violating the requirement that the destination base's checks govern the land.

This rejects every cross-repository PR, even when its base repository is configured and its head SHA is explicitly approved. Hand-made contributions from forks therefore cannot use the confined land queue.
findings.suggestion: Support fetching and safely pinning fork heads, or explicitly narrow the accepted PR scope.
findings.failure_scenario: A contributor opens a PR from their fork against a configured repository and requests landing with its full current head SHA; the request fails with "cross-repository pull requests cannot be landed".

findings.title: Unowned PRs cannot be requested by PR number

findings.failure_scenario: `limitless land 7 --sha <current-full-sha>` for an unowned PR on the configured repository fails before looking up the PR.

findings.title: Rollback permanently blocks an in-flight runless land
findings.detail: The request requires compatibility with the previous release. A runless entry is persisted with an empty run ID, but the previous release resumes active entries by looking up that ID and blocks the entry when no run exists. If a deployment rolls back while such a land is queued or in progress, the old daemon changes it to blocked instead of preserving it for the newer release to resume.
findings.suggestion: Make runless entries invisible to the previous release's active queue, or otherwise provide a rollback-compatible persistence and resume mechanism.
findings.failure_scenario: A runless land is waiting for CI when the daemon rolls back to the base release; on startup the old queue claims it and blocks it with "run  is gone".

candidates.title: Rollback blocks active unowned land entries
candidates.detail: Unowned entries are stored with an empty run ID in the existing queue table. After a rollback, the previous release claims these entries and requires that ID to resolve to a run; it instead marks them blocked as "run  is gone". This loses the active land's progress, including a possible already-pushed base merge, rather than preserving it for the newer release.
candidates.suggestion: Keep entries that the previous release cannot process out of its claimable queue, with a migration and resume strategy that preserves active work across rollback.
candidates.failure_scenario: An unowned land is queued or waiting for CI when the daemon rolls back to the base release. The older queue claims the entry and permanently marks it blocked because no run has ID "".

candidates.title: Open fork PRs are categorically refused
candidates.detail: The request covers open PRs on configured GitHub repositories and does not exclude PRs whose head is in a fork. This check rejects every such PR before attempting the land, leaving a common class of hand-opened PRs outside the feature.

candidates.title: Rollback blocks active unowned lands
candidates.detail: The empty-string sentinel keeps the old schema writable, but the previous release reads it as a run ID and requires that run to exist. After a rollback, its queue claims an unowned entry and blocks it as a missing run instead of resuming it. candidates.title: Revalidate the PR base before landing

candidates.suggestion: Re-read and validate the PR's base branch before the merge, and block if it differs from the branch used for the base merge and checks. Ensure the validation is tied as closely as possible to the merge operation.

findings.title: Runless land test does not exercise actual confinement
findings.detail: The test named for a confined land injects `recordingConfinement`, whose `wrap` returns the command unchanged and whose `verify` only records a call. It therefore passes even if the runless gate executes without an effective sandbox, leaving the central confined-check requirement without an end-to-end regression test.
findings.suggestion: Add a platform-appropriate real-confinement test for a runless land that proves a forbidden operation is denied and an allowed operation succeeds.
findings.failure_scenario: The runless land gate invokes its command outside Seatbelt while still calling the fake backend's `verify`; this test reports success.

verification.evidence: test/land-queue.test.ts:299 injects `confinement: landConfinement.backend`; test/confinement.ts:8–11 defines `verify` as only `calls.push({ roots, opts })` and `wrap: (cmd) => cmd`. The test's confinement assertion at test/land-queue.test.ts:3241 is only `expect(landConfinement.calls.length).toBeGreaterThan(0)`. Actual execution uses `cmd: backend.wrap(payload.cmd, roots)` at src/harness/sandbox.ts:316.
verification.trigger: The runless gate executes without a Seatbelt wrapper while calling the fake backend's verify method; the call-count assertion passes and the test reports success without establishing actual confinement.

findings.title: Revalidate the PR base before merging
findings.detail: The queue records the base branch at request time and uses it to select the base commit and its gate configuration, but the merge path only revalidates the head SHA. GitHub permits a PR to be retargeted without changing its head. A retargeted PR can therefore merge into a branch whose base and checks were never used for the land.
findings.suggestion: Confirm the current PR base still matches the checked branch before publication and merge, and block if it changes.
findings.failure_scenario: An unowned PR is queued against main, then retargeted to release while its head remains unchanged. The queue checks main's configuration and head, then GitHub merges the PR into release.

verification.evidence: src/land/queue.ts:264 persists `baseBranch: pr.baseRefName`; line 430 subsequently calls `fetchBase(..., entry.baseBranch, ...)`. Base resolution runs only when the stored base is missing or equals the head (line 417). src/git/repos.ts:1463 fetches only `title,body,headRefOid,state`, and lines 1476–1478 merge using `--match-head-commit` without validating the PR base.
verification.trigger: Queue against main, then retarget the PR to release without moving its head → checks use the stored main base, while GitHub can merge into release.

findings.failure_scenario: A user runs `limitless land 604 --sha <current-full-sha>` for an open PR that no factory run opened; the request fails with `run not found`.

findings.title: Rollback blocks active unowned lands
findings.detail: The request requires compatibility with the previous release. An unowned entry is persisted with an empty run ID, but the previous release's land queue requires every entry to resolve to a run. If a deploy rolls back while such an entry is active, the old daemon resumes it, fails to find run "", and blocks it instead of continuing the land.
findings.suggestion: Provide a rollback-compatible representation and resume strategy for active unowned entries.
findings.failure_scenario: An unowned land is waiting for CI when the new release is rolled back; the previous daemon claims the entry and marks it blocked because its run is gone.

verification.evidence: HEAD src/db/store.ts:2721 stores an unowned land with `entry.runId ?? ""`. At base 381e4384, src/land/queue.ts:348–349 calls `this.context(entry)` before handling any recorded push. Its :819–821 throws when `this.store.getRun(entry.runId)` finds no run; :327 calls `this.block(...)`, and :912 persists `"blocked"`. Base src/db/store.ts:2784 explicitly includes `waiting_ci` among reclaimable states.
verification.trigger: An unowned land is waiting for CI when rollback occurs. On reclaim, the previous daemon fails its run lookup before resuming CI and marks the entry blocked.

findings.failure_scenario: A user queues a hand-made PR and opens the UI to check whether it landed or was blocked; the entry is not displayed.

verification.evidence: src/land/queue.ts:259–260 creates the entry with `runId: null`. ui/store.ts:93–97 hydrates only `deps.listRuns({ limit: 200 }), deps.getProviders(), deps.getAlerts()`. ui/pages/Dashboard.tsx:49 derives displayed records from `Object.values(live.runs)`, and :148 renders `<RunsTable runs={filteredRuns()} />`. ui/main.tsx:39–47 registers run and other existing pages but no land queue page; there is no land-entry fetch or renderer in ui/.

findings.title: A crash during discovery leaves unrecorded descendants running
findings.detail: Cleanup persists members one at a time, but recovery only examines persisted members and never resumes marker discovery. If the daemon crashes while reading or recording the initial snapshot, or after freezing a snapshot but before discovering a newly forked descendant, any unrecorded descendants survive. Recovery deletes the partial record and permits the next invocation to start, even though those descendants can still write to the checkout.
findings.suggestion: Persist enough invocation-level discovery state before cleanup begins to resume discovery after a crash, and retain the record until the complete marked set is confirmed gone.
findings.failure_scenario: An invocation has two marked sleepers. The daemon records the first PID and dies while inspecting the second. On restart, recovery kills the first, deletes the record, and starts the next command while the second sleeper remains running.

verification.evidence: src/util/proc.ts:386–400 processes candidates sequentially: `const birth = await readBirth(pid)` followed by `recordMember(pid, birth)`. Recovery only visits persisted members at src/util/proc.ts:64: `store.pendingProcessCleanups().filter((r) => r.invocation === invocation)`, then clears the invocation at line 78: `store.completeProcessCleanup(invocation)`.
verification.trigger: Crash after recording the first sleeper but before recording the second. Recovery kills only the first and clears its record; it never rediscovers the second, allowing subsequent commands while that sleeper remains running.

findings.title: Linux birth identities can match unrelated processes after reboot
findings.detail: On Linux, processBirth returns only the `/proc/<pid>/stat` start-time tick count, which is relative to boot. Persisted records survive reboot, so an unrelated process can have both the same PID and the same boot-relative start tick. Recovery then treats it as the recorded member and sends SIGKILL despite it belonging to a different boot.
findings.suggestion: Include a boot identity in persisted Linux process identities and require it to match before signalling.
findings.failure_scenario: A pending record survives a machine reboot; a new process receives the recorded PID and starts at the same tick after boot. Daemon startup kills that unrelated process.

verification.evidence: src/util/proc.ts:312–319 reads `/proc/${pid}/stat` and returns only `fields[19]`, the boot-relative start tick. Recovery at src/util/proc.ts:66–68 checks `if ((await readBirth(member.pid)) !== member.birth) continue` before `process.kill(member.pid, "SIGKILL")`. No boot identity is included.
verification.trigger: After reboot, an unrelated process has the persisted PID and the same start tick. Its identity compares equal, so startup recovery signals the unrelated process.

findings.title: Recovery clears the record without discovering descendants created during cleanup
findings.detail: The live sweep freezes its currently claimed processes and then rescans because a process can fork between discovery and being frozen. If the daemon crashes after the first freeze but before that rescan, the new descendant has no persisted record. Recovery kills only recorded members and deletes the invocation's records, so it permits the next command while that descendant remains running in the checkout.
findings.suggestion: Persist enough invocation discovery information to resume the marked-process sweep and confirm it is empty before clearing the cleanup record.
findings.failure_scenario: A marked parent forks a sleeper after the initial scan; the daemon dies immediately after freezing the parent. On restart, recovery kills the recorded parent, clears the record, and leaves the unrecorded sleeper able to write to the checkout.

verification.evidence: src/util/proc.ts:407 explicitly relies on another scan: `Freeze every newly discovered member, then rescan before killing the frozen set.` However, recovery at src/util/proc.ts:64 iterates only persisted members and at line 78 calls `store.completeProcessCleanup(invocation)` without scanning for descendants.
verification.trigger: A parent forks after the scan and is frozen before its new child is discovered. A crash then prevents the live rescan. Recovery kills the recorded parent and clears the record, leaving its unrecorded child running.

findings.title: A failed ownership write can leave a running child with no durable cleanup
findings.detail: When the first record write fails, ownershipWriteFailed suppresses the direct-child kill and no cleanup record exists. The current run fails, but a daemon restart has nothing to recover or block on, allowing a resumed invocation to run alongside the surviving child. The same problem can leave an unrecorded member after a later write failure.
findings.suggestion: Ensure a durable unresolved invocation exists before cleanup can encounter member-write failures, and retain enough information to recover its unrecorded members.
findings.failure_scenario: A timeout begins cleanup while the child is still running, and SQLite rejects the first ownership insert. The child continues running; after the database becomes writable and the daemon restarts, recovery finds no record and the next step starts.

verification.evidence: src/util/proc.ts:618–620 sets `ownershipWriteFailed = true` and throws when persistence fails; line 701 guards fallback signalling with `!ownershipWriteFailed`. test/process-cleanup.test.ts:265–267 confirms the child remains alive and the current scope blocks another command. engine.ts:295–298 subsequently persists `needsHumanReason`, and lines 222–229 block resume when that state exists; a crash or database failure before this persistence leaves no durable block.
verification.trigger: The first ownership insert fails while the child runs, followed by a crash before the engine saves its cleanup block, or a database failure that also prevents that save. Once the database recovers, restart has neither an ownership record nor a persisted block, so subsequent work can start alongside the surviving child. A successfully persisted engine block prevents ordinary resume.

findings.title: Checkout blocking compares exact working directories
findings.detail: The request says “A resumed invocation must not start in a checkout whose previous cleanup is unresolved.” Records store the individual command's cwd, but recovery selects another run's records only when that cwd exactly equals the new command's cwd or the run's worktree path. Commands in different directories of the same checkout therefore do not block one another after recovery fails.
findings.suggestion: Associate cleanup records with the canonical checkout root and select unresolved records by that root on every run and invocation entry point.
findings.failure_scenario: A previous invocation ran in checkout/subdir and its identity inspection still fails. A different run or invocation starts in checkout or checkout/other; the record does not match its cwd, so work starts despite the unresolved cleanup.

findings.detail: The new publication diagnostic passes a Git-controlled path to `redactCredentials` without decoding it first. These diagnostics can be stored as events or sent back to an implementer.
findings.suggestion: Decode supported filename encodings before credential redaction, or suppress the filename when its decoded forms contain a credential. Apply the same handling to both audit findings and publication diagnostics.

A percent-encoded credential in a path survives redactCredentials, and redactPrivate does not remove it unless it is also in the private-string list. The resulting publication error exposes the recoverable credential. The new test covers only a literal credential in the path.
candidates.suggestion: Decode or otherwise recognize encoded credential variants before emitting the path, and add a test using a percent-encoded registered credential.
candidates.failure_scenario: A file whose name contains a percent-encoded registered credential has content that triggers the decoding refusal; the error includes the encoded credential.

candidates.title: Identify files whose patch has no index line
candidates.detail: The diagnostic maps a patch section to a path only through its index line. Git omits that line for an empty-file addition and some mode-only changes, so a decoding refusal caused by such a filename falls through to the original generic error without a commit or path. The added tests exercise nonempty files and do not cover this case.
candidates.suggestion: Associate sections with raw diff records even when there is no index line, and test an empty file with a filename that exceeds the decoding limit.
candidates.failure_scenario: A commit adds an empty file whose name contains sufficiently nested percent encoding. Publication is refused, but the error remains 'Published content exceeds the private text decoding limit' without identifying the commit or path.

candidates.title: Encoded credentials in diagnosed paths escape redaction
candidates.detail: The new diagnostic passes the raw filename to `redactCredentials`, which only matches literal credential variants. `redactPrivate` checks encoded forms only against the private-strings entries, not registered credentials. The same issue affects the new audit filename handling in `src/gates/audit.ts`. An encoded credential can therefore be stored in an audit event, sent in round feedback, or included in a publication refusal.
candidates.suggestion: Decode or otherwise recognize encoded credential variants before emitting filenames, and redact the complete diagnostic before it reaches logs, events, or prompts. Cover both audit feedback and publication refusals.
candidates.failure_scenario: A registered credential `secret-token-value` appears in an added filename as `%73ecret-token-value`. A scratch warning or decoding-limit refusal includes that filename unchanged, disclosing a readily decodable credential.

candidates.title: Publication diagnostics preserve terminal control characters in filenames
candidates.detail: The diagnosed path is inserted into the refusal without stripping terminal control characters. Git permits such characters in filenames, so untrusted filenames can inject control sequences or forged lines into displayed or logged errors. The audit path uses `redactGateOutput`, which strips these characters, but the new publication diagnostic does not.
candidates.suggestion: Apply terminal-control normalization to the path before including it in the diagnostic, while retaining credential and private-string redaction.
candidates.failure_scenario: An added file whose name contains a newline or ANSI escape sequence also contains content exceeding the decoding limit. The resulting refusal displays the untrusted control sequence as part of its message.

candidates.title: Scratch warnings do not reach the implementer when the round otherwise passes
candidates.detail: The request says to “Feed it back to the implementer as round feedback, so the next round removes it before anything is published.” The warning is appended only when a later implementer invocation already happens. If gates, review, and verification pass, the run proceeds toward publication without giving the implementer a chance to remove the scratch file. The new approve-case test explicitly expects only one implementer invocation.
candidates.suggestion: Arrange an advisory follow-up that gives the implementer the warning before publication while allowing intentional additions to remain.
candidates.failure_scenario: The first round adds .tmp-gate/report.xml and all other checks pass; the warning is recorded, but the file remains in the commit and the implementer never receives it.

candidates.title: A file moved into a root hidden directory receives no warning
candidates.detail: The request calls for a warning when a round “adds files under a hidden directory at the checkout root.” Git's rename detection reports a move into that directory as R rather than A, so the status check skips the newly introduced hidden-directory path.
candidates.suggestion: Also inspect rename destinations that introduce a path beneath a root hidden directory.
candidates.failure_scenario: A round moves report.xml to .tmp-gate/report.xml; the diff reports R100 and no root-hidden-addition warning is produced.

findings.title: Publication checks omit registered credentials
findings.detail: The new base64 decoder only checks the entries supplied by callers. Production publication callers generally supply private strings, not registered credentials, so encoded credentials in published content remain undetected. The new test supplies credentials explicitly and therefore does not exercise the production call path.
findings.suggestion: Include registered credentials in the protected values used by publication checks, and test through a production publication entry point.

findings.suggestion: Inspect bounded successive decoding layers for eligible base64 runs before deciding that a run is unrelated, and cover nested encodings in filename and publication tests.

findings.title: Review eval calls are attributed to one provider and counted as one invocation
findings.detail: Review systems can invoke several finders, samples, and verifiers, including models on different providers. Their trial totals combine those calls, but the fallback creates one record using the trial's primary provider and model. This assigns other providers' tokens and costs to the primary provider and undercounts invocations.
findings.suggestion: Aggregate individual stored call evidence where available, and represent unattributable combined work explicitly rather than assigning it all to the primary provider.
findings.failure_scenario: A review eval calls provider A as its primary reviewer and provider B as a verifier. The report shows one invocation and the combined spend under A, with no invocation or spend under B.

verification.evidence: src/pipeline/review.ts:926 returns 'result: combined(results, last, { ...decision.review, panel })'; combined sums costs and usage at src/pipeline/review.ts:541–547. src/evals/runner.ts:641 sets 'trial.details.provider = model.provider'. src/db/stats.ts:269–275 attributes the trial's complete tokens and costs to 'provider: details.provider' and 'modelId: String(t.model_id)'; src/db/stats.ts:179 counts 'invocations: rows.length'.
verification.trigger: A review eval invokes reviewer A and verifier B. Their combined usage becomes one trial record attributed to A, producing one reported invocation and no attributed work for B.

findings.title: Implementation evals lose stored cache token totals
findings.detail: Every eval with rounds is assigned null cache-read and cache-write tokens, even when the trial contains those accumulated measurements and has only one round. Because the summation returns null if any row is unknown, one implementation eval also makes the corresponding provider totals unknown.
findings.suggestion: Use the stored trial cache totals when they can be attributed, including single-round trials, and preserve known aggregate totals where per-round splits cannot be recovered.
findings.failure_scenario: A single-round implementation trial stores 100 cache-read tokens and 20 cache-write tokens. Its model and provider statistics report both values as null, including when it is the only eval for that provider.

verification.evidence: src/evals/runner.ts:1143–1144 accumulates 'trial.details.cacheReadTokens' and 'trial.details.cacheWriteTokens'; src/evals/runner.ts:1173–1175 records rounds for implementation cases, even with one round. src/db/stats.ts:280–281 explicitly uses 'rounds?.length ? null' for both cache metrics.
verification.trigger: A single-round implementation trial stores cache-read 100 and cache-write 20. Its nonempty rounds array causes both reported cache metrics to become null.

findings.title: Eval round totals attribute multiple provider calls to one model
findings.detail: A recorded eval round can include retries or panel calls, but its stored tokens and costs are the combined trial delta while its provider and model identify the round target. Treating that round as one invocation assigns all of the combined work to that target and omits the other calls from their providers and models.
findings.suggestion: Use individually attributed call records where available; otherwise expose the attribution as unknown rather than presenting combined spend as belonging to the target.
findings.failure_scenario: An eval panel calls a reviewer on provider A and a verifier on provider B. The resulting round reports both calls' cost and tokens under A and reports no work for B.

verification.evidence: src/pipeline/review.ts:541–547 sums all panel calls' costs and tokens, and :926 returns that combined result. src/evals/runner.ts:1139–1142 adds it to trial totals. src/db/stats.ts:265–275 selects rounds or a trial fallback with 'provider: details.provider', 'modelId: String(t.model_id)', and the complete trial costs and tokens. Review panels use this trial fallback: src/evals/runner.ts:1173–1175 only persists rounds when '"hidden" in item'.
verification.trigger: Reviewer A and verifier B participate in a review eval panel. All panel costs and tokens are reported under A's model, with none under B. This duplicates C1's attribution defect; the stored aggregate is a trial rather than a review round.

findings.title: Discarding eval cache splits makes available totals unknown
findings.detail: When rounds exist, the code forces cache-read and cache-write values to null even though the enclosing trial stores accumulated cacheReadTokens and cacheWriteTokens. Consequently a single ordinary multi-round trial makes its provider's aggregate cache and uncached input totals null, despite those totals being available in stored data.
findings.suggestion: Preserve trial-level cache totals for aggregates that can be attributed accurately, and mark only unavailable per-round breakdowns unknown.
findings.failure_scenario: A completed multi-round eval has cacheReadTokens and cacheWriteTokens in its details. Its eval totals nevertheless return null for both cache metrics and inputTokens.

verification.evidence: src/evals/runner.ts:1143–1144 preserves aggregate cache-read/write totals in trial.details. src/db/stats.ts:280–281 discards these whenever rounds exist: 'const read = rounds?.length ? null : (details.cacheReadTokens ?? null)' and the equivalent write expression. src/db/stats.ts:291 consequently sets inputTokens to null; :171–173 propagates null measurements into aggregate totals.
verification.trigger: A completed multi-round eval has stored cache totals. Its round records all receive null cache metrics and inputTokens, so provider eval totals also return null despite available trial-level totals.

findings.title: Count a running eval trial before any provider invocation exists
findings.detail: A running trial with no recorded rounds is converted into a workload record even when it is still preparing and has no invocation status or usage. This silently reports an invocation and an unsuccessful share for work that may never reach a provider.
findings.suggestion: Only count a trial fallback when persisted evidence establishes that a provider call occurred; represent in-progress preparation separately if needed.
findings.failure_scenario: An eval trial is persisted as running while its workspace is being prepared, with zero usage and no rounds or invocationStatus. The statistics report one failed eval invocation before any model call.

verification.evidence: src/evals/runner.ts:931 persists `store.recordEvalTrial({ ...trial, status: "running" })` before invoking the harness. src/db/stats.ts:246 selects trials with `t.status != 'queued'`; its exclusion at :258 covers only `t.status === "skipped" || details.preparationFailed`. The fallback at :271 uses `details.invocationStatus ?? String(t.status)`, and :179-180 counts every row while treating only `"ok"` as successful.
verification.trigger: A newly running trial has zero usage and no rounds or invocationStatus before the harness call starts → one eval invocation with successfulShare 0. The running checkpoint occurs after initial workspace preparation, but still before the provider call.

findings.title: Eval successful share can reflect grading failures instead of provider results
findings.detail: For implementation evals, the runner can change a round's status from `ok` to `error` or `timeout` when grading fails, even though the provider invocation succeeded. This aggregation uses that modified round status as the provider invocation status, understating the successful share.
findings.suggestion: Preserve and aggregate the provider invocation status separately from the grading outcome.
findings.failure_scenario: An implementation model returns successfully, but its grading process times out. The eval provider statistics count the invocation as unsuccessful.

verification.evidence: src/evals/runner.ts:1208-1212 explicitly changes a successful provider round's status: `if (result.status === "ok" && (grade?.implement?.reason === "error" || grade?.implement?.reason === "timeout")) roundEvidence.status = grade.implement.reason`. src/db/stats.ts:265-266 chooses stored rounds, :287 uses `status: r.status`, and :180 counts success only for `r.status === "ok"`.
verification.trigger: An implementation provider returns ok, then grading times out → the stored round has status timeout and provider successfulShare reports failure.

findings.title: Eval aggregation tests do not exercise runner-produced round evidence
findings.detail: The eval test constructs round records directly and assumes their status and duration describe provider calls. The runner can modify round status after grading and records duration through grading, so this fixture does not catch the resulting misclassification of provider success.
findings.suggestion: Add a test using runner-produced eval evidence where the provider succeeds but grading fails or times out, and assert the provider success share.
findings.failure_scenario: A regression or existing defect that treats a grading timeout as a failed provider invocation passes the manually seeded round test.

verification.evidence: test/provider-workload.test.ts:465–482 manually constructs rounds with `status: "ok"` and `status: "timeout"`. src/evals/runner.ts:1209–1212 overwrites successful invocation evidence on grading failure: `result.status === "ok" && (grade?.implement?.reason === "error" || grade?.implement?.reason === "timeout")` → `roundEvidence.status = grade.implement.reason`. src/db/stats.ts:265–266 selects those rounds, :287 uses `status: r.status`, and :180 computes successful share using `r.status === "ok"`.
verification.trigger: An eval provider invocation succeeds, then hidden-test or gate grading times out. The runner stores the round as timeout, so provider statistics count the successful call as unsuccessful. The manually seeded aggregation test does not exercise this runner-to-statistics path.

findings.title: Multi-call eval trials are attributed to one provider and counted as one invocation
findings.detail: The request asks for workload “per provider and model” with “eval invocations shown separately.” A review eval can invoke multiple panel members or samples, including providers other than the trial target. The runner combines their usage and costs into the trial, but this code attributes the entire combined record to the trial target and counts it once. The resulting provider, model, invocation-count, and success figures are misleading.
findings.suggestion: Aggregate individual persisted call evidence where available, and explicitly represent measurements that cannot be attributed from existing records rather than assigning all combined usage to the target.
findings.failure_scenario: A panel eval invokes a target on provider A and a verifier on provider B. Its combined cost and tokens are reported as one invocation for A, while B receives no eval workload.

verification.evidence: src/evals/runner.ts:1115 invokes the selected verifier through `sendTo(request, to, ...)`. src/pipeline/review.ts:926 returns `result: combined(results, last, ...)`; :541-547 sums all member costs and tokens. src/evals/runner.ts:1139-1142 adds that combined usage to the trial. src/db/stats.ts:269-275 attributes the fallback record entirely to `details.provider` and `t.model_id`.
verification.trigger: A panel trial calls a target on provider A and a verifier on B → their combined usage becomes one trial record attributed to A; B receives no corresponding eval workload.

findings.title: Eval rounds discard stored cached-token totals
findings.detail: The request requires input, output, and cached-token statistics. For every trial with rounds, this code sets both cache fields to null even though the runner accumulates cacheReadTokens and cacheWriteTokens on the trial. Because summarize returns null when any contributing value is unknown, one such trial makes the entire provider's eval cache and uncached-input totals unknown.
findings.suggestion: Use the stored trial-level cache totals for aggregations where they can be attributed without double counting, and preserve unknown values only for breakdowns that cannot be reconstructed.
findings.failure_scenario: An implement eval has one recorded round and stored cacheReadTokens of 500. Its provider's eval totals report cacheReadTokens and inputTokens as null instead of reporting the available values.

verification.evidence: src/evals/runner.ts:1143-1144 stores cumulative `trial.details.cacheReadTokens` and `cacheWriteTokens`. src/db/stats.ts:280-281 nevertheless sets `const read = rounds?.length ? null : ...` and likewise for write; :291 then makes inputTokens null whenever either cache value is null.
verification.trigger: A single-round implementation eval stores cacheReadTokens 500 and cacheWriteTokens 0 → historical cache totals and uncached inputTokens become null despite the available, unambiguous trial totals.

findings.title: Historical workload omits stored concierge calls
findings.detail: The request asks for long-term provider workload numbers computed from stored invocations. Historical production reads only the invocations table, while stored concierge calls live in chat_calls and are already counted by the existing provider workload calculation. Consequently the new long-term provider and model totals omit that work even when a provider appears in the legacy today and seven-day fields.
findings.suggestion: Include stored chat calls in the historical workload with an appropriate role and their stored model, status, usage, cost, and duration.
findings.failure_scenario: A provider has a completed concierge call and no pipeline invocations. Its existing today count is one, but the new production totals report zero invocations and zero usage.

verification.evidence: src/concierge.ts:331 persists completed concierge calls with `store.recordChatCall(...)`; src/db/store.ts:1015 inserts their results into `chat_calls`. src/db/stats.ts:80 includes that table in existing workload counts, but :241 sources historical production records exclusively from `invocations`, and :312 computes production solely from those records.
verification.trigger: A provider has a completed concierge call today and no pipeline invocations → today.invocations is 1 while historical production reports zero invocations and usage, omitting stored provider work.
