findings.title: Multi-provider eval costs are attributed to the trial's provider
findings.detail: Review panels can invoke finders and verifiers on different providers and models. The runner combines their usage and costs into the trial totals, but this code assigns all of those totals to details.provider and the trial model. The resulting provider and model workload numbers can therefore charge one provider for work performed by another.
findings.suggestion: Attribute calls from the stored per-call evidence where available; represent an unresolvable split as unknown rather than assigning the combined amount to one provider.
findings.failure_scenario: A review trial targets provider A but also invokes a verifier on provider B. The full combined token count and cost appear under A, while B receives none.

verification.evidence: src/pipeline/review.ts:541-547 sums panel costs and usage: `costUsd: sum((r) => r.costUsd)` and `input: sum((r) => r.usage.input)`. src/evals/runner.ts:1139-1142 adds that combined result to trial totals. src/db/stats.ts:269-275 attributes those totals to `provider: details.provider`, using `tokensIn: Number(t.tokens_in)` and `costUsd: Number(t.cost_usd)`.
verification.trigger: A review trial targeting provider A also calls provider B. The combined trial tokens and costs are attributed to A; B receives no corresponding workload.

findings.title: Implementation evals discard stored cache token totals
findings.detail: Every eval with round evidence forces both cache measurements to null, even though the runner accumulates cacheReadTokens and cacheWriteTokens on the trial. Consequently, a normal implementation eval makes the corresponding provider totals unknown, including when the trial has only one round and its cache split is unambiguous.
findings.suggestion: Use the stored trial cache totals where they can be attributed, and preserve them at an appropriate aggregate level when individual rounds cannot be split.
findings.failure_scenario: A single-round implementation trial records 100 cache-read tokens and 20 cache-write tokens. Its eval statistics report both as null, as do the containing provider totals.

verification.evidence: src/evals/runner.ts:1143-1144 persists `trial.details.cacheReadTokens` and `trial.details.cacheWriteTokens`; src/evals/runner.ts:1173-1175 stores implementation rounds. src/db/stats.ts:280-281 explicitly discards the trial cache totals whenever rounds exist: `const read = rounds?.length ? null : (details.cacheReadTokens ?? null)` and the equivalent for write. src/db/stats.ts:171-172 propagates null into aggregate sums.
verification.trigger: A single-round implementation trial stores 100 cache-read and 20 cache-write tokens. Both metrics become null in its eval statistics and containing provider totals.

findings.title: Recorded rounds are reported as individual invocations
findings.detail: A round can contain multiple provider calls: the runner retries a failed resumed session within the same round and sums both calls into one round record. Counting each round as one invocation understates workload and its success share reflects only the final result, despite the API naming the field invocations.
findings.suggestion: Count individual calls when evidence supports it, or expose round counts separately without presenting them as invocation counts or invocation success rates.
findings.failure_scenario: An implementation round makes a failed resumed call followed by a successful fresh call. Statistics report one successful invocation instead of two calls with one failure.

verification.evidence: src/evals/runner.ts:1146-1150 retries an errored resumed call by clearing `sessionId` and executing `continue`. src/evals/runner.ts:1164 records only the final `status: result.status`, and :1175 pushes one `roundEvidence`. src/db/stats.ts:265-266 uses those rounds as records; :179-180 computes `invocations: rows.length` and successful share from each record's final status.
verification.trigger: One implementation round makes a failed resumed call followed by a successful fresh call. Statistics report one invocation with successfulShare 1 instead of two calls with successfulShare 0.5.

findings.title: Combined eval calls are attributed to one provider and counted as one invocation
findings.detail: For evals without recorded implementation rounds, the fallback treats the entire trial as one provider invocation. Review panels and sampled reviews can make multiple calls, including calls to other providers, while the runner combines their usage into the trial totals. This assigns all of that usage to the trial target and omits the other providers' calls, so provider and model workload numbers are wrong.
findings.suggestion: Aggregate per-call evidence where it is persisted, and make unavailable attribution explicit rather than assigning combined usage to a single provider.
findings.failure_scenario: An eval review panel calls a finder on provider A and a verifier on provider B. The report counts one invocation and assigns both calls' tokens and cost to A; B receives no workload.

verification.evidence: src/evals/runner.ts:1111-1115 selects a verifier target and calls `sendTo(request, to, ...)`. src/pipeline/review.ts:926 returns `result: combined(results, last, ...)`; :541-547 sums costs and tokens. src/db/stats.ts:267-277 creates one fallback record using `provider: details.provider` and trial totals, while :179 counts `invocations: rows.length`.
verification.trigger: An eval review panel calls a finder on A and a verifier on B. Statistics count one invocation and assign both calls' tokens and costs to A, omitting B's workload.

findings.title: Missing durations are reported as zero total wall time
findings.detail: The duration aggregation silently drops unknown durations and returns the sum of the remaining values. If every duration is unknown, it reports zero milliseconds; if only some are unknown, it presents a partial sum as the total. This differs from the explicit unknown handling used for the other metrics.
findings.suggestion: Represent total wall time as unknown when any included duration is unavailable, or expose the measured count and clearly identify the sum as partial.
findings.failure_scenario: A provider has one unfinished invocation with no finished timestamp. Its historical totals report one invocation and zero milliseconds of total wall time even though its duration is unknown.

verification.evidence: src/db/stats.ts:240 selects `finished_at - started_at AS duration`, which is null for an unfinished invocation. src/db/stats.ts:174-175 removes null durations, then :193 computes `wallTimeMs: durations.reduce((n, ms) => n + ms, 0)`, while :179 still counts the invocation.
verification.trigger: A provider has one unfinished invocation with no finished timestamp. Historical statistics report one invocation and wallTimeMs 0 although its duration is unknown.

findings.title: Eval rounds discard available cache-token totals
findings.detail: Every eval trial with recorded rounds reports unknown input and cache-token totals, even when the trial stores those measurements and has only one round. The test explicitly expects null for round cache splits, so it would not catch this loss of available workload data.
findings.suggestion: Attribute the stored cache totals when they can be assigned unambiguously, and test a single-round trial with nonzero stored cache-read and cache-write tokens.
findings.failure_scenario: An eval trial has one recorded round and details.cacheReadTokens = 20 and details.cacheWriteTokens = 5; its provider and model report null for both cached-token metrics and uncached input.

verification.evidence: src/db/stats.ts:280–281: `const read = rounds?.length ? null : (details.cacheReadTokens ?? null);` and `const write = rounds?.length ? null : (details.cacheWriteTokens ?? null);`. Line 291 sets `inputTokens` to null when either is null. src/evals/runner.ts:1143–1144 persists both cache totals, and lines 1174–1175 persist round evidence.
verification.trigger: A trial with one recorded round and cacheReadTokens=20, cacheWriteTokens=5 reports null cache totals and uncached input, although the trial totals are available and attributable to that single round.

findings.title: Round aggregation test asserts missing cache measurements
findings.detail: The seeded round test expects null cache metrics but does not seed the trial-level cache measurements recorded by the eval runner. Consequently it passes while the aggregation discards cache data for an unambiguous single-round trial.
findings.suggestion: Add a single-round eval with nonzero trial-level cache totals and assert the provider/model input, cache-read and cache-write aggregates.
findings.failure_scenario: A single-round eval stores cache usage in its trial details, but the statistics endpoint returns null for those metrics and the existing test still passes.

verification.evidence: src/evals/runner.ts:1143–1144 stores `trial.details.cacheReadTokens` and `trial.details.cacheWriteTokens`; :1175 adds recorded round evidence. However, src/db/stats.ts:280–281 uses `const read = rounds?.length ? null : (details.cacheReadTokens ?? null)` and the equivalent for writes, discarding these measurements even for one round. test/provider-workload.test.ts:479–483 supplies rounds without trial cache measurements, and :512–515 explicitly expects null input/cache metrics, leaving this case uncovered.
verification.trigger: A stored eval trial has exactly one recorded round and known cacheReadTokens/cacheWriteTokens in its details. Provider statistics return null for both cache metrics and uncached input tokens despite the available measurements; the existing test passes.

findings.title: Cross-origin requests can trigger unbounded historical aggregation
findings.detail: The existing GET endpoint now synchronously loads and aggregates every stored invocation and eval trial when no cutoff is supplied. GET requests are exempt from the origin check, so a web page can repeatedly trigger this work against a local daemon even though it cannot read the response. As history grows, each request consumes increasing CPU and memory and blocks the daemon's event loop.
findings.suggestion: Bound or protect the historical computation against unsolicited cross-origin requests, and avoid loading the entire history synchronously for the existing workload endpoint.
findings.failure_scenario: A user with a large invocation history visits a page that repeatedly loads the local /api/stats/providers URL; each request runs the full historical aggregation and can make the daemon unresponsive.

verification.evidence: src/server/http.ts:225-229 excludes GET/HEAD from the Origin guard: `req.method !== "GET" && req.method !== "HEAD"`. Token protection depends on `factory.cfg.requireApiToken` (src/server/http.ts:149-151), which defaults off: `requireApiToken: server.require_api_token === true` (src/config.ts:385). The endpoint directly calls `computeProviderStatistics(...)` on every request (src/server/http.ts:754-756). That synchronous function defaults `since = -8_640_000_000_000_000` and loads matching invocation history with `.all(since)` (src/db/stats.ts:230-242), then repeatedly groups and sorts it (src/db/stats.ts:175-176,199-221).
verification.trigger: With default token enforcement disabled and a large stored history, repeated cross-origin GET requests reaching loopback without `since` recompute the entire history synchronously. This can stall daemon request processing; the degree of unresponsiveness is plausible but was not measured.

findings.title: Multi-call evals are counted and attributed as one invocation
findings.detail: The request requires workload “per provider and model” and eval invocations separately. A review panel or sampled review can make several provider calls in one trial, but this code turns a trial without implement-round evidence into one record under the trial target. The runner combines panel members' spend into that trial, so other providers' costs and tokens are attributed to the target and the invocation count is understated.
findings.suggestion: Aggregate individual persisted call evidence where available, and preserve or explicitly identify attribution that cannot be recovered from older records.
findings.failure_scenario: An eval review panel calls provider A once and provider B twice. The result reports one invocation and all combined spend under A, with no workload for B.

verification.evidence: src/pipeline/review.ts:926 returns `result: combined(results, last, { ...decision.review, panel })`; src/evals/runner.ts:1139–1142 adds that result's combined spend and tokens to the trial. Its provider is set with `trial.details.provider = model.provider` (line 641). src/db/stats.ts:265–278 uses one fallback record containing `provider: details.provider` and `costUsd: Number(t.cost_usd)` when rounds are absent; line 179 counts `invocations: rows.length`. Round records are persisted only inside `if ("hidden" in item)` (src/evals/runner.ts:1173–1175).
verification.trigger: A review panel trial without round records calls A once and B twice. Statistics count one invocation and attribute the combined trial cost to A; B receives no workload from these calls.

findings.title: Implement evals discard stored cached-token totals
findings.detail: The request requires input, output, and cached tokens. For every eval with round evidence, the code sets both cache measurements to null even though the runner stores their accumulated values in the trial details. Consequently, even a single-round implement eval with a complete cache split reports its input and cached tokens as unknown.
findings.suggestion: Use the stored trial cache totals when they can be attributed to the selected provider and model, including the single-round case.
findings.failure_scenario: A one-round implement eval records 100 input tokens and 20 cache-read tokens; its eval statistics return null for inputTokens and cacheReadTokens.

verification.evidence: src/evals/runner.ts:1143–1144 accumulates `trial.details.cacheReadTokens` and `trial.details.cacheWriteTokens`; lines 1173–1175 store implement round evidence. src/db/stats.ts:280–281 explicitly assigns null to both cache measurements whenever rounds exist, and line 291 computes `inputTokens: read === null || write === null || r.tokensIn == null ? null : r.tokensIn - read - write`.
verification.trigger: A one-round implement eval with recorded input usage and 20 cache-read tokens returns null for inputTokens and cacheReadTokens, discarding the available trial cache totals.

findings.title: Implementation substantially exceeds the requested source-line budget
findings.detail: The request sets a budget of “About 80 source lines plus tests.” This change adds roughly 250 source lines across the statistics, CLI, HTTP, and date parsing code, substantially exceeding that budget.
findings.suggestion: Reduce the implementation toward the requested budget or explicitly report and justify the overrun.
findings.failure_scenario: The factory reviews the change against its stated line budget and receives an implementation approximately three times the requested source size without an overrun report.

findings.title: Normalizing the log before redaction can expose credential fragments
findings.detail:
The excerpt is redacted after timestamps have been removed from every line. A registered multiline credential containing a timestamp at the start of a line no longer matches its registered value, so its remaining contents are published. A direct Bun probe with the credential `private-first
2026-10-05T00:00:00Z private-second` returned the excerpt `error: failure
private-first
private-second
(fail) test`.
findings.suggestion: Redact the original log before normalization, or preserve a mapping to the original text so credential matching happens before characters are removed.
findings.failure_scenario: A CI log contains a registered multiline credential with a timestamp-shaped line, followed by a failure; the fix trigger and feed publish the credential's other lines.

verification.evidence: src/integrations/ci-classifier.ts:62-64 normalizes with `Bun.stripANSI(log)` and `line.replace(/^\d{4}-\d\d-\d\dT\S+\s+/, "")` before redaction at :52. src/util/proc.ts:1115 registers only original and CRLF-normalized variants. A direct probe returned `credential-middle\ncredential-last` in the excerpt.
verification.trigger: A registered multiline credential contains a timestamp-shaped line. Normalization removes part of the credential, preventing literal redaction; its remaining lines enter the excerpt and are published through emit.

findings.title: A later test failure can replace an unrelated earlier error
findings.detail: The search for a Bun test name crosses arbitrary lines until another recognized failure or passing test appears. For `error: build failed\nBuild stopped\n(fail) unrelated test`, the classifier selects `(fail) unrelated test`, even though the first failure is the build error. This can give the fix round the wrong signature and conflate different build errors.
findings.suggestion: Only associate an error block with a subsequent Bun failure when its intervening structure establishes that they belong together.
findings.failure_scenario: A job reports a build or setup error, then a separate test fails without an intervening passing-test line.

verification.evidence: src/integrations/ci-classifier.ts:87-89 searches after any initial `error:` using `findIndex((l) => failureLine.test(l) || /^\s*\(pass\)/i.test(l))`, then selects a following `(fail)` line without checking whether it belongs to that error. A probe selected `(fail) unrelated test` over `error: build setup broken`.
verification.trigger: A setup/build `error:` precedes an unrelated `(fail)` line with no intervening passing-test or other failure-shaped line. The later test replaces the original error in the signature.

findings.title: A long failing test line can disappear from its own excerpt
findings.detail: The tail window keeps the end of the block, so a sufficiently long `(fail)` line loses its beginning, including the test name. The command `bun -e 'import {ciSignature} from "./src/integrations/ci-classifier.ts"; const s=ciSignature("test", "error: assertion\n"+"x".repeat(3000)+"\n(fail) important-test "+"y".repeat(2500), "fallback"); console.log(JSON.stringify({line:s.line.slice(0,40),excerptContainsName:s.excerpt.includes("important-test"),length:s.excerpt.length}));'` returned `{"line":"(fail) important-test yyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyy","excerptContainsName":false,"length":1999}`.
findings.suggestion: Reserve excerpt space for the beginning of the selected signature line as well as the preceding diagnostic context.

A probe with a 2,200-character failing title produced an excerpt containing no `(fail)` marker.
verification.trigger: After an assertion and long diff, the failing test line exceeds the remaining excerpt budget. Taking its suffix discards the test marker and beginning of the chosen signature line.

findings.title: Publication padding bypasses exact-match redaction for short credentials
findings.detail: Credentials shorter than eight characters are redacted only when the entire input equals the credential. The new publication helper passes surrounding log text to redaction, so an image value that previously was redacted independently can be published and persisted in the signature. A direct probe registering "short" and a longer credential, then classifying "Image: short\nerror: fail", returned image "short".
findings.suggestion: Preserve exact-match redaction for the selected value while retaining enough surrounding context to redact longer credentials crossing the window.

A probe returned image `s3cr` and a signature containing it. The feed image itself is subsequently protected by `quote(f.image)` at :271.

Surrounding text defeats exact-match redaction, leaving the credential in the generated image, stored signature and excerpt. The separately quoted feed image is redacted, but the excerpt still exposes it.

findings.title: Preserve event sequence across job attempts
findings.detail: Each attempt starts its event sequence at zero, but agent_job_events is keyed by job ID and sequence, and the coordinator silently ignores conflicts. A retried job therefore loses batches whose sequence numbers overlap an earlier attempt, while later batches can be mixed with the earlier attempt's events.
findings.suggestion: Make event storage and sequencing attempt-aware, or otherwise ensure a retry cannot collide with previously stored batches.
findings.failure_scenario: Worker A posts batch 0 and then fails; worker B retries the same job and posts its own batch 0. The coordinator returns success but retains worker A's batch and discards worker B's.

verification.evidence: src/workers/client.ts:469-477 initializes each execution with `seq = 0` and sends `{ seq: seq++, events }`. src/db/workers.ts:355-359 requeues the same job id on failure (`j.attempt < 2 ? "queued" : "failed"`) without clearing events. src/db/workers.ts:342 inserts batches with `ON CONFLICT(job_id,seq) DO NOTHING`. src/server/workers.ts:215-222 then returns `{ ok: true }`.
verification.trigger: Worker A persists batch 0 and fails. Worker B leases the same job and starts at batch 0; its batch is silently discarded because A's batch already occupies that sequence.

findings.title: Report failure when an event batch is rejected
findings.detail: A rejected events request aborts the job controller. The catch block then skips the failure endpoint because jobSignal is aborted, so the coordinator continues to hold the lease until it expires instead of recording the rejected batch as a job failure.
findings.suggestion: Distinguish an event-post failure from cancellation and report it with a separate bounded signal before releasing the job.
findings.failure_scenario: The coordinator rejects an oversized or invalid event batch with HTTP 400. The harness is aborted, but no failure is posted and the job remains leased until expiry.

verification.evidence: src/workers/client.ts:273-276 throws on nonretryable HTTP responses. At :479-480, rejected event posts invoke `agentJobs.get(id)?.controller.abort()`. The failure handler at :533-538 posts `/failure` only under `if (!jobSignal.aborted)`. src/server/workers.ts:272-275 returns 400 or 413 for invalid or oversized bodies without failing the agent job.
verification.trigger: An event batch receives HTTP 400 while the lease is valid. The rejection aborts the job signal, suppressing the failure notification; the coordinator retains the leased job until expiry.

findings.title: Fence at the lease deadline rather than the next interval
findings.detail: The periodic check can run almost one heartbeat interval after the lease period has elapsed. During that window the coordinator can expire and reassign the job while the original worker continues running the harness and spending quota.
findings.suggestion: Schedule fencing against the last successful heartbeat's actual deadline and reset that deadline on each success.
findings.failure_scenario: A heartbeat succeeds just after a fence tick and connectivity is then lost. The tick immediately before the deadline sees a fresh heartbeat, and the worker continues until the following tick, potentially nearly another heartbeat interval after lease expiry.

verification.evidence: src/workers/client.ts:314 sets `lastHeartbeat = performance.now()`. At :552-557 fencing uses `setInterval` with `Math.min(options.heartbeatMs ?? timing.heartbeat, leaseMs)` and aborts only when `performance.now() - lastHeartbeat > leaseMs`.
verification.trigger: A successful heartbeat occurs just after a fence tick, followed by a partition. The last tick before the lease deadline does nothing, allowing the agent to continue until the next tick, nearly one heartbeat interval beyond the deadline.

findings.title: Report a failure when an event batch is rejected
findings.detail: A rejected events request aborts the job controller. The resulting error reaches the catch block with `jobSignal.aborted` already true, so it skips the failure POST and removes the job from the worker's held list. The coordinator retains the lease until expiry, and the rejection is lost instead of immediately failing the attempt. The new rejection test checks only that the job is not done, so it does not detect this.
findings.suggestion: Track event-post failures separately from cancellation, abort the harness, and report the failure using a bounded signal that is not already aborted.
findings.failure_scenario: The coordinator returns HTTP 400 or 413 for an event batch while the lease is still valid; the harness stops, but the job remains leased until its lease expires.

verification.evidence: src/workers/client.ts:479-480 handles an event-post rejection with `agentJobs.get(id)?.controller.abort()`. At :533-538, `/failure` is guarded by `if (!jobSignal.aborted)`. src/server/workers.ts:272-275 responds to validation or body-size errors with 400 or 413 and does not transition the agent job.
verification.trigger: The coordinator rejects an event batch with HTTP 400 or 413 during a valid lease. The worker aborts the harness and skips reporting failure, leaving the job leased until expiry.

findings.title: Fence at the lease deadline rather than the next interval
findings.detail: The fencing interval polls every heartbeat period and uses a strict greater-than comparison. A missed heartbeat can therefore leave an agent running beyond the one-lease-period limit, potentially for another full heartbeat interval. The coordinator may already have expired and reassigned the job while the original session continues spending quota.
findings.suggestion: Schedule fencing against the exact deadline derived from the last successful heartbeat, and reset that deadline on each success.
findings.failure_scenario: With the default 60-second lease and 10-second heartbeat interval, a partition begins after a heartbeat; the agent can continue for nearly 70 seconds after the last successful heartbeat.

verification.evidence: src/workers/protocol.ts:103-105 defines `heartbeat: 10_000` and `lease: 60_000`. src/workers/client.ts:552-557 checks elapsed heartbeat time only on an interval and aborts when `performance.now() - lastHeartbeat > leaseMs`.
verification.trigger: With default timing, a heartbeat succeeds just after a fence tick and connectivity fails. Fencing can occur nearly 70 seconds after that heartbeat instead of at the 60-second deadline, wasting additional paid work.

findings.title: A rejected event batch aborts the job without reporting failure
findings.detail: A rejected events request aborts the agent controller. The catch handler then skips the failure endpoint because the same job signal is aborted. The coordinator retains the lease until it expires instead of promptly recording the failed attempt and making it available for retry.
findings.suggestion: Distinguish an event-post failure from cancellation and report it through a separate bounded signal while the lease is still held. Add a test that asserts the failure endpoint is called and the attempt is requeued or failed.
findings.failure_scenario: The coordinator rejects an oversized events batch with HTTP 413 while the lease remains valid; the harness stops, but no failure is posted and the job stays leased until expiry.

verification.evidence: src/workers/client.ts:273–276 throws on HTTP responses below 500. verification.trigger: An oversized events batch receives 413 while the lease remains valid. The rejection aborts the harness and suppresses the failure report, leaving the coordinator job leased until expiry.

findings.title: Rejected-batch test accepts a job that remains leased
findings.detail: The test checks only that the job is not done, so it passes when no failure is reported and the job remains leased. Its request wrapper also lets the real server accept the batch before changing the response to 409, so it does not exercise a genuinely rejected batch.
findings.suggestion: Reject the events request before forwarding it, then assert that the failure endpoint is called and the coordinator records the failed attempt.
findings.failure_scenario: An events endpoint returns a client error while the worker still holds the lease; the worker aborts locally without notifying the coordinator, but this test passes.

findings.detail: The burst case waits for all three batches, including the partial batch that must wait for the timer. It would also pass if the two full batches were delayed until the timer, so it does not protect the 200-event threshold.

findings.title: Report a rejected event batch as a job failure
findings.detail: A rejected events POST aborts the job controller. The catch handler then skips the failure POST because jobSignal is aborted, and the worker stops reporting the job as held. The coordinator must wait for lease expiry instead of receiving the required failure.

findings.failure_scenario: An event batch exceeds the server's 1 MiB body limit or otherwise receives a 4xx response; the harness stops, but the agent job remains leased until expiry.

findings.title: Fence at the lease deadline rather than on a periodic poll
findings.detail: The fencing interval checks elapsed time only once per heartbeat interval and uses a strict greater-than comparison. A partitioned worker can therefore continue running and spending model quota for up to another heartbeat interval after the lease period has elapsed.
findings.suggestion: Arm a deadline timer from the last successful heartbeat and reset it after each success, aborting held agent jobs when that deadline expires.

findings.title: A rejected event batch does not report job failure
findings.detail: The request says, “A rejected batch fails the job.” A rejected post aborts the job controller, but the catch block posts failure only when jobSignal is not aborted. Consequently the coordinator retains the job as leased until lease expiry instead of receiving its failure.
findings.suggestion: Distinguish event-post failure from external cancellation and post a sanitized failure using a signal that remains usable for that notification.
findings.failure_scenario: The coordinator returns 400 for an invalid or oversized event batch while the worker still holds the lease; the harness stops, but no failure is posted and the job remains leased until expiry.

verification.evidence: src/workers/client.ts:273–276 rejects HTTP 400; :480 handles rejected event posts by calling `controller.abort()`. findings.title: Fencing can run substantially later than one lease period
findings.detail: The request requires that a worker abort running agents when no heartbeat has succeeded for longer than one lease period. The interval checks only every heartbeat interval, so an agent can continue running for nearly another 10 seconds after the 60-second lease has expired. The coordinator can meanwhile reassign the job, allowing both sessions to spend quota.
findings.suggestion: Schedule fencing against the exact deadline derived from the last successful heartbeat and reset that deadline after each success.
findings.failure_scenario: A heartbeat succeeds just after a fence interval tick and then the network partitions; the coordinator expires the lease after 60 seconds, while the worker continues its harness until the next interval tick.

verification.evidence: src/workers/client.ts:552–557 uses a periodic check: `if (performance.now() - lastHeartbeat > leaseMs)` followed by aborting agent jobs, with an interval equal to the smaller of heartbeat and lease periods. src/workers/protocol.ts:103–105 supplies default periods of 10 and 60 seconds.

findings.title: Buffered events are discarded when the harness throws
findings.detail: The request requires events to be batched and posted. If the harness emits events and throws before the 250 ms timer fires, the failure path clears the timer without flushing the buffered events, losing the session's final diagnostics.

findings.title: A dirty worktree can bypass detection of a cancelled worker's push
findings.detail: When reconciliation rejects an open job, the executor cancels it and calls prepare(). If the coordinator worktree is dirty, prepare() returns null before checking the remote branch, so the executor runs the local session even if the cancelled worker already pushed an unreported commit. The request requires that case to end NeedsHuman.
findings.suggestion: Check the cancelled job's remote branch for an unreported push before falling back to local execution, including when preparation cannot proceed because the worktree is dirty.
findings.failure_scenario: A worker pushes W but has not reported it; after restart the coordinator worktree is dirty. Reconciliation cancels the leased job, prepare() returns null, and a local session starts instead of reporting the unaccepted push.

verification.evidence: src/pipeline/engine.ts:1138-1139 requires HEAD to match and `(await clean())` for resume. src/pipeline/lan-agent.ts:89-91 then executes `workers.cancelAgentJob(id)` and `id = undefined` when reconciliation fails. src/pipeline/engine.ts:1149 returns `null` for a dirty worktree before checking `remoteSha()` at line 1150. src/pipeline/lan-agent.ts:110 executes `if (!prepared) return fallback();`; line 51 defines fallback as calling `local()` when not aborted. Thus the remote-movement guard at lines 203-208 is bypassed.
verification.trigger: A handled, leased worker job has pushed W without an accepted report; the coordinator restarts with a dirty worktree and an active signal. Resume fails cleanliness, cancels the job, and starts a local session without detecting W or raising NeedsHuman.

findings.title: A fenced pending report no longer renews its lease
findings.detail: The new result request survives the fence, but the fence aborts the job controller and heldJobs() consequently omits the job from heartbeats. Those heartbeats no longer renew its lease. If result requests remain unavailable while heartbeat requests succeed, the lease expires despite the worker continuing to retry the accepted-report request, and the coordinator rejects the eventual report.
findings.suggestion: Keep a pushed job in the heartbeat's held-job list while its independently bounded result report is pending, until the result is accepted or the lease is explicitly lost.
findings.failure_scenario: A worker pushes during an outage and its fence fires. After restart, heartbeats succeed but result requests fail transiently for longer than the remaining lease or restart grace. The coordinator expires the job; a later result receives 409 and the pushed commit cannot be adopted.

verification.evidence: src/workers/client.ts:565-567 fences jobs with `job.controller.abort()`, while :501-504 includes only `job.reported && !job.controller.signal.aborted` in `heldJobs()`. The pushed report continues with `AbortSignal.timeout(Math.max(0, deadline - Date.now()))` (:861). src/db/workers.ts:242-252 renews leases only for IDs in `c.jobs`; :414-420 expires an unrenewed lease with `this.failAgentJob(j.id, "Lease expired")`. src/server/workers.ts:202-203 rejects reports without a held lease with status 409.
verification.trigger: A pushed report remains pending when the fence aborts its job controller. Heartbeats recover but omit that job, so result failures lasting beyond the lease/restart grace cause lease expiry. A later report receives 409, preventing adoption of the pushed commit.

findings.title: Late result retries can prevent worker shutdown
findings.detail: The late-result signal excludes the worker's shutdown signal as well as the job cancellation and fence signals. If the coordinator is unreachable, `call()` keeps retrying until the attempt deadline, while `runWorker` waits for every job task in its shutdown cleanup. Stopping the worker can therefore hang for the remainder of the agent attempt, potentially many minutes.
findings.suggestion: Combine the attempt-deadline signal with the worker's shutdown signal while continuing to exclude the job controller used by cancellation and the fence.
findings.failure_scenario: A worker pushes a commit, begins retrying its result during a coordinator outage, and then receives a shutdown signal. Its result request remains active and `runWorker` does not finish until the attempt deadline expires.

verification.evidence: src/workers/client.ts:857-862 gives a pushed result only `AbortSignal.timeout(Math.max(0, deadline - Date.now()))`, excluding the worker shutdown signal. The request loop retries failures using that signal (:505-526). Shutdown aborts controllers (:984-986), then awaits `...allJobs().map(([, j]) => j.task)` in `Promise.allSettled` (:987-991), which includes the pending result request.
verification.trigger: A worker pushes, retries its result during a coordinator outage, then receives shutdown. Shutdown cannot abort the result retry, so runWorker remains pending until the attempt deadline or an earlier terminal response.

findings.title: A pinned review model can send a local finder to a worker
findings.detail: Local finders receive the same checkout metadata as production finders. Their free-only routing constraint does not keep them local when the run pins a review model: the router lets a pinned chain override billing constraints. If that model uses a supported harness without backend credentials, the worker executor dispatches the local finder.
findings.suggestion: Carry the local-finder designation to the dispatch decision, or omit checkout metadata for local finders. Add a panel test with a local finder and a pinned Claude or Codex review model.
findings.failure_scenario: A GitHub run enables worker reviews, configures a local panel finder, and pins a Claude review model. The local finder creates a worker job instead of running locally.

verification.evidence: src/pipeline/context.ts:545 sets `chain = shadow ? undefined : this.run.models?.[opts.role as RunRole]`, and lines 593–595 pass it alongside finder constraints. src/router/router.ts:379 computes `paid = !c.chain && c.billing !== undefined && m.billing !== "free" ? 1 : 0`, so a pin bypasses free-only filtering. src/pipeline/engine.ts:1840–1843 supplies checkout to the finder; src/pipeline/lan-agent.ts:26–40 then admits the pinned native Claude target.
verification.trigger: An eligible GitHub run has a local panel finder and a pinned native Claude review model. The pin overrides free-only routing, and the finder creates a worker job.

findings.title: Verify-change worker review base is not covered
findings.detail: The new end-to-end cases exercise ordinary quick runs only. The existing verify-change case stops before review and checks implement eligibility, so no test would catch using the run base instead of verification.baseSha for a verify-change worker checkout.
findings.suggestion: Add a verify-change review case with distinct run and verification bases, and assert the worker request uses verification.baseSha and the reviewed head.
findings.failure_scenario: A future regression passes ctx.run.baseSha to a verify-change review worker; the added worker tests still pass.

verification.evidence: test/pipeline-lan-agent.test.ts:1358 parameterizes only `["single", "panel"]`; its checkout assertion at :1418 expects `baseSha: f.store.getRun(call.runId)?.baseSha`. Production instead uses `const baseSha = ctx.state.verification?.baseSha ?? (ctx.run.baseSha as string)` (src/pipeline/engine.ts:1431), passed into checkout at :1842. These differ for verify-change because :583 sets the run's baseSha to `verification.headSha`. The executor eligibility test supplies checkout directly (test/lan-agent.test.ts:598), bypassing this derivation.
verification.trigger: A future change substitutes ctx.run.baseSha for the review checkout's baseSha. Verify-change worker reviews then receive the verification head as their base, while the added worker tests still pass because they never exercise that flow.

findings.title: Local panel finders can be dispatched to workers
findings.detail: The request says that “shadow reviews and local finders” stay local. The shared review call always supplies checkout metadata, including for a finder marked local. The executor has no local-finder flag and only excludes targets by harness and credential-bearing fields. A local finder routed to an eligible Claude or Codex target therefore creates a worker job. In particular, a pinned review model uses a routing chain that bypasses the free-only billing filter.
findings.suggestion: Carry the local-finder distinction into the shared call and omit checkout or explicitly reject worker dispatch for those calls.
findings.failure_scenario: A panel has a finder with local: true and the run pins review to a Claude or Codex model. The finder receives checkout metadata and runs on a worker instead of locally.

verification.evidence: src/pipeline/engine.ts:1859 represents local finders using `{ billing: "free_only" as const }`, but lines 1840–1843 attach checkout to every shared review call. src/pipeline/context.ts:545,595 applies the run's review model chain; src/router/router.ts:379–380 disables free-only exclusion when `c.chain` exists. src/pipeline/lan-agent.ts:26–40 accepts the resulting Claude/Codex readonly call without a locality guard.
verification.trigger: With worker reviews enabled for the GitHub repository, a local panel finder inherits a pinned native Claude or Codex review model and checkout metadata. It is dispatched to a worker instead of running locally.

candidates.title: Keep explicitly local panel finders on the coordinator

The `free_only` routing constraint does not guarantee an ineligible target: the provider configuration accepts a free `claude-cli` or `codex-cli` provider without a backend. Such a finder is dispatched to a worker, contrary to the requirement that local finders stay local.
candidates.suggestion: Pass the finder's local designation through the call seam and exclude it from worker eligibility.
candidates.failure_scenario: A panel finder has `local: true`, routing selects a free `codex-cli` provider, and review workers are enabled for the repository. The finder creates a worker job instead of running on the coordinator.

candidates.title: Local panel finders can be dispatched to workers

findings.title: Local panel finders can be dispatched to workers
findings.detail: Eligibility infers that a finder is local from its target having a backend, OpenAI, or decisions configuration. The review call does not pass the finder's `local` flag to the executor, so that inference fails when routing selects a plain Claude or Codex CLI target. A pinned review model can select such a target despite the finder's `free_only` constraint. The finder then runs on a worker even though local finders must remain local.
findings.suggestion: Pass an explicit local-finder indicator through the review call and exclude it from worker eligibility.
findings.failure_scenario: A panel has a finder configured with `local: true`, the run pins its review model to a Claude CLI target, and review workers are enabled for the repository. The finder creates a worker job instead of invoking the local harness.

verification.evidence: src/pipeline/engine.ts:1859 represents a local finder only as `...(finder?.local ? { billing: "free_only" as const } : {})`, while engine.ts:1840-1843 supplies checkout to every production review call. src/pipeline/context.ts:545 selects `this.run.models?.[opts.role as RunRole]` as the pinned chain and :595 passes it to routing. src/router/router.ts:379-380 checks billing only when `!c.chain`: `const paid = !c.chain && c.billing !== undefined && m.billing !== "free" ? 1 : 0; if (paid && c.billing === "free_only") continue;`. src/pipeline/lan-agent.ts:26-40 accepts readonly review calls with checkout and a Claude/Codex target without backend/openai/decisions; it has no local-finder guard. Line 157 then calls `workers.enqueueAgentJob(request, id)`.
verification.trigger: A production panel finder has local: true, the run pins review to an available Claude CLI target without backend/openai/decisions, and review workers are enabled for the GitHub repository. The pinned chain bypasses the free-only billing filter, and the finder enqueues a worker job instead of invoking the coordinator's local harness.

A finder marked local can still receive a plain Claude or Codex target when the run supplies an explicit review model chain: the router deliberately bypasses the free-only billing restriction for explicit chains. That target passes this check and runs on a worker, contrary to the requirement that local finders stay local.
findings.suggestion: Pass the finder's local designation through the invocation seam and exclude those calls explicitly from worker dispatch.
findings.failure_scenario: A panel has a local finder, the run specifies a Claude review model, and review workers are enabled for the repository. The finder is dispatched to a worker instead of running on the coordinator.

findings.title: Exercise local repository review routing through the engine
findings.detail: The new eligibility test checks a manually constructed call without checkout metadata, but it does not verify that the engine omits that metadata for a local repository. The end-to-end review cases all register a GitHub repository.
findings.suggestion: Run a review for a local repository with review workers enabled and assert that the review runs locally and no worker job is created.
findings.failure_scenario: If the engine starts supplying checkout metadata for local repositories, a matching configured repository could dispatch its review to a worker while the current new tests continue to pass.

verification.evidence: src/pipeline/engine.ts:1841 currently guards checkout with `ctx.repo.kind === "github" && ctx.run.branch`. The new integration test uses `registerGithub(f, bare)` (test/pipeline-lan-agent.test.ts:1451). The existing local-repository case changes `this.repo.kind = "local"` at :724 but stops at `"stage:gates:before"` (:741), before review. test/lan-agent.test.ts:626 tests missing checkout directly, without exercising the engine guard.
verification.trigger: If the engine begins supplying checkout for local repositories, an otherwise eligible review with a matching configured slug could dispatch to a worker; current tests do not exercise that engine path.

findings.title: Validate hidden tests under the same cleanup conditions as grading
findings.detail: Validation runs the hidden command immediately after setup, leaving untracked setup artifacts in the worktree. The implement grader runs gates and then performs `git reset --hard` and `git clean -fdq` before injecting hidden files. A case can therefore pass at head during generation but fail when graded. The new fixture itself uses a setup-created untracked `ready` file that grading would remove.
findings.suggestion: Mirror the grader's reset and clean before injecting and running hidden tests, and exercise an accepted case through the actual grading path.
findings.failure_scenario: Setup writes an untracked `ready` file and a hidden test reads it. Head validation passes, but grading removes `ready` before running the hidden command, so even the reference implementation fails.

verification.evidence: scripts/implement-replay-cases.ts:229 runs `prepareEvalGates(item, cwd, signal, true)`, then :234 immediately calls `injectHiddenFiles(cwd, files)` without cleanup. Grading instead runs `git reset --hard` and `git clean -fdq` before injection (src/evals/implement.ts:260–270).
verification.trigger: Setup creates an untracked, nonignored ready file required by the hidden test. Validation retains it and accepts the reference head; grading deletes it, causing the reference implementation's hidden test to fail.

candidates.title: Per-PR failures leave the CLI with a successful exit status

Consequently a missing request, failed GitHub call, confinement failure, or failed dataset write can produce no cases while the command reports success to an invoking script.
candidates.suggestion: Preserve per-PR reporting but return a nonzero exit status when a requested PR could not be processed, distinguishing expected duplicates if desired.
candidates.failure_scenario: A caller runs the generator for one PR without a quoted Request block; it prints an error in the table but exits with status 0, so automation proceeds as though generation succeeded.

candidates.title: The CLI never looks up production complexity
candidates.detail: The command-line entry point does not supply lookupRun, so replayProduction always defaults complexity to medium, even when the report identifies a production run whose record is available. This prevents the requested production triage complexity from being recorded.

candidates.failure_scenario: A merged PR identifies a locally recorded run with triage complexity small or large; running the documented generator writes medium instead.

candidates.title: The complexity test bypasses the CLI wiring

candidates.failure_scenario: The documented command generates a case for a known small production run and silently assigns medium, while the existing test still passes.

candidates.title: Run reference tests without granting access to the shared repository cache
candidates.detail: Head validation uses a linked worktree of the shared repository cache. The gate sandbox explicitly grants linked worktrees read access to their Git common directory, so repository setup and hidden test code can read every object and ref in that cache, including history outside the selected base and head. The sandbox permits outbound network access. The isolated eval checkout machinery avoids exposing that history to untrusted code, but this validation path bypasses it.
candidates.suggestion: Validate head in a standalone repository containing only the required pinned history, using the same isolation approach as the eval checkout.
candidates.failure_scenario: A merged PR contains a test that reads an unrelated private ref or historical blob from the common Git directory and sends its contents over the network during head validation.

candidates.title: Wire production run lookup into the generator CLI
candidates.detail: The CLI never supplies `lookupRun`, so every generated case defaults to medium complexity even when the factory run named in the PR footer is available locally. The injectable lookup is exercised only by programmatic callers, while the requested generator interface is the CLI.

candidates.failure_scenario: A factory PR has a footer naming a locally stored run with small triage complexity; invoking the documented generator records medium instead.

candidates.title: Mandatory snapshot preparation excludes the factory’s own replay cases
candidates.detail: The request calls for generating cases from the factory’s merged PRs and validating whether the hidden command fails at base and passes at head. Every generated case is forced into snapshot mode, and preparation rejects it if any baseline gate fails after snapshot mode removes evals/. The documentation itself states that Limitless’s test suite reads evals/ and therefore cannot use snapshot mode for implement cases. Consequently, qualifying Limitless PRs are excluded before either requested validation result can be obtained.
candidates.suggestion: Support a contamination-safe preparation strategy that can run the factory repository’s baseline without removing files required by its tests, and validate a representative factory PR.
candidates.failure_scenario: A merged Limitless PR has a changed test that fails at its first parent and passes at its squash commit, but the base test suite reads evals/. Snapshot preparation removes evals/, its baseline check fails, and the generator excludes the PR.

Verifier: 11 candidates, 11 checked, 2 refuted.

findings.title: Apply the gates stage's timeout retry before returning the session result
findings.detail: The session path calls retryRegressions but does not perform the gates stage's timeout-only rerun. Timed-out results are then excluded from storage, so the session immediately receives a failure and the gates stage runs the suite again even on the identical tree. This loses the normal timeout retry and classification and defeats the requested reuse for this failure mode.
findings.suggestion: Share the gates stage's timeout handling with the session gate path and persist the resulting completed execution and retry information.
findings.failure_scenario: The first test attempt times out transiently and would pass on the normal timeout rerun. The implementer sees a failure, and the gates stage starts the full suite again instead of reusing the factory execution.

verification.evidence: src/pipeline/agent-gate.ts:158 executes `const after = await run()`, then calls only `retryRegressions` at line 176. src/gates/run.ts:470 excludes `c.result.timedOut` from that retry. src/pipeline/agent-gate.ts:61 excludes timed-out results from storage. By contrast, src/pipeline/engine.ts:1561 reruns when `timeoutOnly && !baseTimeout`.
verification.trigger: A transient first-attempt timeout that would pass on the normal timeout rerun is returned as failure without that rerun. No reusable record is saved, so the gates stage runs the suite again.

findings.title: Preserve worker-session behavior when the repository selects gate mode
findings.detail: The new gate mode is translated to refuse for worker sessions. The request limits the new behavior to local implement sessions and says worker implement rounds retain their existing behavior. Previously, an implementer in slot mode could run its full suite under a slot; with this repository switched to gate, the same worker request is now refused.
findings.suggestion: Keep the existing worker full-suite behavior when translating the local-only gate policy.
findings.failure_scenario: A LAN worker runs an implement round for this repository and invokes bun test. The wrapper rejects the command instead of running it in the existing slotted lane.

verification.evidence: src/pipeline/lan-agent.ts:153 maps gate mode to refusal: `agentFullSuite: call.agentFullSuite === "gate" ? "refuse" : call.agentFullSuite`. src/workers/client.ts:881 forwards that policy: `{ role: req.role, agentFullSuite: req.agentFullSuite }`. src/cli/agent-test.ts:229 checks `lane === "gate" && config.role === "implement" && config.agentFullSuite === "refuse"`, prints `full suite refused`, and returns `1` at line 237.
verification.trigger: A LAN worker implement session receives agent_full_suite="gate" and invokes a wrapped full-suite command such as bun test. The coordinator converts the policy to "refuse", so the wrapper rejects the command instead of using the existing slotted execution path required for worker sessions.

findings.title: Return failure when confinement fails with exit status zero
findings.detail: The command status is derived from the process exit code without checking result.ok or confinementFailed(result). The gate runner can mark a result as a confinement failure even when the shell exits zero. In that case the wrapper reports a successful command to the implementer despite the failed isolation check.
findings.suggestion: Return a nonzero status whenever confinementFailed(result) is true, including for a failed setup step.
findings.failure_scenario: A setup or test command emits the confinement failure detected by the gate runner, then exits zero. The factory prints FAIL but the wrapper exits 0, so a script or agent treats the failed security check as successful.

verification.evidence: src/gates/run.ts:132 computes `ok = !confinementError && res.exitCode === 0 && !res.timedOut && !res.cancelled`, preserving the original `exitCode` at line 139. src/pipeline/agent-gate.ts:198 returns that exit code unless interrupted or timed out, while line 200 prints `FAIL` when `result.ok` is false. src/cli/agent-test.ts:223 returns `result.status`.
verification.trigger: A command emits a detected confinement failure and exits zero. The factory labels it FAIL but returns zero to the session wrapper.

findings.title: A synthetic commit can make a reused gate pass on a different Git state
findings.detail: The snapshot checkout uses a synthetic commit whose message and SHA differ from the round commit, and always adds a child commit even when the tree equals HEAD. Gate commands can inspect Git history or HEAD, so a test may pass in the snapshot checkout but fail in the eventual round checkout. Reuse is keyed only by tree and then suppresses that test at the gates stage.
findings.suggestion: Ensure gate checks observe the same relevant Git state as the round checkout, or refuse reuse when that equivalence cannot be established.
findings.failure_scenario: A test checks the latest commit message or the number of commits since a tag. It passes against the synthetic 'Factory gate snapshot' commit but would fail against the actual round commit; the matching tree causes the passing result to be reused.

verification.evidence: src/git/repos.ts:548-553 creates `commit-tree tree -p HEAD` with `stdin: "Factory gate snapshot\n"`; line 568 installs that synthetic commit as checkout HEAD. The actual round uses `commitAll(cwd, commitMessage(ctx, round))` (src/pipeline/engine.ts:1404). Reuse resolves only `${sha}^{tree}` and looks up that key (src/pipeline/agent-gate.ts:94-98); the engine then removes the test check from execution (src/pipeline/engine.ts:1525-1528).
verification.trigger: A repository test inspects `git log -1 --format=%s` and passes for the synthetic snapshot message but fails for the actual round message. With unchanged files and matching configuration/environment, the tree matches and the passing snapshot execution suppresses the failing round test.

findings.title: Exercise verify substitution through a reused execution
findings.detail: The integration test stops after checking that reused metadata reaches gate evidence. The added substitution test separately fabricates a GateEvidence object, so neither test proves that a real reused execution is accepted by verify, or that session-produced output is rejected there.
findings.suggestion: Add fake-harness pipeline cases that reach verify with a reused factory execution and with only a session claim, then assert the respective criterion outcomes.
findings.failure_scenario: The gates stage records reused metadata but verify discards it or accepts an agent's printed success claim; the current tests can still pass.

verification.evidence: test/agent-full-suite-gate.test.ts:132 selects `triage({ suggested_profile: "quick" })`; src/pipeline/engine.ts:2079–2083 skips verify for `profile(ctx) === "quick"`. The assertion at test/agent-full-suite-gate.test.ts:216 only checks `state.gateEvidence?...result.reused`. test/gate-evidence.test.ts:136–137 manually assigns `check.result.reused = ...` before calling `resolve(blocked, evidence)`, bypassing the pipeline integration.
verification.trigger: A regression in the pipeline's handoff of reused evidence to verify could leave these tests passing: the integration test skips verify, and the substitution unit test supplies synthetic evidence directly. This confirms a coverage gap, not a demonstrated production failure.

findings.title: Test changes to the actual gate configuration and environment
findings.detail: The configuration and environment mismatch scenarios directly overwrite the stored hash with a literal. They test database lookup, but would still pass if the key calculation stopped incorporating the actual gate configuration or environment.
findings.suggestion: Change a gate configuration input and a gate-relevant environment input between recording and lookup, and assert that each causes a normal test gate execution.
findings.failure_scenario: A regression makes the configuration or environment digest constant, causing an execution to be reused after its inputs change; the existing mismatch scenarios still miss because they manually alter the stored hash.

verification.evidence: test/agent-full-suite-gate.test.ts:172–175 implements both mismatch scenarios with `UPDATE agent_gate_executions SET ${scenario === "config" ? "gates_hash" : "env_hash"} = 'different'`. Production derives those values in src/pipeline/agent-gate.ts:74–86 through `baselineCacheKey(...)` and `gateEnvDigest(env, ctx.deps.cfg.baselineEnv)`. The tests never change those actual inputs.
verification.trigger: If agentGateKey regressed to supplying constant configuration or environment inputs, manually changing the stored hash would still force a cache miss and pass these scenarios, while actual input changes could incorrectly reuse an execution. Existing digest unit tests do not cover this wiring.

findings.title: Do not follow candidate-controlled lockfile symlinks in the daemon
findings.detail: The new gate key hashes lockfiles from the exported candidate checkout using lockfileHash, which follows symlinks and reads their targets synchronously in the daemon, outside gate confinement. A candidate can therefore make the daemon read arbitrary accessible paths or block indefinitely on a special file. The same lookup also occurs when deciding whether to reuse a result.
findings.suggestion: Hash the lockfile blob from the Git tree, or validate with lstat that each lockfile is a regular file before reading it without following symlinks.
findings.failure_scenario: An implementer commits bun.lock as a symlink to /dev/zero and requests the full suite. Computing the gate key reads an unbounded stream synchronously, potentially exhausting daemon memory or blocking the daemon.

verification.evidence: src/pipeline/agent-gate.ts:79 calls `lockfileHash(cwd)` on the candidate snapshot checkout. src/gates/cache.ts:124 uses `if (existsSync(path)) hash.update(...).update(readFileSync(path))`, with no symlink, file-type, or size check. src/git/repos.ts:575 exports the candidate tree into that checkout.
verification.trigger: A candidate bun.lock symlink to /dev/zero reaches synchronous readFileSync in the daemon. Reading the unbounded device can block the daemon or exhaust memory before gate confinement starts.

findings.title: Include the test worker count in the environment key
findings.detail: gateEnv sets LIMITLESS_TEST_WORKERS, but gateEnvDigest does not include that variable unless it is explicitly configured in baseline_env. A persisted result can therefore be reused after a daemon restart with a different test worker count, even though parallelism can change test outcomes.
findings.suggestion: Include LIMITLESS_TEST_WORKERS in the environment digest used for agent gate executions.
findings.failure_scenario: The in-session suite passes with LIMITLESS_TEST_WORKERS=1, then the daemon restarts with LIMITLESS_TEST_WORKERS=8 before the gates stage. The environment hash remains the same and the earlier pass suppresses the test run despite the changed environment.

verification.evidence: src/gates/run.ts:98 sets `LIMITLESS_TEST_WORKERS: String(resolveTestWorkers())`. src/pipeline/agent-gate.ts:84 hashes `gateEnvDigest(env, ctx.deps.cfg.baselineEnv)`. src/gates/cache.ts:135-136 includes only explicitly listed variables, configured extras, or matching prefixes; `LIMITLESS_TEST_WORKERS` is absent from the list at lines 56-90 and does not match the prefixes at line 97.
verification.trigger: With no explicit baseline_env entry for LIMITLESS_TEST_WORKERS, changing its resolved value from 1 to 8 across a restart leaves the reuse key unchanged. A previous pass suppresses a suite run under the changed worker count.

findings.title: Timed-out factory gate results are never recorded or reused
findings.detail: The request says to record the gate result and that “its pass or failure, retries and classification carry over unchanged.” The completed predicate excludes every timeout, so a timed-out in-session factory gate is discarded. When the round ends on the same tree, the gates stage runs the full test check again instead of carrying over that failure.
findings.suggestion: Apply the normal gate timeout retry and classification behavior to the factory execution, then persist and reuse its completed failure result.
findings.failure_scenario: The test check times out during an implement session, and the implementer makes no further changes. The gates stage starts the same test check again despite the matching tree, configuration, and environment.

verification.evidence: src/pipeline/agent-gate.ts:55–62 defines `completed` with `result.exitCode !== null` and `!result.timedOut`. Recording requires `completed(result)` at :189, and reuse requires `completed(comparison.result)` at :105. src/pipeline/engine.ts:1526–1531 retains and executes the test check when reuse is absent. test/agent-full-suite-gate.test.ts:222–234 explicitly expects no recorded execution for the `timeout` scenario.
verification.trigger: An implement-session factory test gate times out and the session leaves the same tree. Its result is not recorded, so the gates stage executes the same test check again despite matching configuration and environment.

The gates stage checks HEAD only in the separate session checkout, so it cannot detect this change. A passing result can consequently be reused and accepted as verification evidence for a tree the test did not check.
candidates.suggestion: Check the snapshot checkout's HEAD after execution and retries, and refuse to record evidence if it no longer identifies the snapshot commit.

findings.title: Reject results when the snapshot gate changes HEAD
findings.detail: The execution is recorded under the original tree without checking whether setup or the test command changed the snapshot checkout's HEAD. The normal gates stage explicitly checks HEAD before making its results available as evidence. A passing result from a different checkout can therefore be reused and accepted as evidence for the original tree.
findings.suggestion: Record the snapshot commit before execution and verify that HEAD still points to it before storing the result; fail closed if it changed.
findings.failure_scenario: A configured setup or test command checks out another commit and passes there. The agent leaves its original tree unchanged, and the gates stage reuses that passing result for the original tree.

verification.evidence: src/pipeline/agent-gate.ts:189–194 stores the comparison when `key && after.setupOk && comparison && completed(result)`, without checking the snapshot checkout's HEAD. `completed` (lines 55–62) checks only result fields. In contrast, src/pipeline/engine.ts:1651–1653 guards normal evidence with `(await headSha(cwd)) === checkedSha`.
verification.trigger: Setup or the test command checks out an older passing commit in the snapshot checkout. Its passing result is recorded under the original snapshot tree and reused when the session commits that tree.

findings.title: Synthetic commit metadata can change the test result
findings.detail: The snapshot checkout uses a synthetic commit with a different SHA and commit message from the round commit, yet the result is reused solely by tree hash. Gate commands can inspect Git metadata, so this execution need not produce the result the normal gate would produce for the final commit.
findings.suggestion: Do not reuse a snapshot result when its execution can observe commit metadata that differs from the final commit; establish equivalent commit provenance or conservatively run the normal gate.
findings.failure_scenario: The test check validates the latest commit message or derives a version from git describe. It passes for the synthetic "Factory gate snapshot" commit but would fail for the actual round commit with the same tree; the gates stage skips it.

verification.evidence: src/git/repos.ts:548-553 creates a synthetic commit using `"commit-tree", tree, "-p", "HEAD"` and `stdin: "Factory gate snapshot\n"`; line 568 installs it as HEAD. Reuse looks up `${sha}^{tree}` (src/pipeline/agent-gate.ts:94-98), then removes the test check: `checks: gates.checks.filter((c) => c.name !== "test")` (src/pipeline/engine.ts:1526-1527).
verification.trigger: A configured test check passes for the synthetic commit's message or derived version but fails for the actual round commit. With identical tree, configuration and environment hashes, the snapshot pass is reused and the failing round test is skipped.

findings.title: Include the first failure in output after a passing retry
findings.detail: When a regression fails and then passes on retry, the comparison retains the first attempt, but the response formats only the final passing result. The session sees a clean pass and receives none of the original failure excerpts, despite the recorded classification being flaky.
findings.suggestion: Include the first attempt's failure excerpts and the retry classification in the response alongside the final result.
findings.failure_scenario: The full suite fails with an assertion, then passes on the factory's retry. The wrapper returns exit status zero and only the passing retry output, hiding the assertion from the implementer.

verification.trigger: A regression qualifies for retry and passes on retry. The wrapper returns status zero and the passing attempt's output, omitting the original assertion and failure excerpts.

findings.title: Reject evidence if the gate changed its checkout's HEAD

A test command can check out another commit and pass there; this result is then recorded under the original snapshot tree and reused as evidence for it.
findings.suggestion: Record the snapshot checkout's initial HEAD and verify it is unchanged before storing or returning reusable evidence.
findings.failure_scenario: The configured test command checks out an older passing commit before running tests. The snapshot contains failing tests, but the passing result is stored and reused for the snapshot tree.

verification.evidence: src/pipeline/agent-gate.ts:134 computes the key before execution; lines 189–194 persist the result under that key without validating HEAD afterward. src/pipeline/agent-gate.ts:95–105 subsequently matches the round tree and accepts the stored completed result.

findings.title: Carry timeout results through the normal gate retry and reuse flow
findings.detail: The session path does not perform the gates stage's timeout rerun, and completed() prevents timed-out results from being recorded. Consequently, an unchanged tree runs the full test check again in the gates stage instead of carrying over its timeout and retry classification, contrary to the request to reuse failures and retries unchanged.
findings.suggestion: Apply the normal bounded timeout handling to the factory session execution and persist its resulting timeout and retry classification for reuse.
findings.failure_scenario: A full-suite request times out on the snapshot and the implementer makes no further changes. The gates stage finds no record and starts the full suite again.

verification.evidence: src/pipeline/agent-gate.ts:61 explicitly requires `!result.timedOut`; line 189 records only `completed(result)`. src/gates/run.ts:469–474 excludes timed-out results from `retryRegressions`. src/pipeline/agent-gate.ts:99 returns null when no record exists, causing normal gate execution.
verification.trigger: The snapshot test times out and the session leaves its tree unchanged. The request neither follows the normal timeout retry path nor records reusable evidence, so the gates stage starts the suite again.

findings.title: Do not substitute a reused test result after gate setup fails
findings.detail: The comparison replacement runs even when the current gates-stage setup failed. It replaces the test's blocking not_run result with a prior passing result, and gate evidence subsequently includes that passing test. Although the setup failure remains blocking, verify can receive a passing test result despite the current stage's failed setup and skipped checks.
findings.suggestion: Only insert the reused comparison when the current gate setup succeeded; retain the blocking not_run result when setup fails.
findings.failure_scenario: An in-session test gate passes, but setup fails when the gates stage runs the remaining checks. The stage records the old test as passing instead of retaining the setup-failure not_run result.

verification.evidence: src/gates/run.ts:370–388 handles failed setup with `if (!after.setupOk)` and produces `verdict: "not_run"`, `output: "not run: setup failed"`. Although src/pipeline/engine.ts:1534 guards initial insertion with `reused && run.setupOk`, lines 1589–1591 subsequently override comparisons unconditionally: `if (reused) { cmp = cmp.map((c) => (c.name === "test" ? reused : c)); if (!cmp.some((c) => c.name === "test")) cmp.push(reused); }`. Lines 1640 and 1665 persist these comparisons as lastGates and the gate artifact.
verification.trigger: A matching passing agent gate execution exists, then setup fails during the gates stage. The unconditional comparison replacement records test as passing instead of not_run. The separate setup failure remains blocking, so this does not make the entire stage pass.

findings.title: Exercise actual configuration and environment changes in cache-miss tests
findings.detail: The config and env scenarios directly replace the stored hash with a different string. They prove that a database lookup misses a changed key, but do not test that changes to the gate configuration or environment produce different keys. A regression that omits either input from the hash would still pass these scenarios.
findings.suggestion: Change a gate configuration input and a gate-relevant environment input between the session execution and reuse lookup, then assert that the test gate runs again.
findings.failure_scenario: The cache-key calculation stops incorporating a gate setup command or a configured environment variable; the existing tests still pass because they overwrite the stored hash directly.

verification.evidence: test/agent-full-suite-gate.test.ts:172–175 handles both scenarios by directly executing `UPDATE agent_gate_executions SET ${scenario === "config" ? "gates_hash" : "env_hash"} = 'different'`; line 197 then checks that the test gate runs. Neither scenario changes actual configuration or environment inputs. The integration being left untested is src/pipeline/agent-gate.ts:78 `gates,` and :84 `envDigest: gateEnvDigest(env, ctx.deps.cfg.baselineEnv)`.
verification.trigger: If agentGateKey stops incorporating setup commands or configured environment variables, these cache-miss scenarios still force a mismatch by changing the stored hash, so they pass despite incorrect reuse for actual input changes.

The integration test selects `suggested_profile: "quick"` (test/agent-full-suite-gate.test.ts:131), which bypasses verify: `profile(ctx) === "quick" ... return true;` (src/pipeline/engine.ts:2079–2083). findings.detail: The snapshot checkout has a synthetic HEAD with a fixed commit message and branch, while the gates stage would run against the actual round commit. findings.failure_scenario: A test passes when `git log -1 --format=%s` is `Factory gate snapshot` but fails for the actual round commit message. The snapshot pass is recorded and reused, so the failing round gate never runs.

Reuse uses the round's tree rather than commit identity: `rev-parse`, `${sha}^{tree}` and `getAgentGate(key)` (src/pipeline/agent-gate.ts:94-98). On reuse, `checks: gates.checks.filter((c) => c.name !== "test")` suppresses execution (src/pipeline/engine.ts:1526-1527).
verification.trigger: A test passes when `git log -1 --format=%s` equals `Factory gate snapshot` and fails for the actual round message. Its snapshot pass is recorded and reused for the identical tree, bypassing the failing test.

findings.title: A failed confinement check can return a successful command status
findings.detail: The returned status uses the process exit code without accounting for `result.ok`. The gate runner marks a result failed when it detects a confinement launch failure even if the process exits zero. In that case the wrapper prints FAIL but exits zero, telling the implement session that its command succeeded.
findings.suggestion: Return a nonzero status whenever the selected gate result is not ok and its exit code is zero.
findings.failure_scenario: A gate command emits the confinement-failure marker and exits 0. The factory classifies the gate as failed, but the agent-test command returns status 0.

verification.evidence: src/gates/run.ts:131–139 sets `ok = !confinementError && res.exitCode === 0 ...` while preserving `exitCode: res.exitCode`. src/pipeline/agent-gate.ts:198 returns `result.exitCode` unless timed out, null, or greater than 128; it does not check `result.ok` or confinement failure.
verification.trigger: A gate prints the confinement-failure marker and exits zero. The factory marks the result failed and prints FAIL, but the agent-test command returns status zero.

findings.title: Timed-out gate executions are never reused
findings.detail: The request says to record the gate result and carry over “its pass or failure, retries and classification” for the same key. The completed predicate rejects every timed-out result, so a full-suite timeout produces no record and the gates stage runs the suite again. The in-session path also does not apply the gates stage’s timeout rerun policy before returning.
findings.suggestion: Apply the normal timeout retry and classification policy to the factory execution, and persist and reuse its completed failure outcome when the key matches.
findings.failure_scenario: The factory test check exceeds its configured timeout during an implement session and the agent makes no subsequent tree changes; the gates stage starts the full test check again instead of reusing the timeout outcome.

verification.evidence: src/pipeline/agent-gate.ts:55–62 defines `completed` with `!result.timedOut`; line 189 records only when `completed(result)`. Lines 98–99 return null without a record. src/pipeline/engine.ts:1526–1531 retains all checks and calls `runGateExecution` when reuse is null.
verification.trigger: An implement-session factory test gate times out and the final tree, configuration and environment remain identical. The timeout is not recorded, so the gates stage executes the full suite again instead of preserving its outcome.

findings.detail: The separate checkout uses a synthetic commit with its own message, timestamp and SHA, but reuse is keyed only by the tree. findings.suggestion: Ensure the execution context matches the round commit for metadata-sensitive checks, or refuse reuse when equivalence cannot be established.
findings.failure_scenario: A test check validates the HEAD commit message or derives a version from `git rev-parse HEAD`; it passes for `Factory gate snapshot` but would fail for the round commit, whose tree is identical. The gates stage accepts the earlier pass without running the check.

Factory construction permits an absent boot SHA.
findings.suggestion: Provide a stable environment identity for this supported initialization path, or make the factory gate unavailable before running it when a reusable key cannot be established.
findings.failure_scenario: A factory is initialized without `bootSha`, and an implementer requests the full suite without changing the tree afterward. Both the in-session factory gate and the gates stage run the test check.
