findings.title: Blocked comments are permanently discarded instead of replaced

findings.title: An in-flight old worker can still push an ungranted workflow
findings.detail: The new publication guard runs in the worker process. Release matching prevents an old worker from leasing a new job, but it does not cancel a job already leased when the coordinator is upgraded. The old worker can finish that job and push its commit using the previous publication code, before the new coordinator can inspect it. Observing a new release schedules a worker update without aborting the active job.
findings.suggestion: Fence or cancel publication-capable jobs from the previous release during upgrade, and ensure the old worker cannot push after the new policy takes effect.
findings.failure_scenario: A worker leases an edit job on the previous release, the daemon is upgraded while the job is running, and the edit adds .github/workflows/ci.yml without an allowance. The old worker pushes the commit before the upgraded coordinator audits it.

verification.evidence: src/workers/publication.ts:102 adds `await assertWorkflowPublication(...)` only to the new worker. At base 804cb6d, src/workers/publication.ts:99–100 proceeds directly from the parent check to `loadPrivateStrings(...)`, then pushes at :136–144. Existing leases survive release changes: src/db/workers.ts:314–320 renews leased jobs without checking releaseSha, and src/workers/client.ts:963–964 waits for `Promise.all(allJobs().map(([, job]) => job.task))` before updating. src/pipeline/lan-agent.ts:43 also preserves edit jobs during daemon shutdown: `if (id && (readonly || !gateShutdown(spec.signal))) workers.cancelAgentJob(id);`.
verification.trigger: An old worker holds an edit lease when the coordinator upgrades. Its edit adds an ungranted workflow; the worker finishes and pushes using the previous publication code before updating or the coordinator auditing the result.

findings.failure_scenario: An allowed workflow edit is delivered without any audit finding because the allowed branch stops emitting `ci-config`; the current test still passes.

verification.trigger: If the granted-workflows branch stops emitting ci-config findings, this test still passes, leaving the loss of the expected warning undetected.

findings.title: Workflow refusal exposes private strings in filenames
findings.detail: The publication guard includes the raw workflow path in its error before the worker checks private strings. That error is sent as the worker failure reason and can also be logged by the pipeline. A filename containing a configured private string therefore leaves the private-string boundary, even though auditDiff separately detects the private filename.
findings.suggestion: Redact private strings from the filename before constructing the error, or use the private-string finding to return a sanitized refusal.
findings.failure_scenario: An agent creates .github/workflows/<private-string>.yml without a workflows allowance. The guard blocks the push but includes the private string in the reported failure reason.

findings.title: Terminal status prevents the scheduler from resuming rollback
findings.detail: The rejection is saved with status needs_human before rollback begins. On daemon restart, Scheduler.start() requeues only running and waiting_input runs, so it never calls executeRun for this checkpoint. A restart after this write can leave the checkout at the rejected merge, or leave the rollback state and draft reporting unfinished. The new tests bypass the scheduler by calling executeRun directly, so they do not exercise the actual restart path.
findings.suggestion: Persist the rejection while the run remains resumable, then mark it needs_human after rollback completes, or explicitly teach scheduler recovery to resume terminal runs with an unfinished rejection checkpoint. Test through a restarted scheduler.
findings.failure_scenario: The daemon exits after the rejection updateRun commits but before reset --hard completes. On startup the run remains needs_human, the scheduler does not requeue it, and the checkout remains at the rejected merged SHA.

verification.evidence: src/pipeline/engine.ts:3503–3508 persists `{ status: "needs_human", ... }` before `return rollbackRejectedMerge(ctx)`. src/scheduler.ts:43 selects interrupted runs only with `status: ["running", "waiting_input"]`; src/scheduler.ts:136 dispatches only `nextQueuedRuns(capacity)`. src/db/store.ts:2099 restricts that query to `runs.status = 'queued'`.
verification.trigger: The daemon exits after the rejection checkpoint commits but before reset finishes. Startup skips the needs_human run, leaving the checkout at the rejected merge instead of completing rollback.

findings.title: Rollback errors are treated as completed terminal runs
findings.detail: Any ordinary error or abort during rollback returns needs_human without arranging another attempt or recording that cleanup failed in the run error. Because the rejection was already marked terminal, the scheduler will not retry it. A transient Git failure therefore leaves the checkout or persisted head inconsistent indefinitely, while the visible error reports only the original gate regression.
findings.suggestion: Keep an incomplete rollback eligible for recovery and record the rollback failure; transition to the terminal state only after cleanup succeeds.
findings.failure_scenario: git reset or git clean fails after the rejection is persisted, or shutdown aborts either command. executeScopedRun returns needs_human and no scheduler retry finishes the rollback.

verification.evidence: src/pipeline/engine.ts:3267–3268 awaits `mergeGit(cwd, ["reset", "--hard", rejected.head])` and `mergeGit(cwd, ["clean", "-fdq"])`. At src/pipeline/engine.ts:341–343, `ctx.state.postMergeRejection && (signal.aborted || !(e instanceof NeedsHumanError))` logs the interruption and returns `"needs_human"`. The checkpoint already saved that terminal status at line 3505; scheduler recovery selects only running/waiting_input runs (src/scheduler.ts:43).
verification.trigger: Reset or clean fails or is aborted after rejection persistence. The engine returns needs_human without completing rollback or making the run eligible for automatic recovery.

findings.title: Terminal status prevents interrupted rollback from resuming
findings.detail: The checkpoint sets the run to needs_human before rollback completes. On daemon startup, the scheduler only requeues running and waiting_input runs, so it never calls the new rollback recovery path for this terminal run. The added tests call executeRun directly and therefore bypass scheduler recovery.
findings.suggestion: Keep the run eligible for scheduler recovery until rollback is complete, or explicitly recover terminal runs with an unfinished rejection checkpoint.
findings.failure_scenario: The daemon restarts immediately after the rejection checkpoint or after reset but before the rollback state save. The run remains needs_human, but its checkout or persisted head and gate state are never fully rolled back.

verification.evidence: src/pipeline/engine.ts:3505 writes `status: "needs_human"` before rollback. Rollback resets and cleans at lines 3267–3268, then clears pending merge state and saves headSha at lines 3269–3274. src/scheduler.ts:43 recovers only `status: ["running", "waiting_input"]`.
verification.trigger: Restart immediately after rejection persistence leaves the rejected checkout; restart after reset but before the rollback save leaves stale persisted head/gate state. Neither needs_human run is automatically resumed.

findings.title: A failed rejection checkpoint is treated as a recorded rejection
findings.detail: postMergeRejection is assigned in memory before updateRun persists it. If that update throws, this catch sees the in-memory field and returns needs_human without recording the status or rejection. The scheduler then leaves the database run running, and a later restart can repeat the merge and gates.
findings.suggestion: Distinguish a successfully persisted rejection from an in-memory attempt, and propagate or handle checkpoint write failures without reporting a terminal outcome.
findings.failure_scenario: The database rejects the rejection checkpoint write, for example because of an I/O error. executeRun returns needs_human while the durable run still has its earlier running state and no rejection checkpoint.

verification.evidence: src/pipeline/engine.ts:3495 assigns `ctx.state.postMergeRejection` before calling `ctx.store.updateRun` at lines 3503–3507. src/db/store.ts:2130 performs the database UPDATE directly. If that throws, src/pipeline/engine.ts:341–343 checks the in-memory rejection and returns `"needs_human"` without another persistence attempt.
verification.trigger: The rejection checkpoint UPDATE fails before committing. The in-memory rejection causes executeRun to return needs_human while the durable run remains running with no rejection checkpoint; rollback has not started.

findings.title: Keep interrupted rejection rollback eligible for scheduler recovery
findings.detail: The checkpoint is saved with status needs_human before rollback starts. Scheduler.start only requeues interrupted running or waiting_input runs, so a daemon restart after this write never invokes rollbackRejectedMerge. The checkout can remain at the rejected merge or retain uncleaned files and stale pending-merge state.
findings.suggestion: Keep the run recoverable until rollback is complete, or teach scheduler startup to enqueue terminal rejections whose rollback is unfinished.
findings.failure_scenario: The daemon stops immediately after saving the rejection, or immediately after resetting HEAD. On restart the run is already needs_human, so the scheduler skips it and does not finish rollback.

verification.evidence: src/pipeline/engine.ts:3503–3508 saves `{ status: "needs_human", ... }` before invoking rollback. src/pipeline/engine.ts:3267 resets HEAD, but the rollback state save occurs only at line 3274. src/scheduler.ts:43 selects only running/waiting_input runs for recovery, and src/db/store.ts:2099 selects only queued runs for dispatch.

findings.title: Terminal status prevents interrupted rollback from resuming
findings.detail: The requirement says: “On resume, a recorded rejection finishes the rollback and ends `needs_human` with the same reason.” This write marks the run `needs_human` before rollback starts. The new restart tests call `executeRun` directly, bypassing the scheduler and therefore missing the production restart behavior. A rollback error or shutdown is also caught and returned as `needs_human` without scheduling another attempt.
findings.suggestion: Persist the rejection while the run remains recoverable, finish rollback on normal execution or scheduler-driven restart, and only then mark it `needs_human`. Exercise the restart through the scheduler.

findings.title: An initially empty repository discards its first commands
findings.detail: A successful poll with no open issues stores no enable boundary. When an issue and command later appear, that later poll establishes the boundary from their timestamps and skips the command as if it existed at enablement. The added test explicitly expects this loss.
findings.suggestion: Establish a durable GitHub-time boundary on the first successful poll even when there are no open issues.
findings.failure_scenario: Enable the queue while the repository has no open issues, then create an issue and post a trusted command before the next poll. No run is ever created for that command.

verification.evidence: src/integrations/issue-queue.ts:272–275 derives `newest` from `issues.nodes` and persists only `if (newest)`. Line 282 processes comments only when `boundary` exists; line 301 skips timestamps `<=` that boundary. test/issue-queue.test.ts:3015–3026 explicitly verifies that an empty first poll leaves no boundary and the subsequent command never runs.
verification.trigger: The first successful poll has no open issues. The next poll establishes its boundary from the newly created issue/comment and skips that command permanently.

findings.title: Identity lookup failure bypasses the factory-author exclusion
findings.detail: An identity lookup error is converted to null, but slash commands continue to be processed. With no bot login, the factory-author comparison cannot exclude the App's own account. If that account is trusted, its command is admitted and permanently recorded even though the invariant forbids factory-authored commands.
findings.suggestion: Fail closed for comment processing when the factory identity needed to identify its author cannot be established, leaving comments retryable.
findings.failure_scenario: The trusted list includes the App bot, identity lookup temporarily fails, and the bot has posted `/limitless do work` after the boundary. The poll creates a run from the factory's own comment.

verification.evidence: src/integrations/issue-queue.ts:278 swallows identity failure with `.catch(() => null)`; line 280 consequently sets `bot` to null. The exclusion at line 298 is only `author.toLowerCase() === bot`, while lines 284–285 still parse slash commands and line 318 calls `factory.createRun`.

findings.title: Preserve timeout rerun history when a durable result is replayed
findings.detail: A replayed observation retains its original stage ID, so completion in the resumed stage treats it as an earlier-stage execution. When that replayed attempt timed out and the stage’s timeout rerun passes, this branch returns `retry_passed` before inspecting `firstAttempt`. The requested history is `rerun_passed`; consumers cannot distinguish a timeout rerun from a regression retry.
findings.suggestion: Derive timeout-rerun history from the comparison before using stage ID to recognize a separate earlier execution.
findings.failure_scenario: An in-place initial execution times out, its observation is checkpointed, and the daemon restarts before clearing the handle. The resumed stage replays that result and its timeout rerun passes; the row is finalized as `load`/`retry_passed` instead of `load`/`rerun_passed`.

verification.evidence: src/db/failure-observations.ts:87 passes `row.stage_id !== completion.stageId` to observationHistory; src/pipeline/context.ts:587 creates a new stage with `this.store.startStage(this.run.id, name, round)`. src/gates/failure-class.ts:30 returns `if (earlierStage && passed) return "retry_passed";` before lines 34–35 inspect timeout firstAttempt and return `rerun_passed`. Lines 42–43 classify either passing history as `load`.
verification.trigger: A checkpointed in-place timeout result replays after restart under a new stage row. Its timeout rerun passes. The original observation retains its earlier stage_id, so finalization records load/retry_passed instead of load/rerun_passed.

findings.title: The change exceeds the requested source-line budget
findings.detail: The diff changes 357 source and migration lines (333 additions and 24 deletions), exceeding the issue’s instruction to stop at 320 and report an overrun.
findings.suggestion: Reduce the change to the stated budget or explicitly report and justify the overrun.
findings.failure_scenario: The factory reviews the delivered diff against the issue’s 320-line limit and finds 357 changed non-test lines.

findings.title: Record a rejected timeout rerun as retry_rejected
findings.detail: A timeout rerun whose passing result fails provenance validation carries the rejected attempt in result.retryAttempt, but has no retryOriginal. The history function therefore falls through to rerun_failed, losing the reason the passing attempt was rejected. A targeted probe returned rerun_failed for this state: `bun -e 'import { observationHistory } from "./src/gates/failure-class.ts"; const first={name:"test",command:"bun test",ok:false,timedOut:true,exitCode:null,durationMs:1,output:"timeout"}; const rejected={...first,firstAttempt:first,retryAttempt:{...first,ok:true,timedOut:false}}; console.log(observationHistory({name:"test",verdict:"regressed",blocking:true,result:rejected,firstAttempt:first}));'`.
findings.suggestion: Detect a rejected passing retryAttempt before deriving the timeout rerun history, including when retryOriginal is absent.
findings.failure_scenario: An initial check times out, then its stage rerun passes after changing tracked files or without valid SHA provenance. The observation is finalized with rerun_failed instead of retry_rejected.

findings.title: Fake in-place executor masks the load-source wiring

findings.failure_scenario: An engine supplies a loadSource returning a fixed value and an in-place gate fails; the real executor records host load instead of the injected value while this test still passes.

verification.evidence: test/pipeline-failure-observations.test.ts:46-47 creates a separate WorkerStore and explicitly sets `workers.loadSource = () => load`. The real executor instead creates `const workers = new WorkerStore(store, releaseSha)` (src/gates/inplace.ts:14), whose default is `loadSource = hostLoadPerCore` (src/db/workers.ts:140). Its completion records `local || j?.in_place ? this.loadSource() : null` (src/db/workers.ts:775). Observations read `job?.load_per_core` for durable jobs (src/pipeline/gate-execution.ts:57-58).

findings.title: Signature assertion derives its expected value from stored evidence
findings.detail: The expected signature is computed from the row's own output_tail. If the implementation stored the passing retry's output as both evidence and signature input, this assertion would still pass. The test does not independently establish that the failed attempt supplied the evidence.
findings.suggestion: Compute the expected signature from a separately specified redacted failed-attempt tail and assert the stored tail contains the failure and excludes the passing result.
findings.failure_scenario: A regression records the passing retry's output and computes its signature from that same output; the current equality assertion succeeds.

verification.evidence: test/pipeline-failure-observations.test.ts:185-188 changes `ok` and `exitCode` by attempt but supplies identical output to failing and passing attempts. Lines 196-197 assert the signature against `ciSignature(row?.name ?? "", row?.output_tail ?? "", row?.command ?? "").signature`, deriving the expectation from stored evidence.
verification.trigger: An implementation mistakenly stores passing-retry evidence and computes its signature consistently from that evidence. The assertion still passes, and identical attempt outputs prevent this fixture from detecting the substitution.

findings.title: A worker named coordinator cannot corroborate a coordinator failure
findings.detail: Coordinator executions and remote executions on a worker named coordinator both store the same location string. The promotion predicate treats them as the same location even though executionSite correctly distinguishes their execution sites.
findings.suggestion: Persist an unambiguous location identity that distinguishes the coordinator from worker names, and use it in the promotion predicate.
findings.failure_scenario: A setup failure occurs locally and on a LAN worker named coordinator within seven days with the same signature; neither observation is promoted to undeclared_requirement.

verification.evidence: src/pipeline/gate-execution.ts:28 assigns local executions `location: "coordinator"`; lines 33-34 assign remote executions `location: job.worker`. src/db/failure-observations.ts:99 requires `b.location<>a.location` for promotion.
verification.trigger: Matching setup failures occur locally and remotely on a worker named coordinator within seven days. Both persist the identical location string, preventing corroboration and leaving both classified setup.

findings.title: Replay completed in-place results even when the executor cannot resume live work
findings.detail: The request requires that “a kept LAN or in-place handle ... is re-attached on resume” and its stored result recorded before re-execution. This condition still requires canResume for every in-place handle. The real LAN executor rejects even a completed job when its recorded release SHA, environment, or daemon port differs from the current daemon, so a deploy or configuration change between completion and restart discards the stored result and starts another execution without recording the first failure.
findings.suggestion: Allow replay of an already completed in-place job independently of the checks needed to resume a live executor, while retaining the safety checks for jobs still running.
findings.failure_scenario: An in-place gate fails and stores its result, then the daemon stops before the evidence checkpoint. The daemon restarts on a new release SHA; canResume returns false, the job is discarded, and a passing fresh execution leaves no observation of the failure.

verification.evidence: src/pipeline/gate-execution.ts:138 requires `executor?.canResume?.(pending.handle, env, ctx.deps.cfg.port)` for an in-place handle; lines 142-151 discard an ineligible handle and clear its checkpoint. src/gates/lan.ts:34 requires `req?.releaseSha === workers.releaseSha` even for `j.state === "done"` (line 37). The stored result would otherwise replay at src/gates/lan.ts:124-130: `if (job.state === "done" && job.result) ... return run;`.
verification.trigger: An in-place failure completes before shutdown but has not reached the evidence insert. Restarting on a different release SHA rejects its completed handle before replay. A passing fresh execution then leaves the original failure without an observation.

findings.title: Exercise the actual durable executor on restart
findings.detail: The request explicitly requires a kept in-place job to be re-attached after a real engine restart, including the shutdown keep path. These tests replace the executor with a fake whose canResume always returns true and whose attach method reads the stored result directly. They therefore do not exercise the real in-place executor's resume eligibility, shutdown handling, or reattachment behavior, and miss the completed-job replay defect.
findings.suggestion: Add an integration test using the real in-place executor and a restarted engine, covering a completed kept job across a changed release identity as well as the shutdown keep path.
findings.failure_scenario: A completed in-place job is retained across a daemon restart but the real executor rejects its handle; the fake executor test still passes because its canResume always returns true.

verification.evidence: The restart fixture replaces real validation with `canResume: () => true` (test/pipeline-failure-observations.test.ts:53) and replays JSON directly from `job?.result` (lines 63-65). Production resume requires `executor?.canResume?.(...)` (src/pipeline/gate-execution.ts:138). output.summary:
Reviewed deploy, installation recovery, executor release following, and their tests. The targeted test command could not run because the checkout has missing or incompatible dependencies: Zod lacks prefault, and the entities package is missing.

Reviewed executor discovery, shutdown, reconciliation, and install recovery. Targeted tests could not start: the checkout's installed dependencies lack `entities` and provide a Zod version without `prefault`.

Reviewed the executor service, deploy recovery, process and restart tests. The targeted test command could not run: installed dependencies lack the entities package and provide a Zod version without prefault.

Reviewed executor discovery, shutdown, installation and deploy recovery paths. Focused tests could not start because the checkout has incomplete or incompatible installed dependencies: Zod lacks `prefault`, and `entities` is missing.

Reviewed the executor service, deployment, recovery, restart and test changes against the request. Targeted tests could not run: the installed dependencies lack Zod's prefault method and the entities package, so all four test files failed during import before their tests ran.

Verifier: 12 candidates, 12 checked, 1 refuted.

findings.title: Inspection failure bypasses executor replacement cleanup
findings.detail: If reconciliation enables the replacement executor and the subsequent launchctl print returns an unknown result, ServiceInspectionError is rethrown before the restoration path runs. The new plist remains installed and enabled, and shutdown is never attempted. The added inspection-reconcile test explicitly expects this state. A failed replacement can therefore leave launchd able to start the replacement on a later login, contrary to the requirement that the restored executor remain unloaded and disabled after a failed install.
findings.suggestion: Attempt the journaled executor shutdown and restoration on this error too. If shutdown cannot be confirmed, retain the journal and report the executor recovery commands without claiming restoration succeeded.
findings.failure_scenario: During service install with an existing executor, launchctl enable succeeds for the replacement, but launchctl print times out. Installation exits with the replacement plist enabled and its journal in phase replacing.

verification.evidence: src/cli/service.ts:375-377 enables the executor before inspecting it: `await ctl(["enable", ...])`, then `await isLoaded(installed)`. At :166 an unknown inspection throws `ServiceInspectionError`; :562 immediately rethrows it before restoration at :565. test/service.test.ts:545-555 explicitly asserts the replacement remains, phase is `replacing`, and no bootout occurs.
verification.trigger: During executor replacement, enable succeeds and the following print times out. Installation fails without restoring the old plist or disabling the replacement.

findings.title: A failed plist inspection is treated as no installed executor
findings.detail: Executor discovery relies on `installedUnits`, which silently skips a plist when `plutil` fails. Deploy then writes no intent and can change the checkout without shutting down the loaded executor. Reconciliation can likewise return successfully without confirming it is off. The existing skip becomes unsafe now that this discovery controls the release boundary.
findings.suggestion: Make executor discovery fail closed when an installed plist cannot be inspected, rather than treating the inspection failure as absence.
findings.failure_scenario: An installed executor's plist cannot be read by `plutil` while its launchd job remains loaded; a deploy skips the intent and proceeds to a different release.

verification.evidence: src/cli/service.ts:208-209 runs plutil with allowFail and does `if (result.exitCode !== 0) continue;`. At :361-362 executor discovery returns undefined when inspection skips that plist. Deploy creates its intent only under `if (unit)` at :873-877, then changes the checkout at :894.
verification.trigger: With an executor loaded and no existing recovery journal or intent, plutil fails for its plist. Deploy treats the executor as absent and changes releases without recording its shutdown obligation.

findings.title: A timed-out disable can be accepted as confirmed
findings.detail: `sh` can return both `timedOut: true` and exit code 0, but shutdown checks only the exit code. In that case it treats disable as confirmed and permits rollback to check out older code, even though the disable operation timed out. The same omission affects enable and bootstrap reconciliation.
findings.suggestion: Treat a timeout as failure for every launchctl control operation, including disable, enable, bootout, and bootstrap.
findings.failure_scenario: `launchctl disable` reaches its timeout but exits with code 0 during termination; rollback proceeds and the still-enabled executor can be loaded again at login.

verification.evidence: src/cli/service.ts:339 uses `allowFail: true`; :350-351 checks disable only with `if (result.exitCode !== 0) throw`, ignoring timedOut. src/util/proc.ts:1205-1220 returns the timeout flag without throwing when allowFail is true. Rollback proceeds to checkout at src/cli/service.ts:948-949 after shutdown returns.
verification.trigger: Disable returns `{ exitCode: 0, timedOut: true }`. Shutdown accepts this inconclusive result and permits rollback without confirming that the executor is disabled.

findings.title: Inspection errors bypass executor replacement restoration
findings.detail: After writing the replacement plist and enabling its label, an unknown `launchctl print` result throws `ServiceInspectionError` and bypasses the restoration block. The failed install leaves the replacement enabled, its old plist unrestored, and the journal in `replacing`. If launchd has the replacement loaded or loads it at login, a failed installation leaves an executor running despite the requested disabled restoration guarantee.
findings.suggestion: On inspection failure, attempt the fail-closed executor shutdown and journal restoration; retain the journal and report recovery instructions if shutdown cannot be confirmed.
findings.failure_scenario: During executor replacement, `launchctl enable` succeeds but the subsequent `print` times out or returns an unexpected error. The install exits with the replacement enabled instead of restoring the old plist disabled.

verification.evidence: src/cli/service.ts:375-377 calls enable before isLoaded. Unknown print results become `ServiceInspectionError` at :166, and the replacement catch at :562 says `if (error instanceof ServiceInspectionError) throw error;`, bypassing `await restore(state)` at :565.
verification.trigger: After replacement enable succeeds, print times out or returns an unexpected error. Installation exits with the replacement enabled and its journal still replacing, instead of restoring the old plist disabled.

findings.title: Source executor arguments are not checked as a complete command
findings.detail: The source-unit test checks only that the plist contains the Bun path and the word executor. It does not check the main.ts path, argument order, or extra arguments, so a source plist that cannot start the executor could pass.

findings.title: Inspection failure can leave a newly installed executor enabled
findings.detail: When the executor plist is newly installed, reconcileExecutor enables its label before inspecting whether it is loaded. If launchctl print then returns an unrecognized error or times out, ServiceInspectionError bypasses the cleanup block. The new plist remains installed and the label remains enabled, with no installation journal because there was no old unit. A later login can load it even though service install failed, and recovery has no executor record to shut down.
findings.suggestion: Record the new executor installation before enabling it, and on inspection failure attempt the same fail-closed shutdown and retain a recovery record until shutdown is confirmed.
findings.failure_scenario: A first service install with executor enabled writes the plist and successfully runs launchctl enable; launchctl print times out. Installation exits with an error, but the enabled plist remains available for launchd to load at the next login.

findings.title: Canonicalized names no longer resolve existing mixed-case repository registrations
findings.detail: The queue passes the lowercased repository name into run creation. Repository resolution uses a case-sensitive getRepoBySlug lookup, so an existing mixed-case registration is missed. Resolution then calls GitHub and creates a second repository record with default settings. This can lose the existing registration's merge policy and default branch, and queue admission can fail when the extra GitHub lookup fails.
findings.suggestion: Use canonical keys for comparisons and snapshots while preserving or resolving the registered repository's spelling for run creation.
findings.failure_scenario: A queue configured for Owner/Repo already has a registered Owner/Repo with a custom merge policy. The queue now requests owner/repo, misses that registration, and creates a separate record using the global default policy.

verification.evidence: src/integrations/issue-queue.ts:261: `const repo = configuredRepo.toLowerCase()`; :436 passes `repo` into the request. src/app.ts:398: `resolveRepo(this.store, req.repo, this.cfg.githubMerge)`. src/db/store.ts:1222: `SELECT * FROM repos WHERE slug = ?`; src/db/migrations.ts:10: `slug TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE` has no case-insensitive collation. src/git/repos.ts:209–215 creates the missing registration with `slug` and `mergePolicy: merge`.
verification.trigger: An existing Owner/Repo registration has a custom merge policy. Queue admission requests owner/repo, creates a separate registration, and uses the global policy instead; a restrictive policy can thereby be bypassed.

findings.title: Lowercasing configured repositories bypasses existing registrations
findings.detail: Queue requests now use the lowercased slug, but repository registration and resolveRepo lookups are case-sensitive. An existing registration such as Owner/Repo is therefore not found when the queue creates a run for owner/repo. resolveRepo instead performs a GitHub lookup and creates a second registration with default settings, losing the existing registration's repository-specific settings. If that lookup fails, queue admission fails altogether.
findings.suggestion: Deduplicate using lowercase comparison keys while preserving a configured spelling for repository resolution, or make repository resolution reuse existing registrations case-insensitively.
findings.failure_scenario: A queue configured for Owner/Repo has an existing Owner/Repo registration with a custom merge policy. After upgrade, an approved issue is admitted as owner/repo and resolves to a newly created registration using the default merge policy.

verification.evidence: src/config.ts:440 lowercases configured slugs: `repos: [...new Set(repos.map((repo) => repo.toLowerCase()))]`. src/integrations/issue-queue.ts:434-445 passes that `repo` into `issueRunRequest` and `factory.createRun`. src/app.ts:398 calls `resolveRepo(this.store, req.repo, this.cfg.githubMerge)`. src/db/store.ts:1222 looks up with `SELECT * FROM repos WHERE slug = ?`; the column is case-sensitive (`slug TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE`, src/db/migrations.ts:10). src/git/repos.ts:199-215 retains the lowercase input slug and registers it with `mergePolicy: merge` after both lookups miss; the parameter defaults to `"auto"` at line 170.
verification.trigger: Existing registration Owner/Repo has merge policy pr or none, queue configuration uses Owner/Repo, and github.merge is unset. An eligible issue now requests owner/repo; successful GitHub resolution creates a separate registration with auto merge policy and attaches the run to it.

findings.title: Changes before the repository snapshot still invalidate it
findings.detail: The listener records changes from the start of the poll, and the snapshot no longer clears invalidations. A change completed before `latestIssueRuns` is read is therefore treated as if it made that fresh snapshot stale. Repeated changes during lifecycle reconciliation or the repository lookup can defer an otherwise eligible issue on every poll.
findings.suggestion: Track whether each issue already has a snapshot when its linked run changes, while preserving invalidations for earlier candidates when a case-variant repository is read.
findings.failure_scenario: A linked run finishes during each poll's GitHub lookup, before the queue reads the latest run snapshot. The snapshot includes the finished state, but admission still refuses the issue indefinitely.

Subscription precedes lifecycle reconciliation at :259 and the GitHub lookup at :280. The later snapshot at :318–322 only calls `snapshots.set(repo, latest)`. At :401–404, `changedDuringPoll(...)` still causes admission to be skipped.
verification.trigger: A linked run changes before its repository snapshot, while remaining compatible with the issue's approval. The fresh snapshot incorporates the change, but the retained invalidation defers admission. Repeating such changes each poll starves the issue.

findings.title: A restart after the primary result can record the same attempt twice
findings.detail: The primary rebase observation is inserted, then the execution handle is cleared and saved before the post-merge comparison is checkpointed. If the daemon stops in that interval, resuming has neither a saved comparison nor the original handle, so it executes the primary gates again under a new handle. Both observations remain and the completion finalizer classifies both from the replacement comparison, inflating failure counts and potentially assigning the first execution the second execution's history.
findings.suggestion: Checkpoint the primary result and its execution identity durably before clearing the handle, and resume the post-merge comparison from that checkpoint.
findings.failure_scenario: A worker fails the primary post-merge gate; the daemon restarts after `gate-result` is saved but before `post-merge-confirmation-pending` is saved. The resumed run executes the gate again and records a second observation for the same post-merge attempt.

verification.evidence: src/pipeline/gate-execution.ts:306-307 clears the handle and persists it: `ctx.state.gateExecution = undefined; await ctx.save("gate-result");`. The consumer result is saved later at src/pipeline/engine.ts:3596-3602: `attempt.result = redactGateData({...}); ... await ctx.save("post-merge-confirmation-pending");`. On resume, engine.ts:3485-3487 uses `attempt.result ?? (await ...)`, rerunning the primary execution when that result is absent. src/gates/executor.ts:271 starts a fresh handle when none is stored: `const handle = stored ?? (await executor.start(req, signal));`. The uniqueness constraint only deduplicates the same handle (src/db/migrations/20261027T134454-failure-observations.sql:9): `UNIQUE (run_id, handle_kind, handle_id, phase, name)`.
verification.trigger: A failed LAN primary post-merge execution records its observation and saves gate-result. Restart before post-merge-confirmation-pending leaves neither a saved handle nor attempt.result. Resume executes the primary gate with a new handle; if it fails again, another observation is inserted for the same post-merge attempt.

findings.title: Confirmation is saved before observation finalization
findings.detail: `confirmPostMerge` saves each confirmation through the callback before the later transaction finalizes observations. This leaves a durable state in which confirmation has completed but its observation is unfinalized. A terminal run update in that interval invokes the generic finalizer and records `interrupted`, losing the confirmation classification and reason. It also violates the requested atomic confirmation-and-finalization boundary.
findings.suggestion: Ensure the save that durably records the completed confirmation also finalizes the corresponding observations in the same transaction.
findings.failure_scenario: A coordinator passes confirmation and its callback saves `post-merge-confirmed`; the process stops before the subsequent save, and the run is cancelled before it resumes. The terminal-state finalizer records the observation as interrupted instead of platform, flaky, or unclassified based on OS.

verification.evidence: src/pipeline/engine.ts:3607-3611 calls confirmPostMerge with `() => ctx.save("post-merge-confirmed")`, then separately calls `ctx.save("post-merge-confirmed", () => ctx.store.observations.finalize(...))`. src/pipeline/post-merge-confirmation.ts:149 executes `await save()` after updating confirmation. src/db/store.ts:2279 terminal cleanup calls `this.observations.finalize(id)` without comparisons; src/db/failure-observations.ts:103-105 consequently selects `"interrupted"`.
verification.trigger: Confirmation passes and its callback persists state; the process stops before the separate finalization save. Cancellation before resume finalizes the observation as interrupted despite the persisted passing confirmation.

findings.title: Source changes exceed the requested stop limit
findings.detail: The issue says to stop at 155 changed source lines. The diff contains 224 added and 36 removed source lines, exceeding that limit; no overrun report was supplied.
findings.suggestion: Reduce the source change to the agreed limit or explicitly report and justify the overrun for review.
findings.failure_scenario: The change reaches review with 260 changed source lines against the requested 155-line stop limit.

findings.title: Resumed post-merge execution can lose the slow-regression flag
findings.detail: Each resumed gates stage receives a new stage ID, but an observation inserted before interruption keeps its original stage ID. If the durable gate execution is resumed, its duplicate insert is ignored and this filter excludes the existing observation. The selector then cannot mark that observation as a slow regression, so a passing re-check is classified as flaky instead of load and the slow-regression evidence is lost.
findings.suggestion: Identify observations by the durable post-merge execution identity rather than the current stage ID, and add a restart test that interrupts after observation insertion but before the re-check selector runs.
findings.failure_scenario: A durable post-merge gate records a slow failure, the process restarts before retryRegressions selects it, and the same execution resumes under a new gates stage; its re-check passes.

verification.evidence: src/pipeline/context.ts:625 creates a stage with `this.store.startStage(this.run.id, name, round)`; src/db/store.ts:2516 inserts a new stage row. src/db/failure-observations.ts:73 uses `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`, retaining the original observation on execution replay. src/pipeline/engine.ts:3514 restricts observed handles to `r.stage_id === ctx.stageId`, so the original observation is excluded. The slow flag update at engine.ts:3572-3578 runs only for those handles. src/gates/failure-class.ts:70 requires `o.slow_regression && o.history === "retry_passed"` for load; line 81 otherwise returns flaky.
verification.trigger: Restart after recording a durable primary slow failure but before selecting its retry. Resume the same execution under a new gates stage, then pass the re-check: the original observation retains slow_regression=0 and is classified flaky instead of load.

findings.title: Confirmation can be saved before its observation is finalized
findings.detail: confirmPostMerge saves each completed confirmation through this callback without finalizing observations. The later save performs finalization in a separate transaction, leaving a window where the confirmed result is durable but its observation is still open. The restart test injects a fault on the first post-merge-confirmed save, so it does not exercise a stop after that save succeeds and before finalization.

If the durable gate execution is resumed, its duplicate insert is ignored and this filter excludes the existing observation. The selector then cannot mark that observation as a slow regression, so a passing re-check is classified as flaky instead of load and the slow-regression evidence is lost.
candidates.suggestion: Identify observations by the durable post-merge execution identity rather than the current stage ID, and add a restart test that interrupts after observation insertion but before the re-check selector runs.
candidates.failure_scenario: A durable post-merge gate records a slow failure, the process restarts before retryRegressions selects it, and the same execution resumes under a new gates stage; its re-check passes.

candidates.title: Confirmation can be saved before its observation is finalized
candidates.detail: confirmPostMerge saves each completed confirmation through this callback without finalizing observations. The later save performs finalization in a separate transaction, leaving a window where the confirmed result is durable but its observation is still open. The restart test injects a fault on the first post-merge-confirmed save, so it does not exercise a stop after that save succeeds and before finalization.
candidates.suggestion: Arrange for the completed confirmation and its observation finalization to be committed together, and add a test that interrupts after the confirmation has been persisted but before the current later save.
candidates.failure_scenario: A coordinator confirmation passes, its callback save succeeds, and the run is cancelled or terminated before the following save; terminal cleanup can finalize the observation as interrupted despite the persisted confirmation.

candidates.title: Land observation tests do not verify executor location or worker OS
candidates.detail: The added land tests assert classification and attempt identity, but none asserts the recorded location and OS for a LAN worker or for a coordinator execution. A regression that records every land execution as local or drops worker_os would pass these tests.
candidates.suggestion: Add land-check cases that inspect location and OS for a completed remote job and a coordinator or local-fallback execution.
candidates.failure_scenario: A LAN land check fails on a Linux worker, but its observation records the coordinator OS or an unknown location; the existing land observation assertions still pass.

candidates.title: Coordinator confirmation discards the preceding retry failure
candidates.detail: The request requires the combined history of a slow regression whose re-check failed and whose coordinator confirmation passed to retain `retry_failed` alongside the confirmation outcome. `observationHistory` returns a single `confirmed_passed` value whenever confirmation exists, so the persisted observation cannot show that the re-check failed. The slow-regression flag remains, but it does not establish the re-check outcome.
candidates.suggestion: Persist both the retry outcome and confirmation outcome, and test the combined history after finalization and restart.
candidates.failure_scenario: A slow worker regression fails its re-check and then passes coordinator confirmation. Its observation records `confirmed_passed` and `slow_regression=1`, but no evidence that the re-check failed.

candidates.title: Source changes exceed the requested stopping budget
candidates.detail: The request says to stop at 155 changed source lines and report the overrun. The diff changes 224 source lines by addition and 36 by deletion, and the implementer supplied no report explaining the overrun.
candidates.suggestion: Reduce the change to the stated budget or explicitly report and justify the overrun.
candidates.failure_scenario: The factory receives a change substantially beyond the issue's stated source-line limit without the requested explanation.

findings.title: A resumed local post-merge gate finalizes an interrupted execution with the new execution's outcome
findings.detail: The completion finalizer matches rebase observations by purpose, round and SHA, but not by execution handle. Local gate executions cannot be resumed: if the process stops after recording a failure and before saving the post-merge comparison, restart runs the primary gate again with a new handle. Verifier: 19 candidates, 19 checked, 1 refuted.

findings.title: Release-intent replay bypasses lease-time validation
findings.detail: Reconciliation delegates a pending release to `reconcileLeaseIntent`, which can replay the release with `client.write` without a GitHub-time sample or `beforeSend` predicate. Both startup recovery and ordinary operations use that path, so an expired generation can mutate the claim after its lease window has closed.
findings.suggestion: Ensure release replay uses the same fresh time decision and send-time revalidation as other same-generation writes.
findings.failure_scenario: A release intent is journaled, the process stops before sending it, and recovery runs more than ten minutes later while the old tip remains current. Recovery writes the expired generation's release without checking whether it is renewable.

verification.evidence: src/integrations/leases.ts:65 calls `recoverLeases({ client, store })`; :89 calls `reconcileLeaseIntent({ client, store, signal }, repo, ref)`. src/integrations/lease-store.ts:118-121 replays releases using `client.write(..., { signal, onCommit: ... })` without `beforeSend`. src/integrations/claim-ref.ts:206-208 aborts only when `opts.beforeSend?.()` returns false.
verification.trigger: A pending release references the still-current confirmed tip. Recovery after lease expiry replays the same-generation release without sampling GitHub time or checking renewability.

findings.title: Renewal loop omits recovered confirmed leases
findings.detail: The loop iterates only the in-memory `handles` map, which is populated by writes applied in this manager instance. Confirmed held rows loaded at startup, and acquisitions confirmed by intent reconciliation, never enter that map. Even if `active` would accept their handles, the loop never renews them.
findings.suggestion: Enumerate confirmed held rows when starting or reconciling and make their handles available to the renewal loop.
findings.failure_scenario: A manager restarts with a confirmed held lease and starts the loop. Every tick skips that lease; it expires even though the associated run is active.

findings.failure_scenario: A confirmed generation 2 write encounters two moved responses whose tips are malformed or generation 1. The manager marks generation 2 lost and calls `onLost` despite having no superseding record.

findings.title: An exception in one renewal tick rejects the timer callback

verification.evidence: src/integrations/leases.ts:239–243 installs an async interval callback containing `for (const h of handles.values()) if (current(h) && next.active(h)) await manager.update(h, {});` with no exception handling. findings.title: Release intent replay bypasses send-time lease validation

findings.title: Cross-run requests bypass pending-intent reconciliation

An unresolved intent must instead be reconciled first and return wait while pending; if it resolves as a dropped, never-confirmed acquisition, the next run must be able to acquire. findings.title: Replayed releases bypass lease-time revalidation
findings.detail: Reconciliation can replay a pending release through `reconcileLeaseIntent`, whose replay write has no time sample or before-send predicate. A release interrupted before its ref update can therefore be sent after its generation has expired, violating the requirement that every same-generation mutation be revalidated immediately before the ref update. Startup recovery uses the same replay path.
candidates.suggestion: Make release reconciliation perform the same fresh time decision and send-time validation as an ordinary release, including during startup recovery.
candidates.failure_scenario: A release creates its commit but stops before updating the ref; the manager restarts after the lease has expired while the old tip is still present. Recovery writes the released record for the expired generation without checking GitHub time.

candidates.title: A different run cannot reconcile a pending acquisition
candidates.detail: The different-run check returns `refused` before reconciling an existing intent. If the prior run's first acquisition was unconfirmed and is later known to have left the ref unchanged, subsequent acquisitions by another run cannot drop and forget that row through this operation. Until a running renewal loop happens to reconcile it, the next run is incorrectly blocked; while the intent remains unresolved, the required result is `wait`, not `refused`.
candidates.suggestion: Reconcile pending intents before applying the different-run ownership check, then inspect the resulting row.
candidates.failure_scenario: Run A leaves an unconfirmed acquisition intent on an absent ref and ends. Run B calls `acquire` before the loop runs, after GitHub is readable and confirms the ref is still absent; it receives `refused` instead of resolving A's intent and acquiring.

candidates.title: Recovered held leases are absent from the renewal loop
candidates.detail: The loop iterates only the in-memory `handles` map, which is populated after a write returns `applied` in this manager instance. Recovery and later intent reconciliation can confirm a held lease without adding its handle to that map. Such a lease is never presented to `active` or renewed by the loop, even though it is confirmed in the store.
candidates.suggestion: Populate or derive renewal handles from confirmed held rows after recovery and reconciliation, while preserving generation checks.
candidates.failure_scenario: An acquisition's ref update succeeds but returns `unconfirmed`; a later loop tick reconciles it as applied. No handle is added to `handles`, so subsequent ticks never renew the confirmed lease and it expires.

duplicates.title: Recovered confirmed leases are absent from the renewal loop
duplicates.detail: The request requires the loop to update each confirmed held handle. The loop visits only the in-memory `handles` map, which is populated by an immediately applied write. Recovery and tick-time reconciliation can confirm a held acquisition without adding its handle, and existing confirmed rows are not loaded on manager creation. Those leases therefore receive no periodic renewal.
duplicates.suggestion: Populate or derive the loop's handles from confirmed held rows after recovery and reconciliation, as well as after writes.
duplicates.failure_scenario: An acquisition's write is unconfirmed, then a later tick reconciles it as applied. The row is held, but no handle is registered, so subsequent ticks never renew it and the lease expires.

candidates.title: A different run bypasses pending-intent reconciliation
candidates.detail: The request says “Before every operation” a pending intent is reconciled and, while unresolved, the operation returns `wait`. This early return instead reports `refused: live` whenever a different run encounters an intent, even if reconciliation would drop an unsuccessful first acquisition and permit the new run.
candidates.suggestion: Reconcile the row before deciding whether its existing run prevents the requested acquisition.
candidates.failure_scenario: Run A's first acquisition remains unconfirmed with a pending intent. Run B acquires the same ref after the write becomes readable and is known not to have applied; B is refused instead of reconciling and acquiring.

candidates.title: Replayed releases bypass send-time lease validation
candidates.detail: The request requires “Immediately before the `updateRefs` send” revalidation for same-generation writes. `reconcileLeaseIntent` can replay a pending release through `client.write` without a `beforeSend` hook, and this manager invokes it both during recovery and before operations. A release replay can consequently write after the lease window has expired or after a suspend without a fresh GitHub-time decision.
candidates.suggestion: Ensure replayed release writes receive the same fresh time decision and send-time revalidation as ordinary releases.
candidates.failure_scenario: A release intent is persisted before its ref update, the process restarts after the lease expires, and recovery replays the release against the unchanged tip without checking whether the generation is still renewable.

candidates.title: Mutation tests explicitly accept two winners
candidates.detail: The request says tests 1 and 3 must fail with the unconditional-ref-write mutant. Instead, the shared race helper expects two winners when that mutant is enabled, so both mutant cases pass precisely when the one-holder invariant is violated. These tests do not provide the requested mutation check.
candidates.suggestion: Assert exactly one winner in the invariant tests regardless of the fake's write mode, and run the mutant separately to verify those assertions fail.
candidates.failure_scenario: The fake unconditionally overwrites the ref during concurrent create or takeover; both managers report `held`, and the test accepts that outcome.

findings.title: A superseded unsent question set can never be published later
findings.detail: An unsent question effect is permanently marked done when its run temporarily stops waiting. If the run later returns to waiting with the same unanswered question IDs, observe() sees the existing effect and never creates another publication. The same problem occurs after recovery establishes that a stale POST was not accepted. The run can therefore remain waiting indefinitely without its questions appearing on the issue.
findings.suggestion: Distinguish a superseded effect with no confirmed publication from a completed publication, and allow a fresh eligible waiting episode to publish the set after any uncertain prior POST has been recovered.
findings.failure_scenario: A run enters waiting_input with question 42, but its pending comment has not been posted. The run temporarily changes to running, so reconciliation marks the effect done. It returns to waiting_input with question 42 still unanswered; subsequent polls and restarts never post the question.

verification.evidence: src/integrations/issue-lifecycle.ts:356–358: `if (stale && !pending.page) { save(effect, "done"); continue; }`. At :129, publication requires `!effects.has(`comment:questions:${ids}`)`, so a done checkpoint prevents recreation.
verification.trigger: An unposted question set becomes ineligible while the run is running. Reconciliation marks it done; returning to waiting_input with the same unanswered questions never publishes it, including after restart.

findings.title: Retired unsent question sets cannot be published if they become eligible again
findings.detail: Superseding an unsent question effect marks it done, and observe() will never create that effect again because it already exists. A temporary linkage or status change can therefore permanently suppress a question set that was never posted.
findings.suggestion: Distinguish superseded unsent effects from completed publications and allow the same set to be scheduled again when it becomes eligible.
findings.failure_scenario: A waiting run has a pending question publication, loses its issue link before the POST, and later regains the same link while the question remains open. The effect is done without a comment, so subsequent polls never publish that question set.

verification.evidence: src/integrations/issue-lifecycle.ts:206–208 requires the current linked repository/issue in `eligible()`. At :355–358, ineligibility with no recovery page calls `save(effect, "done")`. At :129, `!effects.has(`comment:questions:${ids}`)` prevents recreating that effect.
verification.trigger: The issue link disappears before POST and reconciliation retires the unsent checkpoint. Restoring the same link and question set leaves the done checkpoint blocking publication.

findings.title: Privacy reinspection can close an uncertain POST without recovery
findings.detail: The pending body is reinspected before marker recovery, and any inspection failure immediately marks the effect done. For a checkpoint with page set, GitHub may already have accepted the POST; closing it without checking the marker violates the required recovery behavior and loses the recorded outcome.
findings.suggestion: Recover an uncertain POST using its independently generated marker and checkpointed identity before closing the effect, even when the stored body can no longer pass publication inspection. Keep any new POST suppressed if inspection fails.
findings.failure_scenario: GitHub accepts a question comment but the response is lost. Before the next poll, private-string configuration becomes unreadable or changes to match the stored body. Reinspection fails, the checkpoint is marked done, and the accepted comment is never recovered.

verification.evidence: src/integrations/issue-lifecycle.ts:426–427 records `page: 1` before POST. At :365–369, `checkBody(run, pending.body, ...)` failure calls `save(effect, "done")` and continues. Recovery starts only afterward at :371: `if (pending.page)`.
verification.trigger: GitHub accepts a POST but its response is lost. Before retry, privacy configuration becomes unreadable or matches the body. Reinspection closes the uncertain checkpoint without looking up the accepted comment.

findings.title: Publication failures log exception output instead of a fixed code
findings.detail: The delivery catch passes the exception to logFailure, which logs its text. The subprocess error can include the full command and stderr, and credential redaction does not remove configured private strings. This violates the requirement that publication diagnostics contain fixed codes and never exception output. The new privacy tests inject fixed errors and do not exercise an exception containing withheld content.

candidates.title: Retired unsent sets cannot publish when they become eligible again

candidates.title: Publication failures log arbitrary exception output

The request requires fixed diagnostic codes and no exception output.
candidates.suggestion: Log a fixed delivery or recovery failure code without interpolating the exception, including for GitHub and parsing failures.
